547:         opts: RequestOptions::default(),
548:         subagent_cancels: Arc::new(CancelMap::new()),

802:     /// path, the schema no longer matches the Rust type and serde exploded
803:     /// after validation said it was fine.

805:     fn every_tool_rejects_bogus_input_without_internal_bug() {

824:                         );

826:                 }
827:             }
828:         }
829:     }

251: /// Lock-free reads via `ArcSwap`, writes swap in a new snapshot atomically.
252: ///
253: /// Bundled Lua plugins can replace a native tool with their own version.
254: /// The original native tool is kept in `native_fallbacks` so we can still
255: /// look up its header info. User plugins are not allowed to replace tools
256: /// that aren't native (that gives a `NameConflict` error).
257: pub struct ToolRegistry {
258:     tools: ArcSwap<Vec<RegisteredTool>>,
259:     native_fallbacks: ArcSwap<Vec<RegisteredTool>>,
260: }
261: 
262: impl Default for ToolRegistry {
263:     fn default() -> Self {
264:         Self::new()
265:     }
266: }
267: 
268: #[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
269: pub enum RegistryError {
270:     #[error("tool '{name}' is already registered (existing source: {existing})")]
271:     NameConflict { name: String, existing: String },
272: }
273: 
274: impl ToolRegistry {
275:     pub fn new() -> Self {
276:         Self {
277:             tools: ArcSwap::from_pointee(Vec::new()),
278:             native_fallbacks: ArcSwap::from_pointee(Vec::new()),
279:         }
280:     }
281: 
282:     pub fn native() -> &'static Self {
283:         Self::native_arc()
284:     }
285: 
286:     pub fn native_arc() -> &'static Arc<Self> {
287:         static NATIVE: LazyLock<Arc<ToolRegistry>> =
288:             LazyLock::new(|| Arc::new(ToolRegistry::build_native()));
289:         &NATIVE
290:     }
291: 
292:     pub fn with_natives() -> Self {
293:         Self::build_native()
294:     }
295: 
296:     /// `register_tools!` catches dupes at compile time. Plugins and MCP skip
297:     /// that macro, so this runtime check is the safety net.
298:     fn build_native() -> Self {
299:         let registry = Self::new();
300:         let natives = super::native_tools();
301:         let mut vec: Vec<RegisteredTool> = Vec::with_capacity(natives.len());
302:         for tool in natives {
303:             let name = tool.name().to_owned();
304:             assert!(
305:                 !vec.iter().any(|t| t.name() == name),
306:                 "duplicate native tool name: {name}"
307:             );
308:             vec.push(RegisteredTool {
309:                 tool,
310:                 source: ToolSource::Native,
311:             });
312:         }
313:         registry.tools.store(Arc::new(vec));
314:         registry
315:     }
316: 
317:     pub fn get(&self, name: &str) -> Option<RegisteredTool> {
318:         self.tools.load().iter().find(|t| t.name() == name).cloned()
319:     }
320: 
321:     pub fn has(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
322:         self.tools.load().iter().any(|t| t.name() == name)
323:     }
324: 
325:     pub fn register(&self, tool: Arc<dyn Tool>, source: ToolSource) -> Result<(), RegistryError> {
326:         let name = tool.name().to_owned();
327:         let mut conflict = None;
328:         self.tools.rcu(|current| {
329:             conflict = None;
330:             if let Some(existing) = current.iter().find(|t| t.name() == name) {
331:                 conflict = Some(existing.source.as_log_field().into_owned());
332:                 return Vec::clone(current);
333:             }
334:             let mut next = Vec::with_capacity(current.len() + 1);
335:             next.extend(current.iter().cloned());
336:             next.push(RegisteredTool {
337:                 tool: Arc::clone(&tool),
338:                 source: source.clone(),
339:             });
340:             next
341:         });
342:         if let Some(existing) = conflict {
343:             return Err(RegistryError::NameConflict { name, existing });
344:         }
345:         Ok(())
346:     }
347: 
348:     /// All-or-nothing: a name clash rolls back the whole batch so an MCP server
349:     /// never ends up half-registered.
350:     pub fn register_many(
351:         &self,
352:         entries: impl IntoIterator<Item = (Arc<dyn Tool>, ToolSource)>,
353:     ) -> Result<(), RegistryError> {
354:         let entries: Vec<_> = entries.into_iter().collect();
355:         let mut conflict = None;
356:         self.tools.rcu(|current| {
357:             conflict = None;
358:             let mut next = Vec::clone(current);
359:             for (tool, source) in &entries {
360:                 let name = tool.name();
361:                 if let Some(existing) = next.iter().find(|t| t.name() == name) {
362:                     conflict = Some(RegistryError::NameConflict {
363:                         name: name.to_owned(),
364:                         existing: existing.source.as_log_field().into_owned(),
365:                     });
366:                     return Vec::clone(current);
367:                 }
368:                 next.push(RegisteredTool {
369:                     tool: Arc::clone(tool),
370:                     source: source.clone(),
371:                 });
372:             }
373:             next
374:         });
375:         if let Some(e) = conflict {
376:             return Err(e);
377:         }
378:         Ok(())
379:     }
380: 
381:     pub fn clear_mcp_server(&self, server: &str) {
382:         self.tools.rcu(|current| {
383:             current
384:                 .iter()
385:                 .filter(
386:                     |t| !matches!(&t.source, ToolSource::Mcp { server: s } if s.as_ref() == server),
387:                 )
388:                 .cloned()
389:                 .collect::<Vec<_>>()
390:         });
391:     }
392: 
393:     pub fn replace_plugin(
394:         &self,
395:         plugin: &str,
396:         new_entries: Vec<(Arc<dyn Tool>, ToolSource)>,
397:     ) -> Result<(), RegistryError> {
398:         let mut conflict = None;
399:         let mut displaced: Vec<RegisteredTool> = Vec::new();
400:         self.tools.rcu(|current| {
401:             conflict = None;
402:             displaced = Vec::new();
403:             let mut next: Vec<RegisteredTool> = current
404:                 .iter()
405:                 .filter(
406:                     |t| !matches!(&t.source, ToolSource::Lua { plugin: p } if p.as_ref() == plugin),
407:                 )
408:                 .cloned()
409:                 .collect();
410:             for (tool, source) in &new_entries {
411:                 let name = tool.name();
412:                 if let Some(idx) = next.iter().position(|t| t.name() == name) {
413:                     if matches!(next[idx].source, ToolSource::Native) {
414:                         displaced.push(next.remove(idx));
415:                     } else {
416:                         conflict = Some(RegistryError::NameConflict {
417:                             name: name.to_owned(),
418:                             existing: next[idx].source.as_log_field().into_owned(),
419:                         });
420:                         displaced = Vec::new();
421:                         return Vec::clone(current);
422:                     }
423:                 }
424:                 next.push(RegisteredTool {
425:                     tool: Arc::clone(tool),
426:                     source: source.clone(),
427:                 });
428:             }
429:             next
430:         });
431:         if let Some(e) = conflict {
432:             return Err(e);
433:         }
434:         if !displaced.is_empty() {
435:             self.native_fallbacks.rcu(|current| {
436:                 let mut next = Vec::clone(current);
437:                 next.extend(displaced.iter().cloned());
438:                 next
439:             });
440:         }
441:         Ok(())
442:     }
443: 
444:     pub fn clear_plugin(&self, plugin: &str) {
445:         let fallbacks = self.native_fallbacks.load();
446:         let tools_guard = self.tools.load();
447:         let plugin_names: Vec<&str> = tools_guard
448:             .iter()
449:             .filter(|t| matches!(&t.source, ToolSource::Lua { plugin: p } if p.as_ref() == plugin))
450:             .map(|t| t.name())
451:             .collect();
452:         let restore: Vec<RegisteredTool> = fallbacks
453:             .iter()
454:             .filter(|t| plugin_names.contains(&t.name()))
455:             .cloned()
456:             .collect();
457:         self.tools.rcu(|current| {
458:             let mut next: Vec<RegisteredTool> = current
459:                 .iter()
460:                 .filter(
461:                     |t| !matches!(&t.source, ToolSource::Lua { plugin: p } if p.as_ref() == plugin),
462:                 )
463:                 .cloned()
464:                 .collect();
465:             next.extend(restore.iter().cloned());
466:             next
467:         });
468:         if !restore.is_empty() {
469:             self.native_fallbacks.rcu(|current| {
470:                 current
471:                     .iter()
472:                     .filter(|t| !plugin_names.contains(&t.name()))
473:                     .cloned()
474:                     .collect::<Vec<_>>()
475:             });
476:         }
477:     }
478: 
479:     fn native_fallback(&self, name: &str) -> Option<RegisteredTool> {
480:         self.native_fallbacks
481:             .load()
482:             .iter()
483:             .find(|t| t.name() == name)
484:             .cloned()
485:     }
486: 
487:     /// Resolve a human-friendly summary for a tool invocation.
488:     /// Prefers the native tool's summary (which parses args into a readable
489:     /// string like a file path), falling back to the current registered tool,
490:     /// then to the raw tool name.
491:     pub fn resolve_header(&self, name: &str, input: &Value) -> String {
492:         self.resolve_invocation(name, input)
493:             .map(|inv| inv.start_header().into_ready().text())
494:             .unwrap_or_else(|| name.to_owned())
495:     }
496: 
497:     /// Like [`resolve_header`] but awaits async headers (e.g. Lua plugins).
498:     pub async fn resolve_header_async(&self, name: &str, input: &Value) -> String {
499:         match self.resolve_invocation(name, input) {
500:             Some(inv) => inv.start_header().await.text(),
501:             None => name.to_owned(),
502:         }
503:     }
504: 
505:     fn resolve_invocation(&self, name: &str, input: &Value) -> Option<Box<dyn ToolInvocation>> {
506:         self.native_fallback(name)
507:             .and_then(|e| e.try_parse(input))
508:             .or_else(|| self.get(name).and_then(|e| e.try_parse(input)))
509:     }
510: 
511:     pub fn names(&self) -> Vec<Arc<str>> {
512:         self.tools
513:             .load()
514:             .iter()
515:             .map(|t| Arc::from(t.name()))
516:             .collect()
517:     }
518: 
519:     /// Rebuilt each request so tools registered mid-session (MCP handshake) show
520:     /// up on the very next turn.
521:     pub fn definitions(
522:         &self,
523:         vars: &Vars,
524:         ctx: &DescriptionContext,
525:         supports_examples: bool,
526:     ) -> Value {
527:         let snapshot = self.tools.load();
528:         let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(snapshot.len());
529:         for entry in snapshot.iter() {
530:             if !entry.tool.audience().contains(ctx.audience) {
531:                 continue;
532:             }
533:             if !ctx.filter.matches(entry.name()) {
534:                 continue;
535:             }
536:             let description = vars.apply(&entry.tool.description(ctx)).into_owned();
537:             let mut def = json!({
538:                 "name": entry.name(),
539:                 "description": description,
540:                 "input_schema": entry.tool.schema(),
541:             });
542:             if let Some(examples) = entry.tool.examples() {
543:                 if supports_examples {
544:                     def["input_examples"] = examples;
545:                 } else if let Some(text) = format_examples_as_text(&examples) {
546:                     let merged =
547:                         format!("{}\n\n{}", def["description"].as_str().unwrap_or(""), text);
548:                     def["description"] = Value::String(merged);
549:                 }
550:             }
551:             out.push(def);
552:         }
553:         Value::Array(out)
554:     }
555: 
556:     pub fn iter(&self) -> RegistrySnapshot {
557:         RegistrySnapshot(self.tools.load_full())
558:     }
559: }
560: 
561: pub struct RegistrySnapshot(Arc<Vec<RegisteredTool>>);
562: 
563: impl RegistrySnapshot {
564:     pub fn iter(&self) -> std::slice::Iter<'_, RegisteredTool> {
565:         self.0.iter()
566:     }
567: 
568:     pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
569:         self.0.len()
570:     }
571: 
572:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
573:         self.0.is_empty()
574:     }
575: }
576: 
577: fn format_examples_as_text(examples: &Value) -> Option<String> {
578:     let arr = examples.as_array()?;
579:     if arr.is_empty() {
580:         return None;
581:     }
582:     let mut text = String::from("Examples:");
583:     for ex in arr {
584:         if let Some(code) = ex.get("code").and_then(|c| c.as_str()) {
585:             text.push_str("\n```\n");
586:             text.push_str(code);
587:             text.push_str("\n```");
588:         }
589:     }
590:     Some(text)
591: }

593: /// `impl_tool!` wires up the `Tool` trait on this wrapper using consts from
594: /// `#[derive(Tool)]`. Tool files only need to write their actual logic.
595: pub struct Native<T: 'static>(std::marker::PhantomData<T>);
596: 
597: impl<T: 'static> Native<T> {
598:     pub const fn new() -> Self {
599:         Self(std::marker::PhantomData)
600:     }
601: }
602: 
603: impl<T: 'static> Default for Native<T> {
604:     fn default() -> Self {
605:         Self::new()
606:     }
607: }

55: #[derive(Debug, Default)]
56: pub struct ModelRegistry {
57:     /// Keyed by tier (not spec) so inserting a model automatically evicts the
58:     /// previous holder. Persisted to disk.
59:     overrides: BTreeMap<ModelTier, String>,
60:     /// Ordered model info per provider, populated from `list_models()`.
61:     /// Not persisted - rebuilt every session. Used for auto-tier assignment
62:     /// and discovered metadata lookup.
63:     known_models: HashMap<ProviderKind, Vec<ModelInfo>>,
64: }
65: 
66: impl ModelRegistry {
67:     pub fn set_overrides(&mut self, overrides: BTreeMap<ModelTier, String>) {
68:         self.overrides = overrides;
69:     }
70: 
71:     pub fn set_known_models(&mut self, provider: ProviderKind, models: Vec<ModelInfo>) {
72:         self.known_models.insert(provider, models);
73:     }
74: 
75:     pub fn set(&mut self, spec: String, tier: ModelTier) {
76:         self.overrides.insert(tier, spec);
77:     }
78: 
79:     pub fn unset(&mut self, spec: &str, tier: ModelTier) {
80:         if self.overrides.get(&tier).map(String::as_str) == Some(spec) {
81:             self.overrides.remove(&tier);
82:         }
83:     }
84: 
85:     pub fn has_override(&self, spec: &str, tier: ModelTier) -> bool {
86:         self.overrides.get(&tier).map(String::as_str) == Some(spec)
87:     }
88: 
89:     /// Lookup discovered metadata for a model by ID.
90:     pub fn discovered(&self, provider: ProviderKind, model_id: &str) -> Option<&ModelInfo> {
91:         self.known_models
92:             .get(&provider)?
93:             .iter()
94:             .find(|m| m.id == model_id)
95:     }
96: 
97:     pub fn tier_for(
98:         &self,
99:         spec: &str,
100:         provider: ProviderKind,
101:         static_tier: Option<ModelTier>,
102:     ) -> ModelTier {
103:         if let Some((&t, _)) = self.overrides.iter().find(|(_, s)| s.as_str() == spec) {
104:             return t;
105:         }
106:         if let Some(t) = static_tier {
107:             return t;
108:         }
109:         if let Some((_, model_id)) = spec.split_once('/')
110:             && let Some(models) = self.known_models.get(&provider)
111:             && let Some(pos) = models.iter().position(|m| m.id == model_id)
112:         {
113:             return tier_for_position(pos);
114:         }
115:         ModelTier::Medium
116:     }
117: 
118:     pub fn spec_for_tier(&self, provider: ProviderKind, tier: ModelTier) -> Option<String> {
119:         let prefix = format!("{provider}/");
120:         if let Some(spec) = self.overrides.get(&tier)
121:             && spec.starts_with(&prefix)
122:         {
123:             return Some(spec.clone());
124:         }
125: 
126:         let models = self.known_models.get(&provider).filter(|m| !m.is_empty())?;
127:         let slot = match tier {
128:             ModelTier::Strong => 0,
129:             ModelTier::Medium => 1,
130:             ModelTier::Weak => 2,
131:             ModelTier::Compaction => return None,
132:         };
133:         let idx = slot.min(models.len() - 1);
134:         let spec = format!("{provider}/{}", models[idx].id);
135: 
136:         let overridden_elsewhere = self.overrides.iter().any(|(&t, s)| s == &spec && t != tier);
137:         (!overridden_elsewhere).then_some(spec)
138:     }
139: 
140:     pub fn spec_for_tier_any(&self, tier: ModelTier) -> Option<String> {
141:         if let Some(spec) = self.overrides.get(&tier) {
142:             return Some(spec.clone());
143:         }
144:         for &provider in self.known_models.keys() {
145:             if let Some(spec) = self.spec_for_tier(provider, tier) {
146:                 return Some(spec);
147:             }
148:         }
149:         None
150:     }
151: 
152:     pub fn override_tier_label(&self, spec: &str) -> Option<String> {
153:         let tiers: Vec<_> = self
154:             .overrides
155:             .iter()
156:             .rev()
157:             .filter(|(_, s)| s.as_str() == spec)
158:             .map(|(t, _)| t.to_string())
159:             .collect();
160:         (!tiers.is_empty()).then(|| tiers.join("/"))
161:     }
162: }
163: 
164: fn tier_for_position(pos: usize) -> ModelTier {
165:     [ModelTier::Strong, ModelTier::Medium, ModelTier::Weak][pos.min(2)]
166: }
167: 
168: // On-disk format: { "provider/model": "tier", ... } for human readability.
169: // Inverted to/from the in-memory BTreeMap<ModelTier, String>.
170: 
171: fn read_overrides(path: &Path) -> BTreeMap<ModelTier, String> {
172:     let Ok(raw) = std::fs::read_to_string(path) else {
173:         return BTreeMap::new();
174:     };
175:     if raw.trim().is_empty() {
176:         return BTreeMap::new();
177:     }
178:     if let Ok(map) = serde_json::from_str::<BTreeMap<ModelTier, String>>(&raw) {
179:         return map;
180:     }
181:     // Legacy format: { "provider/model": "tier" } — invert on read.
182:     match serde_json::from_str::<BTreeMap<String, ModelTier>>(&raw) {
183:         Ok(legacy) => legacy.into_iter().map(|(s, t)| (t, s)).collect(),
184:         Err(e) => {
185:             warn!(path = %path.display(), error = %e, "failed to parse tier overrides, ignoring");
186:             BTreeMap::new()
187:         }
188:     }
189: }
190: 
191: fn write_overrides(path: &Path, overrides: &BTreeMap<ModelTier, String>) {
192:     // Invert to human-readable { "spec": "tier" } format on disk.
193:     let disk: BTreeMap<String, ModelTier> =
194:         overrides.iter().map(|(t, s)| (s.clone(), *t)).collect();
195:     let json = match serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&disk) {
196:         Ok(v) => v,
197:         Err(e) => {
198:             warn!(error = %e, "failed to serialize tier overrides");
199:             return;
200:         }
201:     };
202:     if let Err(e) = atomic_write(path, &json) {
203:         warn!(path = %path.display(), error = %e, "failed to persist tier overrides");
204:     }
205: }

1: //! Session persistence with append-only JSONL log format.
2: //!
3: //! Each session is stored as `{uuid}.jsonl`, one JSON record per line. The format is
4: //! crash-safe: on load, any trailing run of unparseable lines is discarded (a partial
5: //! flush may corrupt multiple trailing records). `SessionLog` tracks cursor state to
6: //! enable O(delta) incremental saves.
7: //!
8: //! Legacy `.json` files are loaded transparently and converted to `.jsonl` on next save.

45: #[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
46: pub struct StoredTokenUsage {
47:     #[serde(default)]
48:     pub input: u32,

50:     pub output: u32,
51:     #[serde(default)]
52:     pub cache_creation: u32,

63:         self.input + self.output + self.cache_creation + self.cache_read
64:     }
65: }
66:

68:     fn add_assign(&mut self, rhs: Self) {

71:         self.cache_creation += rhs.cache_creation;

167: impl StoredThinking {

200: pub trait TitleSource {
201:     fn first_user_text(&self) -> Option<&str>;
202: }
203: 
204: pub fn generate_title<M: TitleSource>(messages: &[M]) -> String {
205:     let first_user_text = messages.iter().find_map(|m| m.first_user_text());
206: 
207:     let Some(text) = first_user_text.map(str::trim).filter(|t| !t.is_empty()) else {
208:         return DEFAULT_TITLE.into();
209:     };
210: 
211:     if text.len() <= MAX_TITLE_LEN {
212:         return text.to_string();
213:     }
214: 
215:     let boundary = text.floor_char_boundary(MAX_TITLE_LEN);
216:     let truncated = &text[..boundary];
217:     match truncated.rfind(' ') {
218:         Some(pos) if pos > MAX_TITLE_LEN / 2 => format!("{}…", &truncated[..pos]),
219:         _ => format!("{truncated}…"),
220:     }
221: }

252: // -- SessionLog: append-only persistence --
253: 
254: pub struct SessionLog {
255:     session_id: String,
256:     file: File,
257:     saved_msg_count: usize,
258:     saved_tool_ids: HashSet<String>,
259:     saved_sub_msg_counts: HashMap<String, usize>,
260: }
261: 
262: fn sub_msg_snapshot<M>(map: &HashMap<String, Vec<M>>) -> HashMap<String, usize> {
263:     map.iter().map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), v.len())).collect()
264: }
265: 
266: impl SessionLog {
267:     pub fn create<M, U, T>(dir: &Path, session: &Session<M, U, T>) -> Result<Self, SessionError>
268:     where
269:         M: Serialize,
270:         U: Serialize,
271:         T: Serialize,
272:     {
273:         fs::create_dir_all(dir).map_err(StorageError::from)?;
274:         let path = dir.join(format!("{}.jsonl", session.id));
275:         let mut file = File::create(&path).map_err(StorageError::from)?;
276:         write_full_session(&mut file, session)?;
277:         file.sync_data().map_err(StorageError::from)?;
278: 
279:         update_cwd_index(dir, &session.cwd, &session.id)?;
280: 
281:         Ok(Self::cursor_from(session, file))
282:     }
283: 
284:     pub fn open<M, U, T>(
285:         dir: &Path,
286:         session_id: &str,
287:     ) -> Result<(Session<M, U, T>, Self), SessionError>
288:     where
289:         M: Serialize + DeserializeOwned,
290:         U: Serialize + DeserializeOwned + Default,
291:         T: Serialize + DeserializeOwned,
292:     {
293:         let path = dir.join(format!("{session_id}.jsonl"));
294:         let session = load_jsonl::<M, U, T>(&path)?;
295: 
296:         let file = OpenOptions::new()
297:             .append(true)
298:             .open(&path)
299:             .map_err(StorageError::from)?;
300: 
301:         let log = Self::cursor_from(&session, file);
302:         Ok((session, log))
303:     }
304: 
305:     pub fn session_id(&self) -> &str {
306:         &self.session_id
307:     }
308: 
309:     pub fn append<M, U, T>(&mut self, session: &Session<M, U, T>) -> Result<(), SessionError>
310:     where
311:         M: Serialize,
312:         U: Serialize,
313:         T: Serialize,
314:     {
315:         if session.id != self.session_id {
316:             return Err(SessionError::IdMismatch {
317:                 log_id: self.session_id.clone(),
318:                 given_id: session.id.clone(),
319:             });
320:         }
321: 
322:         if self.saved_msg_count > session.messages.len()
323:             || self
324:                 .saved_tool_ids
325:                 .iter()
326:                 .any(|id| !session.tool_outputs.contains_key(id))
327:             || self.saved_sub_msg_counts.iter().any(|(sub, &count)| {
328:                 session
329:                     .subagent_messages
330:                     .get(sub)
331:                     .is_none_or(|msgs| count > msgs.len())
332:             })
333:         {
334:             return Err(SessionError::CursorAhead {
335:                 saved: self.saved_msg_count,
336:                 actual: session.messages.len(),
337:             });
338:         }
339: 
340:         let mut buf = Vec::new();
341:         let mut new_msg_count = self.saved_msg_count;
342:         let mut new_tool_ids = Vec::new();
343: 
344:         for msg in &session.messages[self.saved_msg_count..] {
345:             append_record(&mut buf, &LogRecord::<&M, &U, &T>::Msg { d: msg })?;
346:             new_msg_count += 1;
347:         }
348: 
349:         for (id, output) in &session.tool_outputs {
350:             if !self.saved_tool_ids.contains(id) {
351:                 append_record(
352:                     &mut buf,
353:                     &LogRecord::<&M, &U, &T>::Out {
354:                         id: id.clone(),
355:                         d: output,
356:                     },
357:                 )?;
358:                 new_tool_ids.push(id.clone());
359:             }
360:         }
361: 
362:         let mut new_sub_counts: Vec<(String, usize)> = Vec::new();
363:         for (sub_id, msgs) in &session.subagent_messages {
364:             let saved = self.saved_sub_msg_counts.get(sub_id).copied().unwrap_or(0);
365:             for msg in &msgs[saved..] {
366:                 append_record(
367:                     &mut buf,
368:                     &LogRecord::<&M, &U, &T>::SubMsg {
369:                         sub: sub_id.clone(),
370:                         d: msg,
371:                     },
372:                 )?;
373:             }
374:             if msgs.len() > saved {
375:                 new_sub_counts.push((sub_id.clone(), msgs.len()));
376:             }
377:         }
378: 
379:         if buf.is_empty() {
380:             return Ok(());
381:         }
382: 
383:         append_record(
384:             &mut buf,
385:             &LogRecord::<&M, &U, &T>::Meta {
386:                 title: session.title.clone(),
387:                 token_usage: &session.token_usage,
388:                 updated_at: session.updated_at,
389:                 meta: session.meta.clone(),
390:             },
391:         )?;
392: 
393:         self.file.write_all(&buf).map_err(StorageError::from)?;
394:         self.file.sync_data().map_err(StorageError::from)?;
395: 
396:         self.saved_msg_count = new_msg_count;
397:         self.saved_tool_ids.extend(new_tool_ids);
398:         for (sub_id, count) in new_sub_counts {
399:             self.saved_sub_msg_counts.insert(sub_id, count);
400:         }
401: 
402:         Ok(())
403:     }
404: 
405:     pub fn compact<M, U, T>(
406:         &mut self,
407:         dir: &Path,
408:         session: &Session<M, U, T>,
409:     ) -> Result<(), SessionError>
410:     where
411:         M: Serialize,
412:         U: Serialize,
413:         T: Serialize,
414:     {
415:         if session.id != self.session_id {
416:             return Err(SessionError::IdMismatch {
417:                 log_id: self.session_id.clone(),
418:                 given_id: session.id.clone(),
419:             });
420:         }
421: 
422:         let path = dir.join(format!("{}.jsonl", session.id));
423:         let tmp = path.with_extension("jsonl.tmp");
424: 
425:         let mut tmp_file = File::create(&tmp).map_err(StorageError::from)?;
426:         write_full_session(&mut tmp_file, session)?;
427:         tmp_file.sync_data().map_err(StorageError::from)?;
428: 
429:         fs::rename(&tmp, &path).map_err(StorageError::from)?;
430: 
431:         self.file = OpenOptions::new()
432:             .append(true)
433:             .open(&path)
434:             .map_err(StorageError::from)?;
435:         self.saved_msg_count = session.messages.len();
436:         self.saved_tool_ids = session.tool_outputs.keys().cloned().collect();
437:         self.saved_sub_msg_counts = sub_msg_snapshot(&session.subagent_messages);
438: 
439:         Ok(())
440:     }
441: 
442:     fn cursor_from<M, U, T>(session: &Session<M, U, T>, file: File) -> Self {
443:         Self {
444:             session_id: session.id.clone(),
445:             file,
446:             saved_msg_count: session.messages.len(),
447:             saved_tool_ids: session.tool_outputs.keys().cloned().collect(),
448:             saved_sub_msg_counts: sub_msg_snapshot(&session.subagent_messages),
449:         }
450:     }
451: }
452: 
453: fn write_full_session<M, U, T>(
454:     file: &mut File,
455:     session: &Session<M, U, T>,
456: ) -> Result<(), SessionError>
457: where
458:     M: Serialize,
459:     U: Serialize,
460:     T: Serialize,
461: {
462:     let mut buf = Vec::new();
463:     append_record(
464:         &mut buf,
465:         &LogRecord::<&M, &U, &T>::Header {
466:             v: LOG_FORMAT_VERSION,
467:             id: session.id.clone(),
468:             model: session.model.clone(),
469:             cwd: session.cwd.clone(),
470:             created_at: session.created_at,
471:         },
472:     )?;
473:     file.write_all(&buf).map_err(StorageError::from)?;
474:     for msg in &session.messages {
475:         buf.clear();
476:         append_record(&mut buf, &LogRecord::<&M, &U, &T>::Msg { d: msg })?;
477:         file.write_all(&buf).map_err(StorageError::from)?;
478:     }
479:     for (id, output) in &session.tool_outputs {
480:         buf.clear();
481:         append_record(
482:             &mut buf,
483:             &LogRecord::<&M, &U, &T>::Out {
484:                 id: id.clone(),
485:                 d: output,
486:             },
487:         )?;
488:         file.write_all(&buf).map_err(StorageError::from)?;
489:     }
490:     for (sub_id, msgs) in &session.subagent_messages {
491:         for msg in msgs {
492:             buf.clear();
493:             append_record(
494:                 &mut buf,
495:                 &LogRecord::<&M, &U, &T>::SubMsg {
496:                     sub: sub_id.clone(),
497:                     d: msg,
498:                 },
499:             )?;
500:             file.write_all(&buf).map_err(StorageError::from)?;
501:         }
502:     }
503:     buf.clear();
504:     append_record(
505:         &mut buf,
506:         &LogRecord::<&M, &U, &T>::Meta {
507:             title: session.title.clone(),
508:             token_usage: &session.token_usage,
509:             updated_at: session.updated_at,
510:             meta: session.meta.clone(),
511:         },
512:     )?;
513:     file.write_all(&buf).map_err(StorageError::from)?;
514:     Ok(())
515: }
516: 
517: fn append_record<R: Serialize>(buf: &mut Vec<u8>, record: &R) -> Result<(), SessionError> {
518:     serde_json::to_writer(&mut *buf, record).map_err(StorageError::from)?;
519:     buf.push(b'\n');
520:     Ok(())
521: }
522: 
523: fn load_jsonl<M, U, T>(path: &Path) -> Result<Session<M, U, T>, SessionError>
524: where
525:     M: DeserializeOwned,
526:     U: DeserializeOwned + Default,
527:     T: DeserializeOwned,
528: {
529:     let file = File::open(path).map_err(StorageError::from)?;
530:     let reader = BufReader::new(file);
531:     let mut line_count = 0usize;
532: 
533:     let mut id = String::new();
534:     let mut model = String::new();
535:     let mut cwd = String::new();
536:     let mut created_at = 0u64;
537:     let mut messages = Vec::new();
538:     let mut tool_outputs = HashMap::new();
539:     let mut subagent_messages: HashMap<String, Vec<M>> = HashMap::new();
540:     let mut title = DEFAULT_TITLE.to_string();
541:     let mut token_usage = U::default();
542:     let mut updated_at = 0u64;
543:     let mut meta = SessionMeta::default();
544:     let mut got_header = false;
545: 
546:     for line_result in reader.lines() {
547:         let line = line_result.map_err(StorageError::from)?;
548:         line_count += 1;
549:         if line.is_empty() {
550:             continue;
551:         }
552:         let record: LogRecord<M, U, T> = match serde_json::from_str(&line) {
553:             Ok(r) => r,
554:             Err(e) => {
555:                 warn!(
556:                     path = %path.display(),
557:                     error = %e,
558:                     line = line_count,
559:                     "skipping unrecognized JSONL record",
560:                 );
561:                 continue;
562:             }
563:         };
564:         match record {
565:             LogRecord::Header {
566:                 v,
567:                 id: h_id,
568:                 model: h_model,
569:                 cwd: h_cwd,
570:                 created_at: h_created,
571:             } => {
572:                 if v != LOG_FORMAT_VERSION {
573:                     return Err(SessionError::VersionMismatch {
574:                         found: v,
575:                         expected: LOG_FORMAT_VERSION,
576:                     });
577:                 }
578:                 id = h_id;
579:                 model = h_model;
580:                 cwd = h_cwd;
581:                 created_at = h_created;
582:                 got_header = true;
583:             }
584:             LogRecord::Msg { d } => messages.push(d),
585:             LogRecord::Out { id: out_id, d } => {
586:                 tool_outputs.insert(out_id, d);
587:             }
588:             LogRecord::SubMsg { sub, d } => {
589:                 subagent_messages.entry(sub).or_default().push(d);
590:             }
591:             LogRecord::Meta {
592:                 title: m_title,
593:                 token_usage: m_usage,
594:                 updated_at: m_updated,
595:                 meta: m_meta,
596:             } => {
597:                 title = m_title;
598:                 token_usage = m_usage;
599:                 updated_at = m_updated;
600:                 meta = m_meta;
601:             }
602:         }
603:     }
604: 
605:     if !got_header {
606:         return Err(StorageError::NotFound(path.display().to_string()).into());
607:     }
608: 
609:     Ok(Session {
610:         version: SESSION_VERSION,
611:         id,
612:         title,
613:         cwd,
614:         model,
615:         messages,
616:         token_usage,
617:         tool_outputs,
618:         subagent_messages,
619:         meta,
620:         created_at,
621:         updated_at,
622:     })
623: }
624: 
625: // -- CWD index --
626: 
627: fn load_cwd_index(dir: &Path) -> HashMap<String, String> {
628:     fs::read(dir.join(CWD_INDEX_FILE))
629:         .ok()
630:         .and_then(|data| serde_json::from_slice(&data).ok())
631:         .unwrap_or_default()
632: }
633: 
634: fn update_cwd_index(dir: &Path, cwd: &str, session_id: &str) -> Result<(), StorageError> {
635:     let mut index = load_cwd_index(dir);
636:     index.insert(cwd.to_string(), session_id.to_string());
637:     atomic_write(&dir.join(CWD_INDEX_FILE), &serde_json::to_vec(&index)?)
638: }
639: 
640: fn try_remove(path: &Path) -> Result<bool, StorageError> {
641:     match fs::remove_file(path) {
642:         Ok(()) => Ok(true),
643:         Err(e) if e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound => Ok(false),
644:         Err(e) => Err(e.into()),
645:     }
646: }
647: 
648: fn remove_from_cwd_index(dir: &Path, session_id: &str) -> Result<(), StorageError> {
649:     let mut index = load_cwd_index(dir);
650:     let before = index.len();
651:     index.retain(|_, v| v != session_id);
652:     if index.len() != before {
653:         atomic_write(&dir.join(CWD_INDEX_FILE), &serde_json::to_vec(&index)?)?;
654:     }
655:     Ok(())
656: }
657: 
658: // -- Header scanning for session list --
659: 
660: #[derive(Deserialize)]
661: struct JsonlHeader {
662:     v: u32,
663:     id: String,
664:     cwd: String,
665: }
666: 
667: #[derive(Deserialize)]
668: #[serde(tag = "t", rename_all = "snake_case")]
669: enum ScanRecord {
670:     Meta {
671:         title: String,
672:         updated_at: u64,
673:     },
674:     #[serde(other)]
675:     Other,
676: }
677: 
678: fn scan_headers(cwd: &str, dir: &Path) -> Result<Vec<SessionSummary>, StorageError> {
679:     let mut out = Vec::new();
680:     for path in session_entries(dir)? {
681:         let ext = path.extension().and_then(|e| e.to_str()).unwrap_or("");
682:         match ext {
683:             "jsonl" => {
684:                 if let Some(summary) = scan_jsonl_header(cwd, &path) {
685:                     out.push(summary);
686:                 }
687:             }
688:             "json" => {
689:                 if let Some(summary) = scan_legacy_header(cwd, &path) {
690:                     out.push(summary);
691:                 }
692:             }
693:             _ => {}
694:         }
695:     }
696:     Ok(out)
697: }
698: 
699: const TAIL_BUF: u64 = 4096;
700: 
701: fn scan_jsonl_header(cwd: &str, path: &Path) -> Option<SessionSummary> {
702:     let mut file = File::open(path).ok()?;
703:     let header: JsonlHeader = {
704:         let mut reader = BufReader::new(&file);
705:         let mut line = String::new();
706:         reader.read_line(&mut line).ok()?;
707:         serde_json::from_str(line.trim_end()).ok()?
708:     };
709:     if header.v != LOG_FORMAT_VERSION || header.cwd != cwd {
710:         return None;
711:     }
712: 
713:     let (title, updated_at) =
714:         read_last_meta(&mut file).unwrap_or_else(|| (DEFAULT_TITLE.to_string(), 0));
715: 
716:     Some(SessionSummary {
717:         id: header.id,
718:         title,
719:         updated_at,
720:     })
721: }
722: 
723: fn read_last_meta(file: &mut File) -> Option<(String, u64)> {
724:     let len = file.seek(SeekFrom::End(0)).ok()?;
725:     let mut tail = TAIL_BUF.min(len);
726:     loop {
727:         file.seek(SeekFrom::End(-(tail as i64))).ok()?;
728:         let mut buf = vec![0u8; tail as usize];
729:         file.read_exact(&mut buf).ok()?;
730: 
731:         let content = buf.strip_suffix(b"\n").unwrap_or(&buf);
732:         if let Some(nl) = content.iter().rposition(|&b| b == b'\n') {
733:             let last_line = &content[nl + 1..];
734:             if let Ok(ScanRecord::Meta { title, updated_at }) = serde_json::from_slice(last_line) {
735:                 return Some((title, updated_at));
736:             }
737:             return None;
738:         }
739: 
740:         if tail >= len {
741:             return None;
742:         }
743:         tail = (tail * 2).min(len);
744:     }
745: }
746: 
747: fn scan_legacy_header(cwd: &str, path: &Path) -> Option<SessionSummary> {
748:     let data = fs::read(path).ok()?;
749:     let h: LegacyHeader = serde_json::from_slice(&data).ok()?;
750:     if h.version != SESSION_VERSION || h.cwd != cwd {
751:         return None;
752:     }
753:     Some(SessionSummary {
754:         id: h.id,
755:         title: h.title,
756:         updated_at: h.updated_at,
757:     })
758: }
759: 
760: fn session_entries(dir: &Path) -> Result<Vec<PathBuf>, StorageError> {
761:     let mut entries = Vec::new();
762:     for entry in fs::read_dir(dir)? {
763:         let entry = entry?;
764:         let path = entry.path();
765:         let Some(stem) = path.file_stem().and_then(|s| s.to_str()) else {
766:             continue;
767:         };
768:         if stem == CWD_INDEX_FILE.trim_end_matches(".json") {
769:             continue;
770:         }
771:         if path
772:             .extension()
773:             .is_some_and(|e| e == "json" || e == "jsonl")
774:         {
775:             entries.push(path);
776:         }
777:     }
778:     Ok(entries)
779: }

781: // -- Session impl --
782: 
783: impl<M, U, T> Session<M, U, T>
784: where
785:     M: Serialize + DeserializeOwned + TitleSource,
786:     U: Serialize + DeserializeOwned + Default,
787:     T: Serialize + DeserializeOwned,
788: {
789:     pub fn new(model: &str, cwd: &str) -> Self {
790:         let now = now_epoch();
791:         Self {
792:             version: SESSION_VERSION,
793:             id: uuid::Uuid::new_v4().to_string(),
794:             title: DEFAULT_TITLE.into(),
795:             cwd: cwd.into(),
796:             model: model.into(),
797:             messages: Vec::new(),
798:             token_usage: U::default(),
799:             tool_outputs: HashMap::new(),
800:             subagent_messages: HashMap::new(),
801:             meta: SessionMeta {
802:                 mode: Some(StoredMode::Build),
803:                 ..Default::default()
804:             },
805:             created_at: now,
806:             updated_at: now,
807:         }
808:     }
809: 
810:     /// After `messages` is truncated (rewind), state keyed by tool_use_id can
811:     /// point at calls that no longer exist. On restore that shows up as ghost
812:     /// subagent tabs and leaked tool outputs, so this drops everything not
813:     /// reachable from `messages`.
814:     ///
815:     /// If you add another field keyed by tool_use_id, prune it here too.
816:     pub fn prune_orphans(&mut self, tool_ids: impl Fn(&M) -> Vec<String>) {
817:         let main_ids: HashSet<String> = self.messages.iter().flat_map(&tool_ids).collect();
818:         self.subagent_messages.retain(|id, _| main_ids.contains(id));
819:         self.meta
820:             .subagents
821:             .retain(|sa| main_ids.contains(&sa.tool_use_id));
822: 
823:         let live: HashSet<String> = self
824:             .subagent_messages
825:             .values()
826:             .flatten()
827:             .flat_map(&tool_ids)
828:             .chain(main_ids)
829:             .collect();
830:         self.tool_outputs.retain(|id, _| live.contains(id));
831:     }
832: 
833:     pub fn save(&mut self, dir: &StateDir) -> Result<(), SessionError> {
834:         let sessions_dir = dir.ensure_subdir(SESSIONS_DIR)?;
835:         self.save_to(&sessions_dir)
836:     }
837: 
838:     pub fn save_to(&mut self, dir: &Path) -> Result<(), SessionError> {
839:         self.updated_at = now_epoch();
840:         let _log = SessionLog::create(dir, self)?;
841:         Ok(())
842:     }
843: 
844:     pub fn load(id: &str, dir: &StateDir) -> Result<Self, SessionError> {
845:         let sessions_dir = dir.ensure_subdir(SESSIONS_DIR)?;
846:         Self::load_from(id, &sessions_dir)
847:     }
848: 
849:     pub fn load_from(id: &str, dir: &Path) -> Result<Self, SessionError> {
850:         let jsonl_path = dir.join(format!("{id}.jsonl"));
851:         if jsonl_path.exists() {
852:             return load_jsonl(&jsonl_path);
853:         }
854: 
855:         let json_path = dir.join(format!("{id}.json"));
856:         if !json_path.exists() {
857:             return Err(StorageError::NotFound(id.into()).into());
858:         }
859:         let data = fs::read(&json_path).map_err(StorageError::from)?;
860:         let session: Self = serde_json::from_slice(&data).map_err(StorageError::from)?;
861:         if session.version != SESSION_VERSION {
862:             return Err(SessionError::VersionMismatch {
863:                 found: session.version,
864:                 expected: SESSION_VERSION,
865:             });
866:         }
867:         Ok(session)
868:     }
869: 
870:     pub fn list(cwd: &str, dir: &StateDir) -> Result<Vec<SessionSummary>, SessionError> {
871:         let sessions_dir = dir.ensure_subdir(SESSIONS_DIR)?;
872:         Self::list_in(cwd, &sessions_dir)
873:     }
874: 
875:     pub fn list_in(cwd: &str, dir: &Path) -> Result<Vec<SessionSummary>, SessionError> {
876:         let mut summaries = scan_headers(cwd, dir)?;
877:         summaries.sort_unstable_by_key(|s| Reverse(s.updated_at));
878:         Ok(summaries)
879:     }
880: 
881:     pub fn latest(cwd: &str, dir: &StateDir) -> Result<Option<Self>, SessionError> {
882:         let sessions_dir = dir.ensure_subdir(SESSIONS_DIR)?;
883:         Self::latest_in(cwd, &sessions_dir)
884:     }
885: 
886:     pub fn latest_in(cwd: &str, dir: &Path) -> Result<Option<Self>, SessionError> {
887:         let index = load_cwd_index(dir);
888:         if let Some(id) = index.get(cwd)
889:             && let Ok(s) = Self::load_from(id, dir)
890:         {
891:             return Ok(Some(s));
892:         }
893:         let summaries = scan_headers(cwd, dir)?;
894:         let latest = summaries.into_iter().max_by_key(|s| s.updated_at);
895:         match latest {
896:             Some(s) => Self::load_from(&s.id, dir).map(Some),
897:             None => Ok(None),
898:         }
899:     }
900: 
901:     pub fn update_title_if_default(&mut self) {
902:         if self.title == DEFAULT_TITLE {
903:             self.title = generate_title(&self.messages);
904:         }
905:     }
906: 
907:     pub fn delete(id: &str, dir: &StateDir) -> Result<(), SessionError> {
908:         let sessions_dir = dir.ensure_subdir(SESSIONS_DIR)?;
909:         Self::delete_from(id, &sessions_dir)
910:     }
911: 
912:     pub fn delete_from(id: &str, dir: &Path) -> Result<(), SessionError> {
913:         let jsonl_gone = try_remove(&dir.join(format!("{id}.jsonl")))?;
914:         let json_gone = try_remove(&dir.join(format!("{id}.json")))?;
915: 
916:         if !jsonl_gone && !json_gone {
917:             return Err(StorageError::NotFound(id.into()).into());
918:         }
919: 
920:         remove_from_cwd_index(dir, id)?;
921:         Ok(())
922:     }
923: 
924:     pub fn migrate_to_jsonl(dir: &Path, session: &Self) -> Result<SessionLog, SessionError> {
925:         let log = SessionLog::create(dir, session)?;
926:         let _ = fs::remove_file(dir.join(format!("{}.json", session.id)));
927:         Ok(log)
928:     }
929: }

981:     fn prune_orphans_drops_unreachable_tool_state() {
982:         fn ids(m: &Value) -> Vec<String> {
983:             vec![m.as_str().unwrap().to_owned()]
984:         }
985:         fn subagent(id: &str) -> StoredSubagent {
986:             StoredSubagent {
987:                 tool_use_id: id.into(),
988:                 name: "sub".into(),
989:                 prompt: None,
990:                 model: None,
991:             }
992:         }
993: 
994:         let mut session: TestSession = Session::new("model", "/p");
995:         session.messages.push("task-live".into());
996:         session
997:             .subagent_messages
998:             .insert("task-live".into(), vec!["sub-tool".into()]);
999:         session
1000:             .subagent_messages
1001:             .insert("task-stale".into(), vec!["stale-sub-tool".into()]);
1002:         session.meta.subagents = vec![subagent("task-live"), subagent("task-stale")];
1003:         for id in ["task-live", "sub-tool", "stale-sub-tool", "orphan"] {
1004:             session.tool_outputs.insert(id.into(), Value::Null);
1005:         }
1006: 
1007:         session.prune_orphans(ids);
1008: 
1009:         assert_eq!(
1010:             session.subagent_messages.keys().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
1011:             ["task-live"]
1012:         );
1013:         let subagent_ids: Vec<_> = session
1014:             .meta
1015:             .subagents
1016:             .iter()
1017:             .map(|sa| sa.tool_use_id.as_str())
1018:             .collect();
1019:         assert_eq!(subagent_ids, ["task-live"]);
1020:         let mut outputs: Vec<_> = session.tool_outputs.keys().cloned().collect();
1021:         outputs.sort();
1022:         assert_eq!(outputs, ["sub-tool", "task-live"]);
1023:     }

1275:     #[test_case("short title", "short title" ; "short_passthrough")]
1276:     #[test_case("", DEFAULT_TITLE ; "empty_defaults")]
1277:     #[test_case(
1278:         "This is a very long title that exceeds the sixty character limit and should be truncated at a word boundary",
1279:         "This is a very long title that exceeds the sixty character…"
1280:         ; "long_truncates_at_word"

7: const MODEL_FILE: &str = "model";
8: const RECENT_FILE: &str = "recent-models";
9: const MAX_RECENTS: usize = 4;
10: 
11: pub fn persist_model(dir: &StateDir, spec: &str) {
12:     let _ = atomic_write(&dir.path().join(MODEL_FILE), spec.as_bytes());
13: }
14: 
15: pub fn read_model(dir: &StateDir) -> Option<String> {
16:     let raw = fs::read_to_string(dir.path().join(MODEL_FILE)).ok()?;
17:     let spec = raw.trim();
18:     (!spec.is_empty()).then(|| spec.to_owned())
19: }
20: 
21: #[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Default)]
22: struct RecentList(Vec<String>);
23: 
24: pub fn push_recent(dir: &StateDir, spec: &str) -> Vec<String> {
25:     let mut recents = read_recents(dir);
26:     recents.retain(|s| s != spec);
27:     recents.insert(0, spec.to_owned());
28:     recents.truncate(MAX_RECENTS);
29:     write_recents(dir, &recents);
30:     recents
31: }
32: 
33: pub fn read_recents(dir: &StateDir) -> Vec<String> {
34:     let Ok(raw) = fs::read_to_string(dir.path().join(RECENT_FILE)) else {
35:         return Vec::new();
36:     };
37:     let trimmed = raw.trim();
38:     if trimmed.is_empty() {
39:         return Vec::new();
40:     }
41:     match serde_json::from_str::<RecentList>(trimmed) {
42:         Ok(list) => list.0,
43:         Err(_) => Vec::new(),
44:     }
45: }
46: 
47: fn write_recents(dir: &StateDir, recents: &[String]) {
48:     let json = match serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&RecentList(recents.to_vec())) {
49:         Ok(v) => v,
50:         Err(_) => return,
51:     };
52:     let _ = atomic_write(&dir.path().join(RECENT_FILE), &json);
53: }

26: impl ImageMediaType {
27:     pub const ALL: [Self; 4] = [Self::Png, Self::Jpeg, Self::Gif, Self::Webp];
28: 
29:     /// Single source of truth for media-type strings: serde, data URLs,
30:     /// wire formats, and the Lua bridge all go through here.
31:     pub const fn mime(self) -> &'static str {
32:         match self {
33:             Self::Png => "image/png",
34:             Self::Jpeg => "image/jpeg",
35:             Self::Gif => "image/gif",
36:             Self::Webp => "image/webp",
37:         }
38:     }

40:     pub fn from_mime(mime: &str) -> Option<Self> {
41:         Self::ALL.into_iter().find(|m| m.mime() == mime)
42:     }

45: impl Serialize for ImageMediaType {

51: impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for ImageMediaType {
52:     fn deserialize<D: serde::Deserializer<'de>>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error> {

84: }

86: pub const IMAGE_OMITTED_NOTE: &str =
87:     "[image omitted: the current model does not support image input]";
88: 
89: /// For models without vision, image blocks become a text note instead of a
90: /// wire block the API would reject. History keeps the pixels, so switching
91: /// back to a vision-capable model restores them.
92: pub fn adapt_images_for_model<'a>(model: &Model, messages: &'a [Message]) -> Cow<'a, [Message]> {
93:     let has_image = |m: &Message| {
94:         m.content
95:             .iter()
96:             .any(|b| matches!(b, ContentBlock::Image { .. }))
97:     };
98:     if model.vision || !messages.iter().any(has_image) {
99:         return Cow::Borrowed(messages);
100:     }
101:     let adapted = messages
102:         .iter()
103:         .map(|m| {
104:             let mut m = m.clone();
105:             for block in &mut m.content {
106:                 if matches!(block, ContentBlock::Image { .. }) {
107:                     *block = ContentBlock::Text {
108:                         text: IMAGE_OMITTED_NOTE.into(),
109:                     };
110:                 }
111:             }
112:             m
113:         })
114:         .collect();
115:     Cow::Owned(adapted)
116: }

162: #[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
163: pub struct Message {
164:     pub role: Role,
165:     pub content: Vec<ContentBlock>,
166:     #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
167:     pub display_text: Option<String>,
168: }
169: 
170: impl Message {
171:     pub fn user(text: String) -> Self {
172:         Self {
173:             role: Role::User,
174:             content: vec![ContentBlock::Text { text }],
175:             ..Default::default()
176:         }
177:     }
178: 
179:     pub fn user_display(ai_text: String, display: String) -> Self {
180:         Self {
181:             role: Role::User,
182:             content: vec![ContentBlock::Text { text: ai_text }],
183:             display_text: Some(display),
184:         }
185:     }
186: 
187:     pub fn user_with_images(text: String, images: Vec<ImageSource>) -> Self {
188:         let mut content: Vec<ContentBlock> = images
189:             .into_iter()
190:             .map(|source| ContentBlock::Image { source })
191:             .collect();
192:         if !text.is_empty() {
193:             content.push(ContentBlock::Text { text });
194:         }
195:         Self {
196:             role: Role::User,
197:             content,
198:             ..Default::default()
199:         }
200:     }
201: 
202:     pub fn synthetic(text: String) -> Self {
203:         Self {
204:             role: Role::User,
205:             content: vec![ContentBlock::Text { text }],
206:             display_text: Some(String::new()),
207:         }
208:     }
209: 
210:     pub fn user_text(&self) -> Option<&str> {
211:         match &self.display_text {
212:             Some(t) if t.is_empty() => None,
213:             Some(t) => Some(t),
214:             None => self.first_text_content(),
215:         }
216:     }
217: 
218:     pub fn first_text_content(&self) -> Option<&str> {
219:         self.content.iter().find_map(|b| match b {
220:             ContentBlock::Text { text } if !text.is_empty() => Some(text.as_str()),
221:             _ => None,
222:         })
223:     }
224: 
225:     pub fn tool_uses(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (&str, &str, &Value)> {
226:         self.content.iter().filter_map(|b| match b {
227:             ContentBlock::ToolUse { id, name, input } => Some((id.as_str(), name.as_str(), input)),
228:             _ => None,
229:         })
230:     }
231: 
232:     pub fn has_tool_calls(&self) -> bool {
233:         self.content
234:             .iter()
235:             .any(|b| matches!(b, ContentBlock::ToolUse { .. }))
236:     }
237: }
238: 
239: impl TitleSource for Message {
240:     fn first_user_text(&self) -> Option<&str> {
241:         if !self.role.is_user() {
242:             return None;
243:         }
244:         self.user_text()
245:     }
246: }

264: impl StopReason {
265:     pub fn from_anthropic(s: &str) -> Self {
266:         match s {
267:             "end_turn" => Self::EndTurn,
268:             "tool_use" => Self::ToolUse,
269:             "max_tokens" => Self::MaxTokens,
270:             _ => Self::EndTurn,
271:         }
272:     }

274:     pub fn from_openai(s: &str) -> Self {
275:         match s {
276:             "stop" => Self::EndTurn,
277:             "tool_calls" => Self::ToolUse,
278:             "length" => Self::MaxTokens,

283:     pub fn from_google(s: &str) -> Self {
284:         match s {
285:             "STOP" => Self::EndTurn,
286:             "MAX_TOKENS" => Self::MaxTokens,
287:             "SAFETY" | "RECITATION" => {
288:                 warn!("Gemini stop reason: {s}, treating as end_turn");
289:                 Self::EndTurn
290:             }
291:             _ => Self::EndTurn,
292:         }
293:     }

296: const THINKING_USAGE: &str = "Usage: /thinking [off|adaptive|<budget\u{2265}1024>]";
297: const GLM_XHIGH_THRESHOLD: u32 = 8192;
298: 
299: /// Each provider speaks a different dialect of `reasoning_effort`.
300: /// New providers get a variant here instead of a new body-mutating method.
301: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
302: pub enum EffortScale {
303:     /// low / medium / high. Adaptive = medium.
304:     Standard,
305:     /// low / medium / high. Adaptive = high.
306:     PreferHigh,
307:     /// Always "high", ignores budget.
308:     HighOnly,
309:     /// none / high / xhigh. GLM reasons by default, so Off sends "none"
310:     /// explicitly. Only use behind `Model::supports_thinking`.
311:     Glm,
312: }
313: 
314: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
315: pub enum ThinkingConfig {
316:     #[default]
317:     Off,
318:     Adaptive,
319:     Budget(u32),
320: }
321: 
322: impl ThinkingConfig {
323:     pub fn is_enabled(self) -> bool {
324:         !matches!(self, Self::Off)
325:     }
326: 
327:     pub fn budget_to_effort(n: u32) -> &'static str {
328:         if n < 2048 {
329:             "low"
330:         } else if n < 8192 {
331:             "medium"
332:         } else {
333:             "high"
334:         }
335:     }
336: 
337:     pub fn apply_to_body(self, body: &mut Value, model_id: &str) {
338:         match self {
339:             Self::Off => {}
340:             Self::Adaptive => {
341:                 body["thinking"] = json!({"type": "adaptive"});
342:             }
343:             Self::Budget(n) if Self::requires_adaptive(model_id) => {
344:                 body["thinking"] = json!({"type": "adaptive"});
345:                 body["output_config"]["effort"] = json!(Self::budget_to_effort(n));
346:             }
347:             Self::Budget(n) => {
348:                 body["thinking"] = json!({"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": n});
349:             }
350:         }
351:     }
352: 
353:     /// Version check, not an allowlist, so future Opus releases work automatically.
354:     fn requires_adaptive(model_id: &str) -> bool {
355:         let Some(version) = model_id.strip_prefix("claude-opus-") else {
356:             return false;
357:         };
358:         let mut parts = version.split('-');
359:         let (Some(Ok(major)), Some(Ok(minor))) = (
360:             parts.next().map(str::parse::<u32>),
361:             parts.next().map(str::parse::<u32>),
362:         ) else {
363:             return false;
364:         };
365:         (major, minor) >= (4, 7)
366:     }
367: 
368:     pub fn apply_reasoning_effort(self, body: &mut Value, scale: EffortScale) {
369:         let effort = match (self, scale) {
370:             (Self::Off, EffortScale::Glm) => "none",
371:             (Self::Off, _) => return,
372:             (Self::Adaptive, EffortScale::Standard) => "medium",
373:             (Self::Adaptive, _) => "high",
374:             (Self::Budget(_), EffortScale::HighOnly) => "high",
375:             (Self::Budget(n), EffortScale::Glm) => {
376:                 if n >= GLM_XHIGH_THRESHOLD {
377:                     "xhigh"
378:                 } else {
379:                     "high"
380:                 }
381:             }
382:             (Self::Budget(n), EffortScale::Standard | EffortScale::PreferHigh) => {
383:                 Self::budget_to_effort(n)
384:             }
385:         };
386:         body["reasoning_effort"] = json!(effort);
387:     }
388: 
389:     pub fn apply_google_thinking(self, body: &mut Value) {
390:         match self {
391:             Self::Off => {}
392:             Self::Adaptive => {
393:                 body["generationConfig"]["thinkingConfig"] = json!({"includeThoughts": true});
394:             }
395:             Self::Budget(n) => {
396:                 body["generationConfig"]["thinkingConfig"] = json!({"thinkingBudget": n});
397:             }
398:         }
399:     }
400: 
401:     pub fn apply_local_thinking(self, body: &mut Value) {
402:         let budget = match self {
403:             Self::Off => 0,
404:             Self::Adaptive => -1,
405:             Self::Budget(n) => n as i64,
406:         };
407:         body["thinking_budget_tokens"] = json!(budget);
408:     }
409: 
410:     pub fn parse(input: &str, current: Self) -> Result<Self, &'static str> {
411:         if input.is_empty() {
412:             return Ok(if current.is_enabled() {
413:                 Self::Off
414:             } else {
415:                 Self::Adaptive
416:             });
417:         }
418:         StoredThinking::parse_setting(input)
419:             .map(Into::into)
420:             .map_err(|_| THINKING_USAGE)
421:     }
422: 
423:     pub fn status_label(self) -> Option<Cow<'static, str>> {
424:         match self {
425:             Self::Off => None,
426:             Self::Adaptive => Some(Cow::Borrowed("thinking")),
427:             Self::Budget(n) => Some(Cow::Owned(format!("thinking: {n}"))),
428:         }
429:     }
430: }
431: 
432: impl std::fmt::Display for ThinkingConfig {
433:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
434:         match self {
435:             Self::Off => f.write_str("off"),
436:             Self::Adaptive => f.write_str("adaptive"),
437:             Self::Budget(n) => write!(f, "{n}"),
438:         }
439:     }
440: }
441: 
442: impl From<StoredThinking> for ThinkingConfig {
443:     fn from(s: StoredThinking) -> Self {
444:         match s {
445:             StoredThinking::Off => Self::Off,
446:             StoredThinking::Adaptive => Self::Adaptive,
447:             StoredThinking::Budget { tokens } => Self::Budget(tokens),
448:         }
449:     }
450: }
451: 
452: impl From<ThinkingConfig> for StoredThinking {
453:     fn from(c: ThinkingConfig) -> Self {
454:         match c {
455:             ThinkingConfig::Off => Self::Off,
456:             ThinkingConfig::Adaptive => Self::Adaptive,
457:             ThinkingConfig::Budget(n) => Self::Budget { tokens: n },
458:         }
459:     }
460: }
461: 
462: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
463: pub struct RequestOptions {
464:     pub thinking: ThinkingConfig,
465:     /// Raw user preference, reconciled by [`RequestOptions::clamped`] before use.
466:     pub fast: bool,
467: }
468: 
469: impl RequestOptions {
470:     /// Strips options the model does not support. Called once before every
471:     /// request so UI state, restored sessions, and subagent flags all go
472:     /// through the same gate.
473:     pub fn clamped(self, model: &crate::model::Model) -> Self {
474:         Self {
475:             thinking: if model.supports_thinking() {
476:                 self.thinking
477:             } else {
478:                 ThinkingConfig::Off
479:             },
480:             fast: self.fast && model.supports_fast(),
481:         }
482:     }
483: }

492: /// Provider-reported usage quota, independent of local token accounting. Not every
493: /// provider exposes a programmatic quota endpoint; check `Provider::fetch_usage`.
494: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
495: pub struct ProviderUsage {
496:     /// Subscription/plan level when the provider reports one (e.g. "lite").
497:     #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
498:     pub plan: Option<String>,
499:     pub limits: Vec<UsageLimit>,
500: }
501: 
502: /// A single quota window (e.g. a 5-hour or weekly token quota).
503: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
504: pub struct UsageLimit {
505:     /// Human-readable label for the window, provided by the provider.
506:     pub label: String,
507:     /// Usage percentage within the window, 0-100.
508:     pub percentage: u32,
509:     /// When the window resets, as epoch milliseconds.
510:     #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
511:     pub reset_at: Option<u64>,
512:     /// Extra provider-supplied context, e.g. "$2.33 spent" for usage credits.
513:     #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
514:     pub detail: Option<String>,
515: }

291: fn quota_lines(state: &UsageFetchState, theme: &crate::theme::Theme) -> Vec<Line<'static>> {
292:     let fg = Style::new().fg(theme.foreground);
293:     let dim = theme.status_dim;
294:     match state {
295:         UsageFetchState::Loading => {
296:             vec![Line::from(Span::styled(format!("{PREFIX}loading…"), dim))]
297:         }
298:         UsageFetchState::Unsupported => vec![Line::from(Span::styled(
299:             format!("{PREFIX}{NO_USAGE_ENDPOINT}"),
300:             dim,
301:         ))],
302:         UsageFetchState::Error(msg) => {
303:             vec![Line::from(Span::styled(format!("{PREFIX}{msg}"), dim))]
304:         }
305:         UsageFetchState::Ready(usage) => {
306:             let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(usage.limits.len() + 1);
307:             if let Some(plan) = &usage.plan {
308:                 out.push(Line::from(Span::styled(
309:                     format!("{PREFIX}plan: {plan}"),
310:                     fg,
311:                 )));
312:             }
313:             let tz = TimeZone::system();
314:             let label_w = usage
315:                 .limits
316:                 .iter()
317:                 .map(|l| l.label.chars().count())
318:                 .max()
319:                 .unwrap_or(0);
320:             for limit in &usage.limits {
321:                 let mut spans = vec![
322:                     Span::styled(format!("{PREFIX}{:<label_w$}", limit.label), fg),
323:                     Span::styled(format!("{:>3}%", limit.percentage), theme.accent),
324:                     Span::styled(" used", dim),
325:                 ];
326:                 if let Some(detail) = &limit.detail {
327:                     spans.push(Span::styled(format!("  {detail}"), dim));
328:                 }
329:                 if let Some(ms) = limit.reset_at {
330:                     spans.push(Span::styled(
331:                         format!("  Resets {}", format_reset(ms, &tz)),
332:                         dim,
333:                     ));
334:                 }
335:                 out.push(Line::from(spans));
336:             }
337:             out
338:         }
339:     }
340: }
341: 
342: fn format_reset(epoch_ms: u64, tz: &TimeZone) -> String {
343:     let secs = (epoch_ms / 1000) as i64;
344:     let Ok(ts) = Timestamp::from_second(secs) else {
345:         return epoch_ms.to_string();
346:     };
347:     let delta = secs - Timestamp::now().as_second();
348:     if (1..DAY).contains(&delta) {
349:         return relative(delta);
350:     }
351:     let zoned = ts.to_zoned(tz.clone());
352:     let fmt = if delta < WEEK {
353:         "%a %-I:%M %p"
354:     } else {
355:         "%b %-d, %-I:%M %p"
356:     };
357:     zoned.strftime(fmt).to_string()
358: }
359: 
360: fn relative(seconds: i64) -> String {
361:     let hrs = seconds / HOUR;
362:     let mins = (seconds % HOUR) / 60;
363:     if hrs > 0 {
364:         format!("in {hrs} hr {mins} min")
365:     } else {
366:         format!("in {mins} min")
367:     }
368: }

const QUOTA_LIMIT_URL: &str = "https://api.z.ai/api/monitor/usage/quota/limit";

#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct QuotaResponse {
    data: QuotaData,
}

#[derive(Deserialize, Default)]
struct QuotaData {
    #[serde(default)]
    limits: Vec<QuotaLimit>,
    #[serde(default)]
    level: Option<String>,
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct QuotaLimit {
    #[serde(rename = "type")]
    kind: String,
    unit: u32,
    percentage: u32,
    #[serde(default, rename = "nextResetTime")]
    next_reset_time: Option<u64>,
}

anthropic/mod.rs:423-440
fn fetch_usage(&self) -> BoxFuture<'_, Result<Option<ProviderUsage>, AgentError>> {
        Box::pin(async move {
            if !usage_eligible(&self.auth.lock().unwrap()) {
                return Ok(None);
            }
            let request = self
                .build_request("GET", Some(USAGE_URL))
                .header("anthropic-beta", OAUTH_BETA)
                .body(())?;
            let mut response = self.client.send_async(request).await?;
            if response.status().as_u16() != 200 {
                return Err(AgentError::from_response(response).await);
            }
            let parsed: OauthUsage = serde_json::from_str(&response.text().await?)?;
            Ok(Some(parsed.into()))
        })
    }
}

        Ok(endpoint) => endpoint,
        Err(err) => {
            warn!(error = %err, fallback = DEFAULT_API_ENDPOINT, "Copilot endpoint discovery failed");
            DEFAULT_API_ENDPOINT.to_owned()
        }
    }
}

impl From<QuotaResponse> for ProviderUsage {
    fn from(resp: QuotaResponse) -> Self {
        ProviderUsage {
            plan: resp.data.level,
            limits: resp
                .data
                .limits
                .into_iter()
                .map(|l| UsageLimit {
                    label: quota_label(&l.kind, l.unit),
                    percentage: l.percentage,
                    reset_at: l.next_reset_time,
                    detail: None,
                })
                .collect(),
        }
    }
}

Here is the complete token usage tracking architecture.

---

## Token Usage Architecture (v0.3.26)

### 1. Storage Model (per-model accounting)

**`maki-storage/src/sessions.rs:45-101`**

A `StoredTokenUsage` struct (4 fields: `input`, `output`, `cache_creation`, `cache_read`) is stored in `SessionMeta.usage_by_model: HashMap<String, StoredTokenUsage>` (line 101). Each session's JSONL `Meta` record carries this map.

Key design points:

- `#[serde(default)]` on all 4 fields and on the HashMap ensures backward compat with sessions saved before this feature — they load with empty maps (test at line 1081).
- `StoredTokenUsage` implements `AddAssign` (line 67) so the UI can do `entry(model).or_default() += usage`.
- Helpers: `total_input()` = input + cache_read + cache_creation (line 58), `total()` = all four summed (line 62).
- The type is kept storage-local to avoid a circular dep on `maki-providers`.

### 2. Provider-side `TokenUsage` and Cost Model

**`maki-providers/src/model.rs:378-450`**

`TokenUsage` is the canonical provider type — same 4 fields (`input`, `output`, `cache_creation`, `cache_read`) but with serde rename annotations matching Anthropic's wire format. It has bidirectional `From` impls with `StoredTokenUsage` (lines 390-410).

`TokenUsage::cost(pricing, fast)` computes dollar cost:
- Uses regular `pricing.input`, `.output`, `.cache_write`, `.cache_read` by default.
- If `pricing.fast` is set and `fast` is true, substitutes fast-path rates and derives cache pricing as multipliers of the fast input rate: cache_write = input × 1.25, cache_read = input × 0.10 (lines 99-100, 426-427).
- Formula: each counter ÷ 1M × its rate, summed (lines 421-440).

### 3. Accumulation Point

**`maki-ui/src/app/mod.rs:1039-1041`**

On every `TurnComplete` event, the UI does:

```rust
.usage_by_model
    .entry(tc.model.clone())
    .or_default() += tc.usage.into();
```

The `model` field comes from `TurnCompleteEvent.model` — the model ID that actually served the turn. Since subagents can use different models, each gets its own bucket.

### 4. Provider Quota Endpoints

**`maki-providers/src/provider.rs:266-270`**

The `Provider` trait has a default `fetch_usage()` returning `Ok(None)`. Providers opt in:

#### Z.AI (`maki-providers/src/providers/zai/mod.rs:331-337`)
- GET `https://api.z.ai/api/monitor/usage/quota/limit`
- Parses `QuotaResponse` → `ProviderUsage` via `From` impl (line 61):
  - `plan` = `data.level` (subscription tier like "lite")
  - `limits` = each `QuotaLimit` with:
    - Label from `quota_label()`: maps `TOKENS_LIMIT` unit 3 → "5-hour tokens", unit 6 → "Weekly tokens", `TIME_LIMIT` → "Subscription time" (line 52-58)
    - `percentage`, `next_reset_time`
  - No `detail` field from Z.AI.

#### Anthropic (`maki-providers/src/providers/anthropic/mod.rs:423-438`)
- GET `https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage` with `anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20`
- Only on OAuth auth (skips API-key auth — `usage_eligible()` checks for `Authorization` header, line 209)
- `OauthUsage` (line 64) has: general `limits` (with kind/percent/resets_at), plus `spend`, `five_hour`, `seven_day`, `seven_day_sonnet`, `seven_day_opus` fallback windows.
- The `From<OauthUsage>` (line 171) constructs `UsageLimit` items: if API limits exist, they take priority; otherwise synthesizes from the typed window fields (session, weekly-all, Sonnet/Opus-specific).
- Also captures `spend` info into a `detail` string like "$2.33 spent".

### 5. UI: `/usage` Modal

**`maki-ui/src/components/usage_modal.rs` (all 484 lines)**

Renders three sections:

1. **Session total** (line 145-155): one row showing `in`, `out`, `cache read`, `cache write`, `total` token counts (using `format_tokens()`), plus dollar cost if pricing is available.

2. **Provider quota** (line 157-163, `quota_lines()` at 291): shows either `loading…`, `no usage endpoint`, error message, or quota bars:
   - Plan name (e.g. "plan: lite")
   - Each `UsageLimit`: label, percentage ("57% used"), optional detail ("$2.33 spent"), and human-readable reset time (relative like "in 3 hr 36 min" if <1 day, weekday+time if <1 week, date+time otherwise).

3. **Per-model breakdown** (line 166-202): sorted by total tokens descending. Table with columns: `model`, `in`, `out`, `cache`, `total`, `cost`. For each model it looks up pricing via `pricing_for()` (line 130) — checks the current model first, then tries `Model::from_spec`.

### 6. Data Flow Summary

```
Agent turn completes
  → TurnCompleteEvent { usage: TokenUsage, model: String }
  → UI handles at app/mod.rs:1039
    → session.meta.usage_by_model[model] += StoredTokenUsage::from(usage)
    → session.token_usage (legacy aggregate) also updated
  → On save, JSONL Meta record serializes usage_by_model
  → On /usage open, UsageModalContext gathers:
      - total (session.token_usage)
      - by_model (session.meta.usage_by_model)
      - quota (async fetch via Provider::fetch_usage())
```

### 7. Quota Fetch Lifecycle

The `UsageFetchState` enum (`usage_modal.rs:34-38`) has `Loading`, `Ready(ProviderUsage)`, `Unsupported`, `Error`. The event loop triggers the fetch asynchronously and stores the result; the modal reads it each render frame via `ctx.quota: Option<&UsageFetchState>`.

197:             "agent run started"
198:         );

201: 
202:         if matches!(result, Err(AgentError::Cancelled)) {
203:             sanitize_cancelled_history(self.history, self.rollback_len);
204:         }

209:     async fn run_loop(&mut self) -> Result<(), AgentError> {
210:         loop {
211:             if let Some(max) = self.config.max_turns
212:                 && self.num_turns >= max
213:             {
214:                 self.emit_done(None)?;
215:                 return Ok(());
216:             }
217:             match self.turn().await? {
218:                 TurnOutcome::Continue => {}
219:                 TurnOutcome::Done(stop_reason) => {
220:                     self.emit_done(stop_reason)?;
221:                     return Ok(());
222:                 }
223:             }
224:         }
225:     }

227:     async fn turn(&mut self) -> Result<TurnOutcome, AgentError> {
228:         if self.cancel.is_cancelled() {
229:             return Err(AgentError::Cancelled);
230:         }
231:         let response = match stream_with_retry(
232:             &*self.provider,

234:             self.history.as_slice(),
235:             &self.system,
236:             &self.tools,
237:             &self.event_tx,
238:             &self.cancel,
239:             self.opts,
240:             self.session_id.as_deref(),
241:         )
242:         .await
243:         {
244:             Ok(r) => {
245:                 self.reauth_attempts = 0;
246:                 r
247:             }
248:             Err(e) if e.is_auth_error() => {
249:                 return self.wait_for_reauth(e).await;
250:             }
251:             Err(e) => {
252:                 error!(error = %e, model = %self.model.id, self.num_turns, "stream_message failed");
253:                 return Err(e);
254:             }
255:         };
256:         self.num_turns += 1;
257: 
258:         let has_tools = response.message.has_tool_calls();
259:         let stop_reason = response.stop_reason;
260:         info!(
261:             input_tokens = response.usage.input,
262:             output_tokens = response.usage.output,
263:             cache_creation = response.usage.cache_creation,
264:             cache_read = response.usage.cache_read,
265:             has_tools,
266:             self.num_turns,
267:             model = %self.model.id,
268:             stop_reason = stop_reason.map_or("none", Into::into),
269:             "API response received"
270:         );
271: 
272:         self.emit_turn_complete(&response)?;
273:         let usage = response.usage;
274:         self.total_usage += usage;
275:         self.context_size = usage.total_input();
276: 
277:         if has_tools {
278:             let history_len_before = self.history.len();
279:             self.process_tool_calls(response).await?;
