295:                     ..Default::default()
296:                 });
297:                 self.history.push(Message::synthetic(NUDGE_PROMPT.into()));
298:                 return Ok(TurnOutcome::Continue);
299:             }
300: 
301:             self.history.push(response.message);
302: 
303:             if stop_reason == Some(StopReason::MaxTokens)
304:                 && self.num_turns <= self.config.max_continuation_turns
305:             {
306:                 warn!(
307:                     self.num_turns,
308:                     "response truncated (max_tokens), re-prompting"
309:                 );
310:                 return Ok(TurnOutcome::Continue);
311:             }
312:         }
313: 
314:         if self.try_auto_compact().await? || self.handle_queued_command().await? {
315:             return Ok(TurnOutcome::Continue);
316:         }
317: 
318:         if has_tools {
319:             Ok(TurnOutcome::Continue)
320:         } else {
321:             Ok(TurnOutcome::Done(stop_reason))
322:         }
323:     }
324: 
325:     async fn wait_for_reauth(&mut self, err: AgentError) -> Result<TurnOutcome, AgentError> {
326:         if self.reauth_attempts >= MAX_REAUTH_ATTEMPTS {
327:             error!(error = %err, attempts = self.reauth_attempts, "max re-auth attempts reached");
328:             return Err(err);
329:         }
330:         let Some(rx) = &self.user_response_rx else {
331:             error!(error = %err, model = %self.model.id, self.num_turns, "stream_message failed");
332:             return Err(err);
333:         };
334:         self.reauth_attempts += 1;
335:         warn!(error = %err, attempt = self.reauth_attempts, "auth error, waiting for re-authentication");
336:         self.event_tx.send(AgentEvent::AuthRequired)?;
337:         let rx = rx.lock().await;
338:         match futures_lite::future::race(rx.recv_async(), async {
339:             self.cancel.cancelled().await;
340:             Err(flume::RecvError::Disconnected)
341:         })
342:         .await
343:         {
344:             Ok(_) => {
345:                 self.provider.refresh_auth().await?;
346:                 Ok(TurnOutcome::Continue)
347:             }
348:             Err(_) => Err(AgentError::Cancelled),
349:         }
350:     }
351: 
352:     fn emit_turn_complete(&self, response: &StreamResponse) -> Result<(), AgentError> {
353:         self.event_tx
354:             .send(AgentEvent::TurnComplete(Box::new(TurnCompleteEvent {
355:                 message: response.message.clone(),
356:                 usage: response.usage,
357:                 model: self.model.id.clone(),
358:                 context_size: Some(response.usage.context_tokens()),
359:             })))
360:     }
361: 
362:     fn emit_done(&self, stop_reason: Option<StopReason>) -> Result<(), AgentError> {
363:         info!(
364:             self.num_turns,
365:             total_input = self.total_usage.input,
366:             total_output = self.total_usage.output,
367:             "agent run completed"
368:         );
369:         self.event_tx.send(AgentEvent::Done {
370:             usage: self.total_usage,
371:             num_turns: self.num_turns,
372:             stop_reason,
373:         })
374:     }
375: 
376:     async fn process_tool_calls(&mut self, response: StreamResponse) -> Result<(), AgentError> {
377:         self.post_tool_empty_retried = false;
378:         let ctx = self.tool_context();
379:         tool_dispatch::process_tool_calls(
380:             response,
381:             &mut self.recent_calls,
382:             self.mcp.as_ref(),
383:             self.history,
384:             &self.event_tx,
385:             &ctx,
386:         )
387:         .await
388:     }
389: 
390:     fn tool_context(&self) -> ToolContext {
391:         ToolContext {
392:             provider: Arc::clone(&self.provider),
393:             model: Arc::clone(&self.model),
394:             event_tx: self.event_tx.clone(),
395:             mode: self.mode.clone(),
396:             tool_use_id: None,
397:             user_response_rx: self.user_response_rx.clone(),
398:             loaded_instructions: self.loaded_instructions.clone(),
399:             cancel: self.cancel.clone(),
400:             mcp: self.mcp.clone(),
401:             deadline: Deadline::None,
402:             config: self.config.clone(),
403:             tool_output_lines: self.tool_output_lines,
404:             permissions: Arc::clone(&self.permissions),
405:             timeouts: self.timeouts,
406:             file_tracker: Arc::clone(&self.file_tracker),
407:             prompt_slots: Arc::clone(&self.prompt_slots),
408:             opts: self.opts,
409:             subagent_cancels: Arc::clone(&self.subagent_cancels),
410:             registry: Arc::clone(&self.registry),
411:             workflow: self.workflow,
412:             audience: self.audience,
413:             local_tools: Arc::clone(&self.local_tools),
414:             live_sink: None,
415:         }
416:     }
417: 
418:     async fn try_auto_compact(&mut self) -> Result<bool, AgentError> {
419:         if !self.auto_compact
420:             || !compaction::is_overflow(
421:                 &TokenUsage {
422:                     input: self.context_size,
423:                     ..Default::default()
424:                 },
425:                 &self.model,
426:                 self.config.compaction_buffer,
427:             )
428:         {
429:             return Ok(false);
430:         }
431:         info!(context_size = self.context_size, "auto-compacting");
432:         self.event_tx.send(AgentEvent::AutoCompacting)?;
433:         self.do_compact().await?;
434:         Ok(true)
435:     }
436: 
437:     async fn do_compact(&mut self) -> Result<(), AgentError> {
438:         let (compact_provider, compact_model) =
439:             resolve_compaction_model(&self.provider, &self.model, self.timeouts);
440:         self.total_usage += compaction::compact_history(
441:             &*compact_provider,
442:             &compact_model,
443:             self.history,
444:             &self.event_tx,
445:             &self.cancel,
446:         )
447:         .await?;
448:         self.rollback_len = self.history.len();
449:         self.history
450:             .push(Message::synthetic(CONTINUE_AFTER_COMPACT.into()));
451:         Ok(())
452:     }
453: 
454:     async fn handle_queued_command(&mut self) -> Result<bool, AgentError> {
455:         let Some(ref source) = self.interrupt_source else {
456:             return Ok(false);
457:         };
458:         let Some(cmd) = source.poll() else {
459:             return Ok(false);
460:         };
461:         match cmd {
462:             ExtractedCommand::Interrupt(mut input, _) => {
463:                 self.event_tx.send(AgentEvent::QueueItemConsumed {
464:                     text: input.message.clone(),
465:                     image_count: input.images.len(),
466:                 })?;
467:                 for msg in std::mem::take(&mut input.preamble) {
468:                     self.history.push(msg);
469:                 }
470:                 self.mode = input.mode.clone();
471:                 let display = input.message.clone();
472:                 let wrapped = format!(
473:                     "<user-interrupt>\nThe user sent a new message while you were working. Address it and continue.\n\n{display}\n</user-interrupt>"
474:                 );
475:                 self.history.push(Message::user_display(wrapped, display));
476:             }
477:             ExtractedCommand::Compact(_) => {
478:                 self.do_compact().await?;
479:             }
480:         }
481:         Ok(true)
482:     }
483: }
484: 
485: const CHARS_PER_TOKEN: usize = 4;
486: 
487: pub fn estimate_message_tokens(messages: &[Message]) -> u32 {
488:     if messages.is_empty() {
489:         return 0;
490:     }
491:     let total_bytes: usize = messages
492:         .iter()
493:         .flat_map(|m| &m.content)
494:         .filter_map(|b| match b {
495:             ContentBlock::Text { text } => Some(text.len()),
496:             ContentBlock::ToolResult { content, .. } => Some(content.len()),
497:             ContentBlock::ToolUse { input, .. } => Some(input.to_string().len()),
498:             _ => None,
499:         })
500:         .sum();
501:     (total_bytes.max(CHARS_PER_TOKEN) / CHARS_PER_TOKEN) as u32
502: }

739:     fn interrupt_handling(queued: Option<bool>, expect_consumed: bool, expect_injected: bool) {
740:         smol::block_on(async {

745:                 )]))
746:             } else {

748:             };
749: 
750:             let tool_use = queued.unwrap_or(true);
751:             let responses = if tool_use {
752:                 vec![
753:                     tool_call_response("glob", "t1"),
754:                     text_response(StopReason::EndTurn),
755:                 ]
756:             } else {
757:                 vec![

761:             };
762: 
763:             let mut history = History::new(Vec::new());
764:             let (mut agent, event_rx) = make_agent(MockProvider::new(responses), &mut history);
765:             if let Some(s) = source {
766:                 agent = agent.with_interrupt_source(s);
767:             }
768:             let _ = agent.run(default_input()).await;
769:             let events = drain_events(&event_rx);
770: 
771:             assert_eq!(
772:                 has_event(&events, |e| matches!(
773:                     e,
774:                     AgentEvent::QueueItemConsumed { .. }
775:                 )),
776:                 expect_consumed,
777:             );
778:             assert_eq!(
779:                 has_interrupt_in_history(history.as_slice()),
780:                 expect_injected

921:         smol::block_on(async {
922:             let mut history = History::new(Vec::new());
923:             let (mut agent, event_rx) = make_agent(MockProvider::new(responses), &mut history);
924:             let _ = agent.run(default_input()).await;
925:             drop(agent);
926:             let events = drain_events(&event_rx);
927: 
928:             assert!(has_event(&events, |e| matches!(
929:                 e,
930:                 AgentEvent::ToolDone(done) if done.is_error && done.id == expected_error_id
931:             )));
932:         });
933:     }
934: 
935:     #[test_case(
936:         vec![
937:             tool_call_response("glob", "t1"),
938:             empty_response(),
939:             text_response(StopReason::EndTurn),
940:         ],
941:         3, true
942:         ; "nudge_on_empty_after_tools"
943:     )]
944:     #[test_case(
945:         vec![
946:             tool_call_response("glob", "t1"),
947:             text_response(StopReason::EndTurn),
948:         ],
949:         2, false
950:         ; "no_nudge_when_text_after_tools"
951:     )]
952:     #[test_case(

954:             empty_response(),
955:             text_response(StopReason::EndTurn),
956:         ],
957:         1, false
958:         ; "no_nudge_without_recent_tools"
959:     )]
960:     fn nudge_behavior(responses: Vec<StreamResponse>, expected_turns: u32, expect_nudge: bool) {
961:         smol::block_on(async {
962:             let mut history = History::new(Vec::new());
963:             let (mut agent, event_rx) = make_agent(MockProvider::new(responses), &mut history);
964:             let _ = agent.run(default_input()).await;
965:             drop(agent);
966:             let events = drain_events(&event_rx);
967: 
968:             assert_eq!(
969:                 has_event(&events, |e| matches!(e, AgentEvent::Nudge)),
970:                 expect_nudge,
971:             );
972:             let done = events
973:                 .iter()
974:                 .find_map(|e| match &e.event {
975:                     AgentEvent::Done { num_turns, .. } => Some(*num_turns),
976:                     _ => None,
977:                 })
978:                 .expect("expected Done event");
979:             assert_eq!(done, expected_turns);
980:         });

24: Subagent types (set via `subagent_type`):

72: local function bounded_errors(errors)
73:   local out = {}

101:   end

103:   local audience = subagent_type == "research" and "research_sub" or "general_sub"
104:   local prompt_id = subagent_type == "research" and "research" or "general"

131:           if errs then
132:             last_errors = bounded_errors(errs)

134:           end
135:           captured = value
136:           return STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_ACK
137:         end,
138:       },
139:     }
140:   end
141: 
142:   -- Process-wide cap on concurrent subagents, sized from config on first use.
143:   if not semaphore then
144:     semaphore = maki.async.semaphore(math.max(ctx:config("task_max_concurrent", 1), 1))
145:   end
146:   local permit = semaphore:acquire()
147: 
148:   -- pcall so a raised error cannot leak the permit.
149:   local ok, out = pcall(function()

151:       model_spec = model.spec,
152:       system = system,

174:     sess:close()
175: 
176:     if err then

178:     end
179:     if validator and not captured then
180:       local msg = last_errors and (STRUCTURED_INVALID_ERROR .. ":\n" .. last_errors) or STRUCTURED_MISSING_ERROR
181:       return { llm_output = msg, is_error = true }
182:     end
183:     return { llm_output = captured and maki.json.encode(captured) or result.text, format = "markdown" }
184:   end)
185: 
186:   permit:release()
187:   if not ok then
188:     error(out, 0)
189:   end
190:   return out
191: end

23: const DOOM_LOOP_THRESHOLD: usize = 3;
24: const DOOM_LOOP_MESSAGE: &str = "You have called this tool with identical input 3 times in a row. You are stuck in a loop. Break out and try a different approach.";
25: const MCP_BLOCKED_IN_PLAN: &str = "MCP tools are not available in plan mode";

28: pub(super) struct RecentCalls(VecDeque<(String, u64)>);
29: 
30: impl RecentCalls {
31:     pub(super) fn new() -> Self {
32:         Self(VecDeque::new())
33:     }
34: 
35:     fn hash_input(input: &Value) -> u64 {
36:         let mut h = DefaultHasher::new();
37:         input.to_string().hash(&mut h);
38:         h.finish()
39:     }
40: 
41:     fn is_doom_loop(&self, name: &str, input: &Value) -> bool {
42:         let hash = Self::hash_input(input);
43:         self.0.len() >= DOOM_LOOP_THRESHOLD - 1
44:             && self
45:                 .0
46:                 .iter()
47:                 .rev()
48:                 .take(DOOM_LOOP_THRESHOLD - 1)
49:                 .all(|(n, h)| n == name && *h == hash)
50:     }
51: 
52:     fn record(&mut self, name: String, input: &Value) {
53:         self.0.push_back((name, Self::hash_input(input)));
54:         if self.0.len() > DOOM_LOOP_THRESHOLD {
55:             self.0.pop_front();
56:         }
57:     }
58: }

60: /// Parse errors and unknown tools skip the start event so the UI never
61: /// shows a phantom spinner.
62: pub async fn run(
63:     registry: &ToolRegistry,
64:     mcp: Option<&McpHandle>,
65:     id: String,
66:     name: &str,
67:     input: &Value,
68:     ctx: &ToolContext,
69:     emit: Emit,
70: ) -> ToolDoneEvent {
71:     if let Some(local) = ctx.local_tools.get(name) {
72:         return run_local_tool(local, id, name, input, ctx, emit);
73:     }
74:     let entry = registry.get(name);
75:     // LLM providers send tool names in wire format (server__tool) but our
76:     // internal index uses server.tool. Only convert if the name isn't a
77:     // native tool — avoids mangling native names that happen to contain __.
78:     let mcp_name;
79:     let mcp_lookup = if entry.is_none() && name.contains("__") && mcp.is_some() {
80:         mcp_name = crate::mcp::internal_tool_name(name);
81:         mcp_name.as_str()
82:     } else {
83:         name
84:     };
85:     let tool_id: Arc<str> = entry
86:         .as_ref()
87:         .map(|e| Arc::from(e.tool.name()))
88:         .or_else(|| mcp.map(|m| m.interned_name(mcp_lookup)))
89:         .unwrap_or_else(|| Arc::from(UNKNOWN_MCP));
90:     let started = Instant::now();
91: 
92:     let done_error = |msg: String| ToolDoneEvent {
93:         id: id.clone(),
94:         tool: Arc::clone(&tool_id),
95:         output: ToolOutput::Plain(msg.into()),
96:         is_error: true,
97:         annotation: None,
98:         written_path: None,
99:     };
100: 
101:     if let Some(entry) = entry {
102:         let invocation = match entry.tool.parse(input) {
103:             Ok(inv) => inv,
104:             Err(e) => {
105:                 warn!(
106:                     tool = %name,
107:                     source = %entry.source.as_log_field(),
108:                     input_preview = %crate::tools::schema::preview(&input.to_string()),
109:                     error = %e,
110:                     "tool input parse failed"
111:                 );
112:                 return done_error(e.to_string());
113:             }
114:         };
115: 
116:         if let Some(target) = invocation.mutable_path() {
117:             let is_plan_target = ctx.mode.plan_path().is_some_and(|pp| target == pp);
118:             if !is_plan_target {
119:                 if ctx.mode.plan_path().is_some() {
120:                     warn!(
121:                         tool = %name,
122:                         target = %target.display(),
123:                         "blocked write in plan mode"
124:                     );
125:                     return done_error(crate::tools::PLAN_WRITE_RESTRICTED.into());
126:                 }
127:                 if let Some(reason) = ctx.permissions.boundary_block_reason(target) {
128:                     return done_error(reason);
129:                 }
130:             }
131:         }
132: 
133:         let header_result = invocation.start_header().await;
134:         let start = ToolStartEvent {
135:             id: id.clone(),
136:             tool: Arc::clone(&tool_id),
137:             summary: header_result.text(),
138:             render_header: header_result.snapshot(),
139:             annotation: invocation.start_annotation(),
140:             input: None,
141:             raw_input: Some(input.clone()),
142:             output: invocation.start_output(ctx),
143:         };
144:         if matches!(emit, Emit::Notify) {
145:             let _ = ctx.event_tx.send(AgentEvent::ToolStart(Box::new(start)));
146:         }
147: 
148:         invocation.start(ctx).await;
149: 
150:         if let Err(e) = enforce_permission(invocation.as_ref(), name, ctx, &id).await {
151:             return done_error(e);
152:         }
153: 
154:         let result = invocation.execute(ctx).await;
155: 
156:         let elapsed = started.elapsed();
157:         match result.output {
158:             Ok(output) => {
159:                 debug!(
160:                     tool = %name,
161:                     source = %entry.source.as_log_field(),
162:                     elapsed_ms = elapsed.as_millis() as u64,
163:                     "tool ok"
164:                 );
165:                 ToolDoneEvent {
166:                     id,
167:                     tool: tool_id,
168:                     output,
169:                     is_error: false,
170:                     annotation: result.annotation,
171:                     written_path: result.written_path,
172:                 }
173:             }
174:             Err(message) => {
175:                 warn!(
176:                     tool = %name,
177:                     source = %entry.source.as_log_field(),
178:                     elapsed_ms = elapsed.as_millis() as u64,
179:                     error = %message,
180:                     "tool failed"
181:                 );
182:                 done_error(message)
183:             }
184:         }
185:     } else if mcp.is_some_and(|m| m.has_tool(mcp_lookup)) {
186:         // MCP tools skip parsing, so we assemble the start event manually.
187:         let start = ToolStartEvent {
188:             id: id.clone(),
189:             tool: Arc::clone(&tool_id),
190:             summary: format!("mcp: {mcp_lookup}"),
191:             render_header: None,
192:             annotation: None,
193:             input: None,
194:             raw_input: Some(input.clone()),
195:             output: None,
196:         };
197:         if matches!(emit, Emit::Notify) {
198:             let _ = ctx.event_tx.send(AgentEvent::ToolStart(Box::new(start)));
199:         }
200:         execute_mcp_tool(ctx, &id, tool_id, mcp_lookup, input).await
201:     } else {
202:         let msg = format!("{UNKNOWN_TOOL_PREFIX}: {mcp_lookup}");
203:         warn!(tool = %mcp_lookup, "unknown tool");
204:         done_error(msg)
205:     }
206: }

208: fn run_local_tool(
209:     local: &LocalToolFn,
210:     id: String,
211:     name: &str,
212:     input: &Value,
213:     ctx: &ToolContext,
214:     emit: Emit,
215: ) -> ToolDoneEvent {
216:     let tool_id: Arc<str> = Arc::from(name);
217:     if matches!(emit, Emit::Notify) {
218:         let start = ToolStartEvent {
219:             id: id.clone(),
220:             tool: Arc::clone(&tool_id),
221:             summary: name.to_owned(),
222:             render_header: None,
223:             annotation: None,
224:             input: None,
225:             raw_input: Some(input.clone()),
226:             output: None,
227:         };
228:         let _ = ctx.event_tx.send(AgentEvent::ToolStart(Box::new(start)));
229:     }
230:     let (output, is_error) = match local(input) {
231:         Ok(output) => (output, false),
232:         Err(e) => {
233:             warn!(tool = %name, error = %e, "local tool failed");
234:             (e, true)
235:         }
236:     };
237:     ToolDoneEvent {
238:         id,
239:         tool: tool_id,
240:         output: ToolOutput::Plain(output.into()),
241:         is_error,
242:         annotation: None,
243:         written_path: None,
244:     }
245: }

247: /// Enforce permission for a native tool. MCP tools bypass this — they go
248: /// through `execute_mcp_tool` which handles permission checking internally.
249: ///
250: /// Returns an error if `name` contains dots (not a valid native tool name).
251: async fn enforce_permission(
252:     inv: &dyn ToolInvocation,
253:     name: &str,
254:     ctx: &ToolContext,
255:     id: &str,
256: ) -> Result<(), String> {
257:     if name.contains('.') {
258:         return Err(format!(
259:             "enforce_permission called with dotted name: {name}"
260:         ));
261:     }
262:     if let Some(scopes) = inv.permission_scopes().await {
263:         let tool_key = ToolKey::native(name);
264:         ctx.permissions
265:             .enforce(
266:                 &tool_key,
267:                 &scopes,
268:                 &ctx.event_tx,
269:                 ctx.user_response_rx.as_deref(),
270:                 id,
271:                 &ctx.cancel,
272:                 ctx.mode.plan_path(),
273:             )
274:             .await
275:             .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
276:     }
277:     Ok(())
278: }
279: 
280: async fn execute_mcp_tool(
281:     ctx: &ToolContext,
282:     id: &str,
283:     tool_id: Arc<str>,
284:     tool_name: &str,
285:     input: &Value,
286: ) -> ToolDoneEvent {
287:     let done = |output: String, is_error: bool| ToolDoneEvent {
288:         id: id.to_owned(),
289:         tool: Arc::clone(&tool_id),
290:         output: ToolOutput::Plain(output.into()),
291:         is_error,
292:         annotation: None,
293:         written_path: None,
294:     };
295: 
296:     if ctx.mode.plan_path().is_some() {
297:         return done(MCP_BLOCKED_IN_PLAN.into(), true);
298:     }
299: 
300:     let perm_tool = match ToolKey::parse(tool_name) {
301:         Ok(k) => k,
302:         Err(e) => {
303:             return done(format!("invalid MCP tool key '{tool_name}': {e}"), true);
304:         }
305:     };
306:     let perm_scope = {
307:         let json = input.to_string();
308:         if json.len() > 200 {
309:             format!("{}\u{2026}", &json[..200])
310:         } else {
311:             json
312:         }
313:     };
314:     let perm_scopes = crate::tools::PermissionScopes::single(perm_scope);
315: 
316:     if let Err(e) = ctx
317:         .permissions
318:         .enforce(
319:             &perm_tool,
320:             &perm_scopes,
321:             &ctx.event_tx,
322:             ctx.user_response_rx.as_deref(),
323:             id,
324:             &ctx.cancel,
325:             ctx.mode.plan_path(),
326:         )
327:         .await
328:     {
329:         return done(e.to_string(), true);
330:     }
331: 
332:     let Some(mcp) = &ctx.mcp else {
333:         return done(format!("MCP manager not available for {tool_name}"), true);
334:     };
335: 
336:     match mcp.call_tool(tool_name, input).await {
337:         Ok(text) => done(text, false),
338:         Err(e) => done(e.to_string(), true),
339:     }
340: }

342: /// Deduplicates doom-loop repeats, then runs remaining calls in parallel.
343: pub(super) async fn process_tool_calls(
344:     response: maki_providers::StreamResponse,
345:     recent_calls: &mut RecentCalls,
346:     mcp: Option<&McpHandle>,
347:     history: &mut super::history::History,
348:     event_tx: &crate::EventSender,
349:     ctx: &ToolContext,
350: ) -> Result<(), AgentError> {
351:     let tool_uses: Vec<(String, String, Value)> = response
352:         .message
353:         .tool_uses()
354:         .map(|(id, name, input)| (id.to_owned(), name.to_owned(), input.clone()))
355:         .collect();
356: 
357:     history.push(response.message);
358: 
359:     let mut immediate_errors: Vec<ToolDoneEvent> = Vec::new();
360:     let mut runnable: Vec<(String, String, Value)> = Vec::new();
361: 
362:     for (id, name, input) in tool_uses {
363:         debug!(
364:             tool = %name,
365:             id = %id,
366:             input_preview = %crate::tools::schema::preview(&input.to_string()),
367:             "parsing tool call"
368:         );
369:         if recent_calls.is_doom_loop(&name, &input) {
370:             warn!(tool = %name, "doom loop detected, skipping execution");
371:             immediate_errors.push(ToolDoneEvent::error(id.clone(), DOOM_LOOP_MESSAGE));
372:         } else {
373:             runnable.push((id, name.clone(), input.clone()));
374:         }
375:         recent_calls.record(name, &input);
376:     }
377: 
378:     for err in &immediate_errors {
379:         event_tx.try_send(AgentEvent::ToolDone(Box::new(err.clone())));
380:     }
381: 
382:     let mut set = TaskSet::new();
383:     let mut spawned_ids: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
384:     for (id, name, input) in runnable {
385:         spawned_ids.push(id.clone());
386:         let event_tx_clone = ctx.event_tx.clone();
387:         let tool_ctx = ToolContext {
388:             tool_use_id: Some(id.clone()),
389:             ..ctx.clone()
390:         };
391:         let mcp_owned = mcp.cloned();
392:         set.spawn(async move {
393:             let done = run(
394:                 &tool_ctx.registry,
395:                 mcp_owned.as_ref(),
396:                 id,
397:                 &name,
398:                 &input,
399:                 &tool_ctx,
400:                 Emit::Notify,
401:             )
402:             .await;
403:             event_tx_clone.try_send(AgentEvent::ToolDone(Box::new(done.clone())));
404:             done
405:         });
406:     }
407: 
408:     let results: Vec<ToolDoneEvent> = set
409:         .join_all()
410:         .await
411:         .into_iter()
412:         .zip(spawned_ids)
413:         .map(|(r, id)| match r {
414:             Ok(out) => out,
415:             Err(e) => {
416:                 error!(error = %e, "tool task panicked");
417:                 ToolDoneEvent::error(id, format!("internal error: tool panicked: {e}"))
418:             }
419:         })
420:         .collect();
421: 
422:     let mut all_results = results;
423:     all_results.extend(immediate_errors);
424:     let tool_msg = crate::types::tool_results(all_results);
425:     event_tx.send(AgentEvent::ToolResultsSubmitted {
426:         message: Box::new(tool_msg.clone()),
427:     })?;
428:     history.push(tool_msg);
429:     Ok(())
430: }

93: pub enum PermissionAnswer {

104: impl PermissionAnswer {
105:     pub fn is_allow(&self) -> bool {
106:         matches!(
107:             self,
108:             Self::AllowOnce | Self::AllowSession | Self::AllowAlwaysLocal | Self::AllowAlwaysGlobal
109:         )
110:     }
111: 
112:     pub fn encode(&self) -> String {
113:         match self {
114:             Self::AllowOnce => "allow".to_string(),
115:             Self::AllowSession => "allow_session".to_string(),
116:             Self::AllowAlwaysLocal => "allow_always_local".to_string(),
117:             Self::AllowAlwaysGlobal => "allow_always_global".to_string(),
118:             Self::Deny => "deny".to_string(),
119:             Self::DenyWithGuidance(g) => format!("deny:{g}"),
120:             Self::DenyAlwaysLocal => "deny_always_local".to_string(),
121:             Self::DenyAlwaysGlobal => "deny_always_global".to_string(),
122:         }
123:     }
124: 
125:     pub fn decode(s: &str) -> Option<Self> {
126:         match s {
127:             "allow" => Some(Self::AllowOnce),
128:             "allow_session" => Some(Self::AllowSession),
129:             "allow_always_local" => Some(Self::AllowAlwaysLocal),
130:             "allow_always_global" => Some(Self::AllowAlwaysGlobal),
131:             "deny" => Some(Self::Deny),
132:             "deny_always_local" => Some(Self::DenyAlwaysLocal),
133:             "deny_always_global" => Some(Self::DenyAlwaysGlobal),
134:             _ if s.starts_with("deny:") => {
135:                 let guidance = s.strip_prefix("deny:").unwrap();
136:                 if guidance.is_empty() {
137:                     Some(Self::Deny)
138:                 } else {
139:                     Some(Self::DenyWithGuidance(guidance.to_string()))
140:                 }
141:             }
142:             _ => None,
143:         }
144:     }
145: 
146:     pub fn guidance(&self) -> Option<&str> {
147:         match self {
148:             Self::DenyWithGuidance(g) => Some(g),
149:             _ => None,
150:         }
151:     }
152: }

154: pub struct PermissionManager {
155:     session_rules: Mutex<Vec<PermissionRule>>,
156:     config_rules: Vec<PermissionRule>,
157:     builtin_rules: Vec<PermissionRule>,
158:     yolo: AtomicBool,
159:     default: DefaultEffect,
160:     tool_defaults: HashMap<ToolKey, DefaultEffect>,
161:     cwd: PathBuf,
162: }
163: 
164: impl PermissionManager {
165:     pub fn new(config: PermissionsConfig, cwd: PathBuf) -> Self {
166:         let config_rules = config.rules;
167:         let builtin_rules = builtin_rules(&cwd);
168: 
169:         // Warn if wildcard deny is present — it blocks ALL tools including builtins.
170:         let has_wildcard_deny = config_rules
171:             .iter()
172:             .any(|r| matches!(r.tool, ToolKey::Wildcard) && r.effect == Effect::Deny);
173:         if has_wildcard_deny {
174:             warn!(
175:                 "wildcard deny detected — this blocks ALL tools including \
176:                  builtins (write/edit/multiedit/task). Use per-tool rules \
177:                  instead if you want selective access."
178:             );
179:         }
180:         // Warn if wildcard allow is present — it permits ALL tools including write/edit/task.
181:         let has_wildcard_allow = config_rules
182:             .iter()
183:             .any(|r| matches!(r.tool, ToolKey::Wildcard) && r.effect == Effect::Allow);
184:         if has_wildcard_allow {
185:             warn!(
186:                 "wildcard allow detected — this permits ALL tools including \
187:                  write/edit/multiedit/task. Use per-tool rules \
188:                  instead if you want selective access."
189:             );
190:         }
191: 
192:         Self {
193:             builtin_rules,
194:             session_rules: Mutex::new(Vec::new()),
195:             config_rules,
196:             yolo: AtomicBool::new(config.yolo),
197:             default: config.default,
198:             tool_defaults: config.tool_defaults,
199:             cwd,
200:         }
201:     }
202: 
203:     fn session_rules(&self) -> std::sync::MutexGuard<'_, Vec<PermissionRule>> {
204:         self.session_rules.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| {
205:             warn!("permission mutex was poisoned, recovering");
206:             e.into_inner()
207:         })
208:     }
209: 
210:     fn check_inner(
211:         &self,
212:         tool: &ToolKey,
213:         scopes: &[&str],
214:         force_prompt: bool,
215:         plan_path: Option<&Path>,
216:     ) -> PermissionCheck {
217:         let session = self.session_rules();
218: 
219:         // Any matching deny wins. No specificity hierarchy — a Wildcard
220:         // deny blocks everything, a tool-specific deny blocks that tool.
221:         let mut unclaimed_scopes: Vec<&str> = if force_prompt {
222:             Vec::new()
223:         } else {
224:             Vec::with_capacity(scopes.len())
225:         };
226: 
227:         for scope in scopes {
228:             let mut has_allow = false;
229:             for r in session
230:                 .iter()
231:                 .chain(&self.config_rules)
232:                 .chain(&self.builtin_rules)
233:             {
234:                 if !matches_rule(&r.tool, tool) || !rule_matches_scope(r, scope) {
235:                     continue;
236:                 }
237:                 match r.effect {
238:                     Effect::Deny => {
239:                         info!(tool = %tool, scope = %scope, "permission denied");
240:                         return PermissionCheck::Denied;
241:                     }
242:                     Effect::Allow => {
243:                         has_allow = true;
244:                     }
245:                 }
246:             }
247: 
248:             if has_allow {
249:                 // allow wins for this scope (no deny matched)
250:             } else if !force_prompt {
251:                 unclaimed_scopes.push(scope);
252:             }
253:             // force_prompt: all scopes will be prompted anyway
254:         }
255: 
256:         if self.yolo.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
257:             return PermissionCheck::Allowed;
258:         }
259: 
260:         let pending: Vec<&str> = if force_prompt {
261:             scopes.to_vec()
262:         } else {
263:             unclaimed_scopes
264:         };
265: 
266:         if pending.is_empty() {
267:             return PermissionCheck::Allowed;
268:         }
269: 
270:         // Plan file auto-allow: fires AFTER deny rules have been evaluated.
271:         // Only triggers if ALL pending scopes match the plan file path.
272:         // A single non-plan scope means we must prompt for the rest.
273:         if !force_prompt && !pending.is_empty() {
274:             let is_plan_write = plan_path.is_some_and(|pp| {
275:                 matches!(tool, ToolKey::Native(name) if FILE_WRITE_TOOLS.contains(&name.as_ref()))
276:                     && {
277:                         let normalized_plan = normalize_scope_path(&pp.display().to_string());
278:                         pending
279:                             .iter()
280:                             .all(|s| normalize_scope_path(s) == normalized_plan)
281:                     }
282:             });
283:             if is_plan_write {
284:                 return PermissionCheck::Allowed;
285:             }
286:         }
287: 
288:         let eff = self
289:             .tool_defaults
290:             .get(tool)
291:             .copied()
292:             .or_else(|| {
293:                 // McpTool falls back to McpServer-level default (Arc clone, ~2ns)
294:                 let server = match tool {
295:                     ToolKey::McpTool { server, .. } => server,
296:                     _ => return None,
297:                 };
298:                 self.tool_defaults
299:                     .get(&ToolKey::McpServer {
300:                         server: server.clone(),
301:                     })
302:                     .copied()
303:             })
304:             .unwrap_or(self.default);
305:         match eff {
306:             DefaultEffect::Deny => {
307:                 info!(tool = %tool, "denied by default");
308:                 PermissionCheck::Denied
309:             }
310:             DefaultEffect::Allow => PermissionCheck::Allowed,
311:             DefaultEffect::Prompt => PermissionCheck::NeedsPrompt {
312:                 tool: tool.clone(),
313:                 scopes: pending.into_iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect(),
314:                 force_prompt,
315:             },
316:         }
317:     }
318: 
319:     pub fn check(&self, tool: &ToolKey, scope: &str, plan_path: Option<&Path>) -> PermissionCheck {
320:         self.check_inner(tool, &[scope], false, plan_path)
321:     }
322: 
323:     pub fn check_multi(
324:         &self,
325:         tool: &ToolKey,
326:         scopes: &[&str],
327:         force_prompt: bool,
328:         plan_path: Option<&Path>,
329:     ) -> PermissionCheck {
330:         self.check_inner(tool, scopes, force_prompt, plan_path)
331:     }

333:     pub fn add_session_rule(&self, rule: PermissionRule) {
334:         let mut rules = self.session_rules();
335:         let exists = rules
336:             .iter()
337:             .any(|r| r.tool == rule.tool && r.scope == rule.scope && r.effect == rule.effect);
338:         if !exists {
339:             rules.push(rule);
340:         }
341:     }

352:     /// Outside-cwd paths are not blocked here. They flow through the normal
353:     /// permission prompt (which uses the same canonicalization via
354:     /// [`scope_matches`]). Only unresolvable boundaries are hard-blocked.
355:     pub fn boundary_block_reason(&self, path: &Path) -> Option<String> {
356:         match physical_boundary_check(&self.cwd, path) {
357:             Some(_) => None,
358:             None => Some(format!(
359:                 "{BOUNDARY_UNVERIFIABLE_PREFIX} {} \
360:                  (project root could not be resolved)",
361:                 path.display()
362:             )),
363:         }
364:     }
365: 
366:     pub fn session_rules_snapshot(&self) -> Vec<PermissionRule> {
367:         self.session_rules().clone()
368:     }
369: 
370:     pub fn load_session_rules(&self, rules: Vec<PermissionRule>) {
371:         *self.session_rules() = rules;
372:     }
373: 
374:     pub fn apply_decision(&self, tool: &ToolKey, scopes: &[String], answer: &PermissionAnswer) {
375:         let resolved = if answer.is_allow() || tool.is_mcp() {
376:             // MCP scopes are always wildcarded — both allow and deny generalize to "*".
377:             // This makes session and persisted rules consistent: a deny on an MCP tool
378:             // blocks the tool entirely, not just the specific input that triggered it.
379:             generalized_scopes(tool, scopes)
380:         } else {
381:             scopes.to_vec()
382:         };
383: 
384:         match answer {
385:             PermissionAnswer::AllowOnce
386:             | PermissionAnswer::Deny
387:             | PermissionAnswer::DenyWithGuidance(_) => {}
388:             PermissionAnswer::AllowSession => {
389:                 for s in &resolved {
390:                     self.add_session_rule(PermissionRule {
391:                         tool: tool.clone(),
392:                         scope: Some(s.clone()),
393:                         effect: Effect::Allow,
394:                     });
395:                 }
396:             }
397:             PermissionAnswer::AllowAlwaysLocal
398:             | PermissionAnswer::AllowAlwaysGlobal
399:             | PermissionAnswer::DenyAlwaysLocal
400:             | PermissionAnswer::DenyAlwaysGlobal => {
401:                 let effect = if answer.is_allow() {
402:                     Effect::Allow
403:                 } else {
404:                     Effect::Deny
405:                 };
406:                 let target = match answer {
407:                     PermissionAnswer::AllowAlwaysLocal | PermissionAnswer::DenyAlwaysLocal => {
408:                         PermissionTarget::Project(self.cwd.clone())
409:                     }
410:                     _ => PermissionTarget::Global,
411:                 };
412:                 for s in &resolved {
413:                     self.add_session_rule(PermissionRule {
414:                         tool: tool.clone(),
415:                         scope: Some(s.clone()),
416:                         effect,
417:                     });
418:                     if let Err(e) = append_permission_rule(tool, Some(s), effect, &target) {
419:                         tracing::warn!(error = %e, "failed to persist permission rule");
420:                     }
421:                 }
422:             }
423:         }
424:     }

433:         request_id: &str,
434:         cancel: &crate::CancelToken,
435:         plan_path: Option<&Path>,
436:     ) -> Result<(), PermissionError> {
437:         let scope_refs: Vec<&str> = scopes.scopes.iter().map(|s| s.as_str()).collect();
438:         let tool_string = tool.to_string();
439:         let scope_display = || scopes.scopes.join("; ");
440:         let deny = |guidance: Option<String>| match guidance {
441:             Some(g) => PermissionError::with_guidance(&tool_string, &scope_display(), g),
442:             None => PermissionError::new(&tool_string, &scope_display()),
443:         };
444: 
445:         let (pt, ps, force_prompt) =
446:             match self.check_inner(tool, &scope_refs, scopes.force_prompt, plan_path) {
447:                 PermissionCheck::Allowed => return Ok(()),
448:                 PermissionCheck::Denied => return Err(deny(None)),
449:                 PermissionCheck::NeedsPrompt {
450:                     tool,
451:                     scopes,
452:                     force_prompt,
453:                 } => (tool, scopes, force_prompt),
454:             };
455: 
456:         let Some(rx) = user_response_rx else {
457:             warn!(tool = %tool, scope = %scope_display(), "no permission response channel");
458:             return Err(deny(None));
459:         };
460: 
461:         let guard = rx.lock().await;
462:         let refs: Vec<&str> = ps.iter().map(|s| s.as_str()).collect();
463:         let (t2, s2) = match self.check_inner(&pt, &refs, force_prompt, plan_path) {
464:             PermissionCheck::Allowed => return Ok(()),
465:             PermissionCheck::Denied => return Err(deny(None)),
466:             PermissionCheck::NeedsPrompt { tool, scopes, .. } => (tool, scopes),
467:         };
468: 
469:         let _ = event_tx.send(AgentEvent::PermissionRequest {
470:             id: request_id.to_owned(),
471:             tool: t2.clone(),
472:             scopes: s2.clone(),
473:         });
474:         let response = cancel.race(guard.recv_async()).await;
475:         drop(guard);
476: 
477:         let answer = match response {
478:             Ok(Ok(a)) => a,
479:             Ok(Err(_)) => {
480:                 warn!(tool = %tool, scope = %scope_display(), "permission channel closed");
481:                 return Err(deny(None));
482:             }
483:             Err(_) => return Err(deny(None)),
484:         };
485: 
486:         let Some(answer) = PermissionAnswer::decode(&answer) else {
487:             return Err(deny(None));
488:         };
489:         self.apply_decision(&t2, &s2, &answer);
490:         if answer.is_allow() {
491:             Ok(())
492:         } else {
493:             Err(deny(answer.guidance().map(String::from)))
494:         }
495:     }
496: }

498: fn matches_rule(rule_key: &ToolKey, actual: &ToolKey) -> bool {
499:     match (rule_key, actual) {
500:         (ToolKey::Wildcard, _) => true,
501:         (ToolKey::Native(a), ToolKey::Native(b)) => a == b,
502:         (ToolKey::McpServer { server: rs }, ToolKey::McpServer { server: as_ }) => rs == as_,
503:         (ToolKey::McpServer { server: rs }, ToolKey::McpTool { server: as_, .. }) => rs == as_,
504:         (
505:             ToolKey::McpTool {
506:                 server: rs,
507:                 tool: rt,
508:             },
509:             ToolKey::McpTool {
510:                 server: as_,
511:                 tool: at,
512:             },
513:         ) => rs == as_ && rt == at,
514:         _ => false,
515:     }
516: }
517: 
518: fn rule_matches_scope(rule: &PermissionRule, scope: &str) -> bool {
519:     match &rule.scope {
520:         None => true,
521:         Some(pattern) => scope_matches(pattern, scope),
522:     }
523: }
524: 
525: /// Glob matcher for permission scopes. The boundary suffixes (`/**`, `" *"`)
526: /// must be tried before the bare `*`, otherwise a plain prefix would swallow
527: /// them. `" *"` is the bash form `<command> *`: it has to match the bare
528: /// command too (`pwd *` covers `pwd` and `pwd -L`, but not `pwdx`).
529: ///
530: /// For the `/**` path pattern, `Path::starts_with` is used to compare
531: /// components rather than characters, which handles both `/` and `\`
532: /// transparently on all platforms.
533: pub fn scope_matches(pattern: &str, value: &str) -> bool {
534:     if pattern == "*" || pattern == "**" {
535:         return true;
536:     }
537:     if let Some(prefix) = pattern.strip_suffix("/**") {
538:         let norm_prefix = maki_storage::paths::canonicalize_clean(Path::new(prefix));
539:         // Use incremental canonicalization for the value so symlinks in
540:         // existing path components are resolved before any `..` traversal.
541:         // `canonicalize_clean` falls back to lexical normalization when the
542:         // file doesn't exist, which breaks scope matching when the project
543:         // dir itself is a symlink.
544:         let norm_value = maki_storage::paths::incremental_canonicalize(Path::new(value))
545:             .unwrap_or_else(|| maki_storage::paths::normalize_path(Path::new(value)));
546:         return norm_value == norm_prefix || norm_value.starts_with(&norm_prefix);
547:     }
548:     if let Some(prefix) = pattern.strip_suffix(" *") {
549:         return value == prefix || value.starts_with(&format!("{prefix} "));
550:     }
551:     if let Some(prefix) = pattern.strip_suffix('*') {
552:         return value.starts_with(prefix);
553:     }
554:     pattern == value
555: }
556: 
557: /// Lexical normalization for scope paths. Resolves `..` and `.` without
558: /// hitting the filesystem and without producing `\\?\` prefixes on Windows.
559: /// Use this for display, logging, and scope matching.
560: ///
561: /// For symlink-aware security checks, use [`physical_boundary_check`].
562: pub fn normalize_scope_path(path: &str) -> String {
563:     let resolved = crate::tools::resolve_path(path).unwrap_or_else(|_| path.to_string());
564:     maki_storage::paths::normalize_path(Path::new(&resolved))
565:         .to_string_lossy()
566:         .into_owned()
567: }
568: 
569: /// Check whether `child` is physically inside `parent`, following symlinks.
570: ///
571: /// Uses incremental left-to-right canonicalization: each component is
572: /// resolved through the filesystem (including symlinks) *before* any
573: /// subsequent `..` component can act on it. This prevents symlink-based
574: /// boundary escapes where a symlink followed by `..` resolves to a
575: /// location outside the parent.
576: ///
577: /// Returns `true` only when the resolved filesystem location of `child`
578: /// is under `parent`. Returns `None` if the parent itself cannot be resolved.
579: pub fn physical_boundary_check(parent: &Path, child: &Path) -> Option<bool> {
580:     let parent_canon = maki_storage::paths::incremental_canonicalize(parent)?;
581:     let child_canon =
582:         maki_storage::paths::incremental_canonicalize(child).unwrap_or_else(|| child.to_path_buf());
583:     Some(child_canon.starts_with(&parent_canon))
584: }
585: 
586: fn generalize_bash_segment(segment: &str) -> String {
587:     let first_token = segment.split_whitespace().next().unwrap_or(segment);
588:     format!("{first_token} *")
589: }
590: 
591: pub fn generalized_scopes(tool: &ToolKey, scopes: &[String]) -> Vec<String> {
592:     let mut seen = HashSet::new();
593:     scopes
594:         .iter()
595:         .map(|s| generalize_scope(tool, s))
596:         .filter(|g| seen.insert(g.clone()))
597:         .collect()
598: }
599: 
600: fn generalize_scope(tool: &ToolKey, scope: &str) -> String {
601:     match tool {
602:         ToolKey::Native(name) if name.as_ref() == "bash" => generalize_bash_segment(scope),
603:         ToolKey::Native(name) if FILE_WRITE_TOOLS.contains(&name.as_ref()) => {
604:             let p = Path::new(scope);
605:             match p.parent() {
606:                 Some(parent) if !parent.as_os_str().is_empty() => {
607:                     format!("{}/**", parent.display())
608:                 }
609:                 _ => "**".to_string(),
610:             }
611:         }
612:         // MCP tool calls have a scope equal to the JSON-stringified input.
613:         // "Allow always" should whitelist the tool regardless of its arguments,
614:         // so generalize the scope to `*`. The rule's `tool` field still gates
615:         // which MCP tool it applies to, keeping distinct tools distinct.
616:         ToolKey::McpTool { .. } | ToolKey::McpServer { .. } => "*".to_string(),
617:         _ => scope.to_string(),
618:     }
619: }

1038:     /// "Allow always" stores a command's generalized scope as a rule, so the
1039:     /// command must match the very rule it would create. When this broke, the
1040:     /// bare `pwd` never matched its own `pwd *` rule and we reprompted forever.

1046:     #[test_case("myfetch.search", "{\"url\":\"https://a\"}" ; "mcp_tool_call")]
1047:     fn command_matches_its_own_generalized_rule(tool: &str, scope: &str) {
1048:         let tool_key = ToolKey::parse(tool).unwrap();
1049:         let rule = &generalized_scopes(&tool_key, &[scope.into()])[0];
1050:         assert!(
1051:             scope_matches(rule, scope),
1052:             "{scope:?} does not match its generalized rule {rule:?}"
1053:         );
1054:     }

1056:     /// "Allow always" on an MCP tool generalizes the stored scope to `*`, so a
1057:     /// later call with different arguments matches the persisted rule instead of
1058:     /// reprompting, while a different MCP tool is still gated by its `tool` name.
1059:     #[test]
1060:     fn mcp_allow_always_matches_any_args_but_stays_per_tool() {
1061:         let mgr = default_mgr();
1062:         mgr.apply_decision(
1063:             &ToolKey::parse("myfetch.search").unwrap(),
1064:             &["{\"url\":\"https://a\"}".into()],
1065:             &PermissionAnswer::AllowSession,
1066:         );
1067:         // Same tool, different arguments -> allowed without reprompting.
1068:         assert!(matches!(
1069:             mgr.check(
1070:                 &ToolKey::parse("myfetch.search").unwrap(),
1071:                 "{\"url\":\"https://b\"}",
1072:                 None
1073:             ),
1074:             PermissionCheck::Allowed
1075:         ));
1076:         // A distinct MCP tool is not covered by the fetch rule.
1077:         assert!(!matches!(
1078:             mgr.check(
1079:                 &ToolKey::parse("myfetch.exec").unwrap(),
1080:                 "{\"cmd\":\"ls\"}",
1081:                 None
1082:             ),
1083:             PermissionCheck::Allowed
1084:         ));
1085:     }

+const UNKNOWN_SUBAGENT_ERR: &str = "unknown subagent type: bogus";
+const SUB_AGENT_ERROR_PREFIX: &str = "sub-agent error: ";
+
+const TASK_TOOL: &str = "task";
+const PROBE_TOOL: &str = "probe";
+const TASK_PROMPT: &str = "do the thing";
+const PLAIN_TEXT: &str = "plain text result";
+const PROMPT_ERR_MSG: &str = "model exploded";
+const RAISE_MSG: &str = "stub prompt kaboom";
+
+const SCENARIO_PLAIN: &str = "plain";
+const SCENARIO_HAPPY: &str = "happy";
+const SCENARIO_INVALID_THEN_VALID: &str = "invalid_then_valid";
+const SCENARIO_NEVER_STRUCTURED: &str = "never_structured";
+const SCENARIO_INVALID_ONLY: &str = "invalid_only";
+const SCENARIO_PROMPT_ERROR: &str = "prompt_error";
+const SCENARIO_RAISE: &str = "raise";
+
+/// Stubs keyed by `opts.name` (the task's `description`). `maki.json` and
+/// `maki.async` stay real so schema validation and semaphore behavior are tested.
+const STUB_PRELUDE: &str = r#"
+recorder = { prompts = {}, closed = 0, sessions = 0, acquired = 0, released = 0 }
+
+-- Spy wrapper: the real semaphore does the work, counters track that every
+-- permit is explicitly released (gc would silently hide a leak).
+local real_semaphore = maki.async.semaphore
+maki.async.semaphore = function(n)
+  recorder.sem_size = n
+  local sem = real_semaphore(n)
+  return {
+    acquire = function(self)
+      local permit = sem:acquire()
+      recorder.acquired = recorder.acquired + 1
+      return {
+        release = function(p)
+          recorder.released = recorder.released + 1
+          return permit:release()
+        end,
+      }
+    end,
+  }
+end
+
+maki.agent.resolve_model = function(ctx, opts)
+  return { spec = "test/model" }
+end
+
+maki.agent.system_prompt = function(ctx, opts)
+  return "sys"
+end
+
+maki.agent.tools = function(ctx, opts)
+  return {}
+end
+
+local behaviors = {}
+
+behaviors.plain = function(sess, msg)
+  return { text = "@PLAIN_TEXT@" }
+end
+
+behaviors.happy = function(sess, msg)
+  local h = sess.opts.local_tools.structured_output.handler
+  recorder.first_ack, recorder.first_err = h({ answer = "42" })
+  return { text = "raw text ignored" }
+end
+
+behaviors.invalid_then_valid = function(sess, msg)
+  local h = sess.opts.local_tools.structured_output.handler
+  recorder.first_ack, recorder.first_err = h({ answer = 42 })
+  recorder.second_ack, recorder.second_err = h({ answer = "42" })
+  return { text = "raw text ignored" }
+end
+
+behaviors.never_structured = function(sess, msg)
+  return { text = "no structured call" }
+end
+
+behaviors.invalid_only = function(sess, msg)
+  local h = sess.opts.local_tools.structured_output.handler
+  recorder.first_ack, recorder.first_err = h({ a = 1, b = 2, c = 3, d = 4 })
+  return { text = "still invalid" }
+end
+
+behaviors.prompt_error = function(sess, msg)
+  return nil, "@PROMPT_ERR@"
+end
+
+behaviors.raise = function(sess, msg)
+  error("@RAISE_MSG@")
+end
+
+maki.agent.session = function(ctx, opts)
+  recorder.sessions = recorder.sessions + 1
+  recorder.has_local_tools = opts.local_tools ~= nil
+  local sess = { opts = opts }
+  function sess:prompt(msg)
+    recorder.prompts[#recorder.prompts + 1] = msg
+    return behaviors[opts.name](self, msg)
+  end
+  function sess:close()
+    recorder.closed = recorder.closed + 1
+  end
+  return sess
+end
+
+maki.api.register_tool({
+  name = "probe",
+  description = "recorder snapshot",
+  schema = { type = "object", properties = {}, additionalProperties = false },
+  audiences = { "main" },
+  handler = function(input, ctx)
+    local snap = {
+      sessions = recorder.sessions,
+      closed = recorder.closed,
+      prompt_count = #recorder.prompts,
+      has_local_tools = recorder.has_local_tools,
+      first_ack = recorder.first_ack,
+      first_err = recorder.first_err,
+      second_ack = recorder.second_ack,
+      second_err = recorder.second_err,
+      task_cap = ctx:config().task_max_concurrent,
+      acquired = recorder.acquired,
+      released = recorder.released,
+      sem_size = recorder.sem_size,
+    }
+    if #recorder.prompts > 0 then
+      snap.prompts = recorder.prompts
+    end
+    return (maki.json.encode(snap))
+  end,
+})
+"#;
+
+fn load_task_host() -> (Arc<ToolRegistry>, PluginHost) {
+    let reg = Arc::new(ToolRegistry::new());
+    let host = PluginHost::new(Arc::clone(&reg)).unwrap();
+    let prelude = STUB_PRELUDE
+        .replace("@PLAIN_TEXT@", PLAIN_TEXT)
+        .replace("@PROMPT_ERR@", PROMPT_ERR_MSG)
+        .replace("@RAISE_MSG@", RAISE_MSG);
+    host.load_source("task_policy", &format!("{prelude}\n{TASK_PLUGIN_SRC}"))
+        .unwrap();
+    (reg, host)
+}
+
+fn exec_tool(reg: &ToolRegistry, name: &str, input: Value) -> Result<String, String> {
+    let entry = reg
+        .get(name)
+        .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("tool {name} not registered"));
+    let inv = entry.tool.parse(&input).expect("parse failed");
+    let ctx = stub_ctx(&AgentMode::Build);
+    smol::block_on(async { inv.execute(&ctx).await })
+        .output
+        .map(|out| match out {
+            ToolOutput::Plain(s) => s.text,
+            other => panic!("unexpected output: {other:?}"),
+        })
+}
+
+fn probe(reg: &ToolRegistry) -> Value {
+    let out = exec_tool(reg, PROBE_TOOL, json!({})).expect("probe failed");
+    serde_json::from_str(&out).expect("probe returned invalid json")
+}
+
+fn task_input(scenario: &str, output_schema: Option<Value>) -> Value {
+    let mut input = json!({ "description": scenario, "prompt": TASK_PROMPT });
+    if let Some(schema) = output_schema {
+        input["output_schema"] = schema;
+    }
+    input
+}
+
+fn answer_schema() -> Value {
+    json!({
+        "type": "object",
+        "properties": { "answer": { "type": "string" } },
+        "required": ["answer"],
+        "additionalProperties": false,
+    })
+}
+
+/// Four wrong-typed properties, one more than MAX_SCHEMA_ERRORS, so
+/// truncation in `bounded_errors` is observable.
+fn multi_error_schema() -> Value {
+    json!({
+        "type": "object",
+        "properties": {
+            "a": { "type": "string" },
+            "b": { "type": "string" },
+            "c": { "type": "string" },
+            "d": { "type": "string" },
+        },
+        "required": ["a", "b", "c", "d"],
+    })
+}
+
+#[test_case::test_case(json!({"subagent_type": "bogus"}), UNKNOWN_SUBAGENT_ERR ; "unknown_subagent_type")]
+#[test_case::test_case(json!({"output_schema": {"type": 42}}), SCHEMA_COMPILE_ERROR ; "invalid_output_schema")]
+fn bad_input_errors_before_any_session(extra: Value, expected_prefix: &str) {
+    let (reg, _host) = load_task_host();
+    let mut input = task_input(SCENARIO_PLAIN, None);
+    for (k, v) in extra.as_object().unwrap() {
+        input[k.as_str()] = v.clone();
+    }
+    let err = exec_tool(&reg, TASK_TOOL, input).unwrap_err();
+    assert!(err.starts_with(expected_prefix), "got: {err}");
+    let snap = probe(&reg);
+    assert_eq!(snap["sessions"], json!(0));
+    assert_eq!(snap["prompt_count"], json!(0));
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn structured_happy_path_returns_validated_json() {
+    let (reg, _host) = load_task_host();
+    let out = exec_tool(
+        &reg,
+        TASK_TOOL,
+        task_input(SCENARIO_HAPPY, Some(answer_schema())),
+    )
+    .expect("structured task failed");
+    let parsed: Value = serde_json::from_str(&out).expect("result is not json");
+    assert_eq!(parsed, json!({ "answer": "42" }));
+
+    let snap = probe(&reg);
+    assert_eq!(snap["sessions"], json!(1));
+    assert_eq!(snap["closed"], json!(1));
+    assert_eq!(snap["prompt_count"], json!(1));
+    assert_eq!(snap["has_local_tools"], json!(true));
+    assert!(snap["first_ack"].is_string(), "valid input must be acked");
+    assert!(snap.get("first_err").is_none_or(Value::is_null));
+    let prompt = snap["prompts"][0].as_str().expect("prompt missing");
+    assert!(prompt.starts_with(TASK_PROMPT), "got: {prompt}");
+    assert!(
+        prompt.contains(STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_TOOL),
+        "prompt must point at the structured_output tool: {prompt}"
+    );
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn invalid_then_valid_recovers_within_one_prompt() {
+    let (reg, _host) = load_task_host();
+    let out = exec_tool(
+        &reg,
+        TASK_TOOL,
+        task_input(SCENARIO_INVALID_THEN_VALID, Some(answer_schema())),
+    )
+    .expect("task should succeed after inline retry");
+    let parsed: Value = serde_json::from_str(&out).expect("result is not json");
+    assert_eq!(parsed, json!({ "answer": "42" }));
+
+    let snap = probe(&reg);
+    assert!(snap.get("first_ack").is_none_or(Value::is_null));
+    let first_err = snap["first_err"].as_str().expect("first_err missing");
+    assert!(
+        first_err.contains("/answer"),
+        "inline error should point at the failing path: {first_err}"
+    );
+    assert!(snap["second_ack"].is_string(), "valid retry must be acked");
+    assert!(snap.get("second_err").is_none_or(Value::is_null));
+    assert_eq!(snap["prompt_count"], json!(1));
+    assert_eq!(snap["closed"], json!(1));
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn missing_structured_output_nudges_then_errors() {
+    let (reg, _host) = load_task_host();
+    let err = exec_tool(
+        &reg,
+        TASK_TOOL,
+        task_input(SCENARIO_NEVER_STRUCTURED, Some(answer_schema())),
+    )
+    .unwrap_err();
+    assert_eq!(err, STRUCTURED_MISSING_ERROR);
+
+    let snap = probe(&reg);
+    assert_eq!(snap["prompt_count"], json!(1 + MAX_STRUCTURED_RETRIES));
+    for i in 1..=MAX_STRUCTURED_RETRIES {
+        let nudge = snap["prompts"][i].as_str().expect("nudge prompt missing");
+        assert!(nudge.contains(STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_TOOL), "got: {nudge}");
+    }
+    assert_eq!(snap["closed"], json!(1));
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn invalid_only_errors_with_bounded_schema_errors() {
+    let (reg, _host) = load_task_host();
+    let err = exec_tool(
+        &reg,
+        TASK_TOOL,
+        task_input(SCENARIO_INVALID_ONLY, Some(multi_error_schema())),
+    )
+    .unwrap_err();
+    assert!(err.starts_with(STRUCTURED_INVALID_ERROR), "got: {err}");
+    assert_eq!(err.lines().count(), 1 + MAX_SCHEMA_ERRORS, "got: {err}");
+
+    let snap = probe(&reg);
+    assert_eq!(snap["prompt_count"], json!(1 + MAX_STRUCTURED_RETRIES));
+    let first_err = snap["first_err"].as_str().expect("first_err missing");
+    assert_eq!(
+        first_err.lines().count(),
+        1 + MAX_SCHEMA_ERRORS,
+        "inline error must carry at most MAX_SCHEMA_ERRORS validation lines: {first_err}"
+    );
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn prompt_error_maps_to_sub_agent_error() {
+    let (reg, _host) = load_task_host();
+    let err = exec_tool(&reg, TASK_TOOL, task_input(SCENARIO_PROMPT_ERROR, None)).unwrap_err();
+    assert_eq!(err, format!("{SUB_AGENT_ERROR_PREFIX}{PROMPT_ERR_MSG}"));
+    let snap = probe(&reg);
+    assert_eq!(snap["closed"], json!(1));
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn plain_path_returns_text_without_local_tools() {
+    let (reg, _host) = load_task_host();
+    let out = exec_tool(&reg, TASK_TOOL, task_input(SCENARIO_PLAIN, None)).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(out, PLAIN_TEXT);
+
+    let snap = probe(&reg);
+    assert_eq!(snap["has_local_tools"], json!(false));
+    assert_eq!(snap["prompt_count"], json!(1));
+    assert_eq!(snap["prompts"][0], json!(TASK_PROMPT));
+    assert_eq!(snap["closed"], json!(1));
+}
+
+/// Spy counters catch a leaked permit even when gc would silently reclaim it.
+#[test]
+fn raising_prompt_does_not_leak_semaphore_permit() {
+    let (reg, _host) = load_task_host();
+    let err = exec_tool(&reg, TASK_TOOL, task_input(SCENARIO_RAISE, None)).unwrap_err();
+    assert!(err.contains(RAISE_MSG), "got: {err}");
+
+    let snap = probe(&reg);
+    let cap = snap["task_cap"].as_u64().expect("task_cap missing");
+    assert_eq!(
+        snap["sem_size"],
+        json!(cap),
+        "semaphore not sized from config"
+    );
+    assert_eq!(snap["acquired"], json!(1));
+    assert_eq!(snap["released"], json!(1), "permit not explicitly released");
+
+    // Pool is full again (released == acquired), so this cannot block.
+    let out = exec_tool(&reg, TASK_TOOL, task_input(SCENARIO_PLAIN, None)).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(out, PLAIN_TEXT);
+}

### Assistant

Here's a comprehensive report of the architecture changes between v0.3.23 and v0.3.26.

---

## 1. Agent Loop — `maki-agent/src/agent/run.rs`

**Commit `30bb903`** (main workflow commit) and **`d7065a8`** (empty response nudge).

### New fields on `Agent` struct (line 106-107)
- `workflow: bool` — toggles whether the run is in workflow mode
- `post_tool_empty_retried: bool` — guards the nudge mechanism (fires at most once)
- `registry: Arc<ToolRegistry>` and `audience: ToolAudience` — injected via `AgentParams`
- `local_tools: LocalTools` — passed in via `with_local_tools()` builder (line 172)

### `run()` picks up `input.workflow` (line 187)
```rust
self.workflow = input.workflow;
```
This flag flows into `ToolContext` (line 411) and is used by plugins (especially `code_execution` and `task`) to decide which tools to expose.

### Nudge on empty response (lines 283–299)
When the model returns no text content after a tool call, the agent inserts a synthetic assistant "(empty)" message followed by a user-nudge prompt: `NUDGE_PROMPT` (line 27). This prevents silent deadlocks where the model forgets to respond. The nudge fires at most once per round of tool calls (`post_tool_empty_retried` is reset in `process_tool_calls` at line 377).

### Compaction model resolution (lines 29–44)
Now uses `spec_for_tier_any(ModelTier::Compaction)` from the model registry instead of `spec_for_tier`.

---

## 2. Task Plugin — `plugins/task/init.lua`

Commit `30bb903` rewrote this plugin. The old version was a thin wrapper around `maki.agent.run()`. The new version:

### Structured output (lines 1–21, 86–140)
The plugin owns the **structured output** pattern entirely in Lua. Key architecture:

- **`output_schema`** parameter (line 56): If set, a session-local `structured_output` tool is injected into the subagent's toolset (line 126–139)
- **Schema validation** uses `maki.json.schema_validator()` compiled upfront (line 90–91) — zero token cost on bad schema
- **Inline retry**: The validator runs in the tool handler; invalid input returns an inline error the model can fix in the same turn (line 131–134)
- **Post-task nudge loop**: If the subagent finishes without calling `structured_output`, up to `MAX_STRUCTURED_RETRIES` (2) nudges are sent (lines 168–172)
- **Error policy**: 
  - Schema compile errors → immediate error, no session created (line 91–93)
  - Missing structured output → `STRUCTURED_MISSING_ERROR` (line 180)
  - Invalid output after retries → `STRUCTURED_INVALID_ERROR` with up to `MAX_SCHEMA_ERRORS` (3) validation lines (line 180)
  - Result: validated JSON string (`maki.json.encode(captured)`) or plain text (line 183)

### Concurrency control (lines 70, 143–146)
- Process-wide semaphore via `maki.async.semaphore()`, sized from `ctx:config("task_max_concurrent", 1)` (line 144)
- Permit acquired before session creation, released in all paths via `pcall` (lines 146, 186)
- Raised errors cannot leak the permit (line 149 wraps the body in `pcall`)

### Session lifecycle (lines 150–174)
Replaced the old `maki.agent.run()` with an explicit **session API**:
- `maki.agent.session(ctx, {...})` — creates a subagent session (line 150–157)
- `sess:prompt(message)` — sends a message and gets a result (line 167)
- `sess:close()` — tears down the session (line 174)

### `"workflow"` audience (line 201)
The task tool registers for both `"main"` and `"workflow"` audiences, enabling its use from workflow-mode runs.

---

## 3. Policy Tests — `maki-lua/tests/task_policy.rs`

This **new file** (in commit `30bb903`) end-to-end tests the structured-output policy using real Lua plugin source + stubbed model I/O. Key tests:

| Test | What it asserts |
|---|---|
| `bad_input_errors_before_any_session` | Invalid `subagent_type` or bad `output_schema` → error, zero sessions created |
| `structured_happy_path_returns_validated_json` | Valid output → returns JSON, prompt includes `structured_output` tool hint |
| `invalid_then_valid_recovers_within_one_prompt` | Inline schema errors → model can fix same turn, no extra API call |
| `missing_structured_output_nudges_then_errors` | Never calls `structured_output` → nudge × `MAX_STRUCTURED_RETRIES`, then error |
| `invalid_only_errors_with_bounded_schema_errors` | Always invalid → `MAX_SCHEMA_ERRORS` lines in error, both inline and final |
| `raising_prompt_does_not_leak_semaphore_permit` | Error in prompt → permit released (acquired == released), pool usable for next task |

**Testing infrastructure**: A Lua `STUB_PRELUDE` replaces `maki.agent.session` with scriptable behaviors keyed by task `description`, wraps the semaphore with spy counters, and registers a `probe` tool for snapshot inspection. This avoids any real model I/O while testing the real schema validator and semaphore.

---

## 4. Tool Dispatching — `maki-agent/src/agent/tool_dispatch.rs`

### Local tools path (lines 71–73)
A new **`local_tools`** fast path: tools registered in `ctx.local_tools` (a `HashMap<String, LocalToolFn>`) are dispatched directly via `run_local_tool()` (lines 208–245) without going through the registry. This is how the `structured_output` tool works — it's injected per-session as a closure, not registered globally.

### `run()` function now takes `Emit` enum (line 18)
Controls whether `ToolStart` events are emitted: `Emit::Notify` (normal) or `Emit::Silent` (for test paths). Parse errors and unknown tools skip the start event entirely (line 60 doc comment).

### Permission enforcement order (lines 116–131, 150–152)
The dispatch now checks:
1. **Plan mode restricted writes** — if `ctx.mode.plan_path()` is set, only writes targeting the plan file path are allowed (line 117–118)
2. **Boundary check** — non-plan writes blocked by `boundary_block_reason()` (line 127)
3. **Permission enforcement** — `enforce_permission()` runs `after` the tool's `start()` but `before` `execute()` (lines 148–152)

Test `start_runs_before_permission_denial_blocks_execute` (lines 732–782) verifies the start phase runs even when permission is denied.

### MCP tool permission handling (lines 280–340)
MCP tools now go through their own permission path with `ToolKey::parse()` and truncated input scope (lines 300–314). Plan mode blocks MCP tools entirely (line 296–298).

### `TaskSet` for parallel execution (lines 382–420)
Tool calls now run via `TaskSet::spawn()` / `join_all()` — a concurrency primitive in `maki-agent/src/task_set.rs`. Panicking tasks produce an error `ToolDoneEvent` instead of propagating (lines 414–418).

---

## 5. Permissions — `maki-agent/src/permissions.rs`

### Auto-allow plan file writes (commit `a169127`)

The `check_inner()` method now accepts `plan_path: Option<&Path>` (line 214). When set and the tool is a FILE_WRITE_TOOL, paths matching the plan file are auto-allowed after deny evaluation but before unclaimed-scope prompting (lines 273–286 in the current file):

```rust
// Plan file auto-allow: fires AFTER deny rules have been evaluated.
// Only triggers if ALL pending scopes match the plan file path.
if !force_prompt && !pending.is_empty() {
    let is_plan_write = plan_path.is_some_and(|pp| {
        matches!(tool, ToolKey::Native(name) if FILE_WRITE_TOOLS.contains(&name.as_ref()))
            && pending.iter().all(|s| normalize_scope_path(s) == normalized_plan)
    });
    if is_plan_write {
        return PermissionCheck::Allowed;
    }
}
```

Key details:
- **After denies**: A deny rule still blocks plan writes (the deny check at lines 238–241 runs first)
- **All-or-nothing for multi-scope**: For `check_multi`, ALL pending scopes must match the plan path. A single non-plan scope triggers the prompt (test at line 1341–1367 in the current file)
- **`FILE_WRITE_TOOLS` list**: Config-defined set from `maki_config` (imported at line 7), used dynamically instead of hardcoded `["write", "edit", "multiedit"]`

### `builtin_rules()` generalized (lines 21–37)
Now iterates over `FILE_WRITE_TOOLS` instead of hardcoding three tools. The `task` tool gets an unrestricted `*` scope auto-allow.

### `generalize_scope()` updated (line 603)
Uses `FILE_WRITE_TOOLS.contains()` instead of matching individual tool names.

### Propagation throughout the permission pipeline
`plan_path` is threaded through:
- `check()` → `check_inner()` (lines 319–321)
- `check_multi()` → `check_inner()` (lines 329–331)
- `enforce()` → double-check + prompt (lines 446, 463)

---

## Summary: New Workflow/Task Orchestration Architecture

The v0.3.23 → v0.3.26 changes introduce a **Lua-owned orchestration policy** over Rust primitives:

```
Rust primitives:
  ToolRegistry, ToolAudience (incl. WORKFLOW), TaskSet,
  maki.agent.session / sess:prompt / sess:close,
  maki.json.schema_validator, maki.async.semaphore

Lua orchestration (plugins/task/init.lua):
  structured_output tool injection, inline validation, nudge loop,
  semaphore-based concurrency cap, subagent lifecycle
```

1. **Workflow mode** (`workflow: bool` in `AgentInput`) flows through agent → ToolContext → plugin description/handler code. The `task` and `code_execution` plugins check `ctx:workflow()` and `dctx.workflow` to filter tools accordingly.

2. **Structured output** is a pure-Lua pattern: a session-local tool with a closure upvalue captures validated results. No Rust changes needed for the schema validation or retry logic.

3. **Permissions** auto-allow plan file writes for all `FILE_WRITE_TOOLS` (config-driven), evaluated after deny rules but before prompting. Multi-scope checks require all scopes to be plan-file paths.

279:         let request = auth

283:                     .uri(format!(
284:                         "{}{}",
285:                         auth.base_url.as_deref().unwrap_or(""),
286:                         MESSAGES_PATH
287:                     ))
288:                     .header("user-agent", super::user_agent())
289:                     .header("content-type", "application/json")
290:                     .header("anthropic-version", "2023-06-01"),
291:             )
292:             .body(json_body)?;
293: 
294:         debug!(model = %model.id, "sending Anthropic-format request via catalog");
295: 
296:         let response = self.client.send_async(request).await?;
297:         let status = response.status().as_u16();
298: 
299:         if status == 200 {
300:             crate::providers::anthropic::parse_sse(response, event_tx, self.stream_timeout).await
301:         } else {
302:             Err(AgentError::from_response(response).await)
303:         }
304:     }

307: impl Provider for Opencode {
308:     fn stream_message<'a>(
309:         &'a self,
310:         model: &'a Model,
311:         messages: &'a [Message],
312:         system: &'a str,
313:         tools: &'a Value,
314:         event_tx: &'a Sender<ProviderEvent>,
315:         opts: RequestOptions,
316:         _session_id: Option<&'a str>,
317:     ) -> BoxFuture<'a, Result<StreamResponse, AgentError>> {
318:         Box::pin(async move {
319:             let model_for_stream = model.clone();
320: 
321:             let model_id = &model_for_stream.id;
322:             let (sub_provider, actual_id) =
323:                 model_id.split_once('/').unwrap_or(("opencode", model_id));
324: 
325:             let (meta, auth) = {
326:                 let guard = CATALOG.get().unwrap().lock().unwrap();
327:                 let (meta, auth) = guard.lookup(&format!("{sub_provider}/{actual_id}"))?;
328:                 // Dynamic provider auth (e.g. from Lua) overrides the opencode route
329:                 let auth = match (&self.auth, meta.provider_id.as_str()) {
330:                     (Some(provider_auth), "opencode") => provider_auth.lock().unwrap().clone(),
331:                     _ => auth,
332:                 };
333:                 (meta, auth)
334:             };
335: 
336:             let mut buf = String::new();
337:             let system = super::with_prefix(&self.system_prefix, system, &mut buf);
338: 
339:             let model = Model {
340:                 id: actual_id.to_string(),
341:                 max_output_tokens: meta.output,
342:                 context_window: meta.context,
343:                 ..model_for_stream
344:             };
345: 
346:             match meta.api_format {
347:                 EndpointType::ChatCompletions => {
348:                     self.handle_catalog_chat_completions(
349:                         &model, messages, system, tools, event_tx, &auth, &opts,
350:                     )
351:                     .await
352:                 }
353:                 EndpointType::Messages => {
354:                     self.handle_catalog_messages(
355:                         &model, messages, system, tools, event_tx, &auth, &opts,
356:                     )
357:                     .await
358:                 }
359:             }
360:         })
361:     }
362: 
363:     fn list_models(&self) -> BoxFuture<'_, Result<Vec<ModelInfo>, AgentError>> {
364:         Box::pin(self.do_list_models())
365:     }
366: 
367:     fn reload_auth(&self) -> BoxFuture<'_, Result<(), AgentError>> {
368:         Box::pin(async { Ok(()) })
369:     }
370: }

374: fn catalog_cache_path() -> Option<PathBuf> {
375:     let dir = maki_storage::paths::cache_dir().ok()?;
376:     Some(dir.join(CATALOG_CACHE_FILE))
377: }
378: 
379: async fn load_cached_catalog_async() -> Option<CatalogIndex> {
380:     let path = catalog_cache_path()?;
381:     let meta = smol::unblock({
382:         let path = path.clone();
383:         move || fs::metadata(&path)
384:     })
385:     .await
386:     .ok()?;
387: 
388:     let modified = meta.modified().ok()?;
389:     let age = SystemTime::now().duration_since(modified).ok()?;
390:     if age > CATALOG_CACHE_TTL {
391:         debug!("catalog cache expired");
392:         return None;
393:     }
394: 
395:     let text = smol::unblock(move || fs::read_to_string(&path))
396:         .await
397:         .ok()?;
398:     let index: CatalogIndex = serde_json::from_str(&text).ok()?;
399:     debug!("loaded catalog from cache");
400:     Some(index)
401: }
402:
