404:     let path = match catalog_cache_path() {
405:         Some(p) => p,
406:         None => return,
407:     };
408:     if let Some(dir) = path.parent() {
409:         let dir = dir.to_path_buf();
410:         let _ = smol::unblock(move || fs::create_dir_all(&dir)).await;
411:     }
412:     let text = match serde_json::to_string_pretty(index) {
413:         Ok(t) => t,
414:         Err(e) => {
415:             warn!(error = %e, "failed to serialize catalog for cache");
416:             return;
417:         }
418:     };
419:     smol::unblock(move || {
420:         if let Err(e) = fs::write(&path, &text) {
421:             warn!(error = %e, path = %path.display(), "failed to write catalog cache");
422:         } else {
423:             debug!(path = %path.display(), "cached catalog");
424:         }
425:     })
426:     .await;
427: }
428: 
429: async fn fetch_remote_catalog_async(client: &HttpClient) -> Result<CatalogIndex, AgentError> {
430:     let request = Request::builder()
431:         .uri(CATALOG_URL)
432:         .header("user-agent", super::user_agent())
433:         .body(())?;
434: 
435:     let mut resp = client.send_async(request).await.map_err(|e| {
436:         warn!(error = %e, CATALOG_URL, "failed to fetch catalog");
437:         AgentError::Config {
438:             message: format!("failed to fetch catalog from {CATALOG_URL}: {e}"),
439:         }
440:     })?;
441: 
442:     let status = resp.status().as_u16();
443:     if status != 200 {
444:         return Err(AgentError::Api {
445:             status,
446:             message: format!("catalog fetch returned HTTP {status}"),
447:         });
448:     }
449: 
450:     let text = resp.text().await.map_err(|e| AgentError::Config {
451:         message: format!("failed to read catalog response body: {e}"),
452:     })?;
453: 
454:     serde_json::from_str(&text).map_err(|e| AgentError::Config {
455:         message: format!("failed to parse catalog JSON: {e}"),
456:     })
457: }
458: 
459: fn determine_catalog_format(npm: &str) -> EndpointType {
460:     match npm {
461:         "@ai-sdk/anthropic" => EndpointType::Messages,
462:         _ => EndpointType::ChatCompletions,
463:     }
464: }
465: 
466: const ALLOWED_NPM: &[&str] = &["@ai-sdk/openai-compatible", "@ai-sdk/anthropic"];
467: 
468: fn catalog_to_data(index: CatalogIndex, enable_free_models: bool) -> CatalogData {
469:     let mut entries: HashMap<ModelWithProvider, CatalogMeta> = HashMap::new();
470:     let mut auths = HashMap::new();
471: 
472:     for (provider_id, provider) in &index {
473:         if !ALLOWED_NPM.contains(&provider.npm.as_str()) {
474:             debug!(npm = %provider.npm, "skipping provider: unsupported npm package");
475:             continue;
476:         }
477: 
478:         let Some(_base_url) = &provider.api else {
479:             debug!(provider = %provider_id, "skipping: no API URL in catalog");
480:             continue;
481:         };
482: 
483:         let has_key = provider.has_api_key();
484:         let auth = provider.build_auth();
485: 
486:         let mut model_count = 0u32;
487:         for (model_id, model_data) in &provider.models {
488:             let input_price = model_data
489:                 .cost
490:                 .as_ref()
491:                 .and_then(|c| c.input)
492:                 .unwrap_or(0.0);
493:             let output_price = model_data
494:                 .cost
495:                 .as_ref()
496:                 .and_then(|c| c.output)
497:                 .unwrap_or(0.0);
498:             let is_free = input_price == 0.0 && output_price == 0.0;
499: 
500:             if is_free && !enable_free_models {
501:                 continue;
502:             }
503: 
504:             if !(has_key || provider_id == "opencode" && is_free) {
505:                 continue;
506:             }
507: 
508:             let api_format = determine_catalog_format(&provider.npm);
509: 
510:             let context = model_data
511:                 .limit
512:                 .as_ref()
513:                 .and_then(|l| l.context)
514:                 .unwrap_or(128_000);
515:             let output = model_data
516:                 .limit
517:                 .as_ref()
518:                 .and_then(|l| l.output)
519:                 .unwrap_or(64_000);
520: 
521:             let cache_read = model_data
522:                 .cost
523:                 .as_ref()
524:                 .and_then(|c| c.cache_read)
525:                 .unwrap_or(0.0);
526:             let cache_write = model_data
527:                 .cost
528:                 .as_ref()
529:                 .and_then(|c| c.cache_write)
530:                 .unwrap_or(0.0);
531: 
532:             let key = (provider_id.clone(), model_id.clone());
533:             entries.insert(
534:                 key,
535:                 CatalogMeta {
536:                     provider_id: provider_id.clone(),
537:                     api_format,
538:                     context,
539:                     output,
540:                     input_price,
541:                     output_price,
542:                     cache_read,
543:                     cache_write,
544:                 },
545:             );
546:             model_count += 1;
547:         }
548: 
549:         if model_count > 0 {
550:             auths.insert(provider_id.clone(), auth);
551:             debug!(
552:                 provider = %provider_id,
553:                 models = model_count,
554:                 has_key,
555:                 "catalog provider registered",
556:             );
557:         }
558:     }
559: 
560:     CatalogData { entries, auths }
561: }
562: 
563: fn init_catalog_blocking() -> CatalogData {
564:     let enable_free_models = maki_config::providers::ProvidersConfig::load()
565:         .get("opencode")
566:         .and_then(|d| d.enable_free_models)
567:         .unwrap_or(false);
568:     // Try cache first (fast, no network)
569:     if let Some(index) = smol::block_on(load_cached_catalog_async()) {
570:         debug!("using cached catalog");
571:         return catalog_to_data(index, enable_free_models);
572:     }
573: 
574:     // Fetch from remote (blocks the current thread)
575:     let client = isahc::HttpClient::builder()
576:         .connect_timeout(Duration::from_secs(10))
577:         .low_speed_timeout(1, Duration::from_secs(30))
578:         .build()
579:         .expect("failed to build catalog HTTP client");
580: 
581:     match smol::block_on(fetch_remote_catalog_async(&client)) {
582:         Ok(index) => {
583:             smol::block_on(save_cached_catalog_async(&index));
584:             catalog_to_data(index, enable_free_models)
585:         }
586:         Err(e) => {
587:             warn!(error = %e, "catalog fetch failed, using empty catalog");
588:             CatalogData {
589:                 entries: HashMap::new(),
590:                 auths: HashMap::new(),
591:             }
592:         }
593:     }
594: }

26: impl ImageMediaType {
27:     pub const ALL: [Self; 4] = [Self::Png, Self::Jpeg, Self::Gif, Self::Webp];
28: 
29:     /// Single source of truth for media-type strings: serde, data URLs,
30:     /// wire formats, and the Lua bridge all go through here.
31:     pub const fn mime(self) -> &'static str {
32:         match self {
33:             Self::Png => "image/png",
34:             Self::Jpeg => "image/jpeg",
35:             Self::Gif => "image/gif",
36:             Self::Webp => "image/webp",
37:         }
38:     }

41:         Self::ALL.into_iter().find(|m| m.mime() == mime)
42:     }

51: impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for ImageMediaType {
52:     fn deserialize<D: serde::Deserializer<'de>>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error> {
53:         let s = String::deserialize(deserializer)?;

86: pub const IMAGE_OMITTED_NOTE: &str =
87:     "[image omitted: the current model does not support image input]";
88: 
89: /// For models without vision, image blocks become a text note instead of a
90: /// wire block the API would reject. History keeps the pixels, so switching
91: /// back to a vision-capable model restores them.
92: pub fn adapt_images_for_model<'a>(model: &Model, messages: &'a [Message]) -> Cow<'a, [Message]> {
93:     let has_image = |m: &Message| {
94:         m.content
95:             .iter()
96:             .any(|b| matches!(b, ContentBlock::Image { .. }))
97:     };
98:     if model.vision || !messages.iter().any(has_image) {
99:         return Cow::Borrowed(messages);
100:     }
101:     let adapted = messages
102:         .iter()
103:         .map(|m| {
104:             let mut m = m.clone();
105:             for block in &mut m.content {
106:                 if matches!(block, ContentBlock::Image { .. }) {
107:                     *block = ContentBlock::Text {
108:                         text: IMAGE_OMITTED_NOTE.into(),
109:                     };
110:                 }
111:             }
112:             m
113:         })
114:         .collect();
115:     Cow::Owned(adapted)
116: }

170: impl Message {

221:             _ => None,

296: const THINKING_USAGE: &str = "Usage: /thinking [off|adaptive|<budget\u{2265}1024>]";
297: const GLM_XHIGH_THRESHOLD: u32 = 8192;
298: 
299: /// Each provider speaks a different dialect of `reasoning_effort`.
300: /// New providers get a variant here instead of a new body-mutating method.
301: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
302: pub enum EffortScale {
303:     /// low / medium / high. Adaptive = medium.
304:     Standard,
305:     /// low / medium / high. Adaptive = high.
306:     PreferHigh,
307:     /// Always "high", ignores budget.
308:     HighOnly,
309:     /// none / high / xhigh. GLM reasons by default, so Off sends "none"
310:     /// explicitly. Only use behind `Model::supports_thinking`.
311:     Glm,
312: }
313: 
314: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
315: pub enum ThinkingConfig {
316:     #[default]
317:     Off,
318:     Adaptive,
319:     Budget(u32),
320: }
321: 
322: impl ThinkingConfig {
323:     pub fn is_enabled(self) -> bool {
324:         !matches!(self, Self::Off)
325:     }
326: 
327:     pub fn budget_to_effort(n: u32) -> &'static str {
328:         if n < 2048 {
329:             "low"
330:         } else if n < 8192 {
331:             "medium"
332:         } else {
333:             "high"
334:         }
335:     }
336: 
337:     pub fn apply_to_body(self, body: &mut Value, model_id: &str) {
338:         match self {
339:             Self::Off => {}
340:             Self::Adaptive => {
341:                 body["thinking"] = json!({"type": "adaptive"});
342:             }
343:             Self::Budget(n) if Self::requires_adaptive(model_id) => {
344:                 body["thinking"] = json!({"type": "adaptive"});
345:                 body["output_config"]["effort"] = json!(Self::budget_to_effort(n));
346:             }
347:             Self::Budget(n) => {
348:                 body["thinking"] = json!({"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": n});
349:             }
350:         }
351:     }
352: 
353:     /// Version check, not an allowlist, so future Opus releases work automatically.
354:     fn requires_adaptive(model_id: &str) -> bool {
355:         let Some(version) = model_id.strip_prefix("claude-opus-") else {
356:             return false;
357:         };
358:         let mut parts = version.split('-');
359:         let (Some(Ok(major)), Some(Ok(minor))) = (
360:             parts.next().map(str::parse::<u32>),
361:             parts.next().map(str::parse::<u32>),
362:         ) else {
363:             return false;
364:         };
365:         (major, minor) >= (4, 7)
366:     }
367: 
368:     pub fn apply_reasoning_effort(self, body: &mut Value, scale: EffortScale) {
369:         let effort = match (self, scale) {
370:             (Self::Off, EffortScale::Glm) => "none",
371:             (Self::Off, _) => return,
372:             (Self::Adaptive, EffortScale::Standard) => "medium",
373:             (Self::Adaptive, _) => "high",
374:             (Self::Budget(_), EffortScale::HighOnly) => "high",
375:             (Self::Budget(n), EffortScale::Glm) => {
376:                 if n >= GLM_XHIGH_THRESHOLD {
377:                     "xhigh"
378:                 } else {
379:                     "high"
380:                 }
381:             }
382:             (Self::Budget(n), EffortScale::Standard | EffortScale::PreferHigh) => {
383:                 Self::budget_to_effort(n)
384:             }
385:         };
386:         body["reasoning_effort"] = json!(effort);
387:     }
388: 
389:     pub fn apply_google_thinking(self, body: &mut Value) {
390:         match self {
391:             Self::Off => {}
392:             Self::Adaptive => {
393:                 body["generationConfig"]["thinkingConfig"] = json!({"includeThoughts": true});
394:             }
395:             Self::Budget(n) => {
396:                 body["generationConfig"]["thinkingConfig"] = json!({"thinkingBudget": n});
397:             }
398:         }
399:     }
400: 
401:     pub fn apply_local_thinking(self, body: &mut Value) {
402:         let budget = match self {
403:             Self::Off => 0,
404:             Self::Adaptive => -1,
405:             Self::Budget(n) => n as i64,
406:         };
407:         body["thinking_budget_tokens"] = json!(budget);
408:     }
409: 
410:     pub fn parse(input: &str, current: Self) -> Result<Self, &'static str> {
411:         if input.is_empty() {
412:             return Ok(if current.is_enabled() {
413:                 Self::Off
414:             } else {
415:                 Self::Adaptive
416:             });
417:         }
418:         StoredThinking::parse_setting(input)
419:             .map(Into::into)
420:             .map_err(|_| THINKING_USAGE)
421:     }
422: 
423:     pub fn status_label(self) -> Option<Cow<'static, str>> {
424:         match self {
425:             Self::Off => None,
426:             Self::Adaptive => Some(Cow::Borrowed("thinking")),
427:             Self::Budget(n) => Some(Cow::Owned(format!("thinking: {n}"))),
428:         }
429:     }
430: }
431: 
432: impl std::fmt::Display for ThinkingConfig {
433:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
434:         match self {
435:             Self::Off => f.write_str("off"),
436:             Self::Adaptive => f.write_str("adaptive"),
437:             Self::Budget(n) => write!(f, "{n}"),
438:         }
439:     }
440: }
441: 
442: impl From<StoredThinking> for ThinkingConfig {
443:     fn from(s: StoredThinking) -> Self {
444:         match s {
445:             StoredThinking::Off => Self::Off,
446:             StoredThinking::Adaptive => Self::Adaptive,
447:             StoredThinking::Budget { tokens } => Self::Budget(tokens),
448:         }
449:     }
450: }
451: 
452: impl From<ThinkingConfig> for StoredThinking {
453:     fn from(c: ThinkingConfig) -> Self {
454:         match c {
455:             ThinkingConfig::Off => Self::Off,
456:             ThinkingConfig::Adaptive => Self::Adaptive,
457:             ThinkingConfig::Budget(n) => Self::Budget { tokens: n },
458:         }
459:     }
460: }

462: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
463: pub struct RequestOptions {
464:     pub thinking: ThinkingConfig,
465:     /// Raw user preference, reconciled by [`RequestOptions::clamped`] before use.
466:     pub fast: bool,
467: }
468: 
469: impl RequestOptions {
470:     /// Strips options the model does not support. Called once before every
471:     /// request so UI state, restored sessions, and subagent flags all go
472:     /// through the same gate.
473:     pub fn clamped(self, model: &crate::model::Model) -> Self {
474:         Self {
475:             thinking: if model.supports_thinking() {
476:                 self.thinking
477:             } else {
478:                 ThinkingConfig::Off
479:             },
480:             fast: self.fast && model.supports_fast(),
481:         }
482:     }
483: }

492: /// Provider-reported usage quota, independent of local token accounting. Not every
493: /// provider exposes a programmatic quota endpoint; check `Provider::fetch_usage`.
494: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
495: pub struct ProviderUsage {
496:     /// Subscription/plan level when the provider reports one (e.g. "lite").
497:     #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
498:     pub plan: Option<String>,
499:     pub limits: Vec<UsageLimit>,
500: }
501: 
502: /// A single quota window (e.g. a 5-hour or weekly token quota).
503: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
504: pub struct UsageLimit {
505:     /// Human-readable label for the window, provided by the provider.
506:     pub label: String,
507:     /// Usage percentage within the window, 0-100.
508:     pub percentage: u32,
509:     /// When the window resets, as epoch milliseconds.
510:     #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
511:     pub reset_at: Option<u64>,
512:     /// Extra provider-supplied context, e.g. "$2.33 spent" for usage credits.
513:     #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
514:     pub detail: Option<String>,
515: }

134:     type Err = ModelError;
135: 
136:     fn from_str(s: &str) -> Result<Self, Self::Err> {
137:         match s {
138:             "weak" => Ok(Self::Weak),
139:             "medium" => Ok(Self::Medium),
140:             "strong" => Ok(Self::Strong),
141:             "compaction" => Ok(Self::Compaction),
142:             other => Err(ModelError::InvalidTier(other.to_string())),
143:         }
144:     }
145: }
146: 
147: impl From<maki_config::providers::Tier> for ModelTier {
148:     fn from(t: maki_config::providers::Tier) -> Self {
149:         use maki_config::providers::Tier;
150:         match t {
151:             Tier::Weak => Self::Weak,
152:             Tier::Medium => Self::Medium,
153:             Tier::Strong => Self::Strong,
154:             Tier::Compaction => Self::Compaction,
155:         }
156:     }
157: }

159: pub struct ModelEntry {
160:     pub prefixes: &'static [&'static str],
161:     pub tier: ModelTier,
162:     pub family: ModelFamily,
163:     /// Gates vision-only tools (`view_image`) and image blocks at request time.
164:     pub vision: bool,
165:     pub default: bool,
166:     pub pricing: ModelPricing,
167:     pub max_output_tokens: u32,
168:     pub context_window: u32,
169: }
170: 
171: fn lookup_entry<'a>(
172:     entries: &'a [ModelEntry],
173:     model_id: &str,
174: ) -> Result<&'a ModelEntry, ModelError> {
175:     entries
176:         .iter()
177:         .flat_map(|e| e.prefixes.iter().map(move |p| (p, e)))
178:         .filter(|(p, _)| model_id.starts_with(*p))
179:         .max_by_key(|(p, _)| p.len())
180:         .map(|(_, e)| e)
181:         .ok_or_else(|| ModelError::UnknownModel(model_id.to_string()))
182: }
183: 
184: pub fn models_for_provider(provider: ProviderKind) -> &'static [ModelEntry] {
185:     match provider {
186:         ProviderKind::Anthropic => anthropic::models(),
187:         ProviderKind::OpenAi => openai::models(),
188:         ProviderKind::Copilot => copilot::models(),
189:         ProviderKind::Ollama => ollama::models(),
190:         ProviderKind::LlamaCpp => llama_cpp::models(),
191:         ProviderKind::Mistral => mistral::models(),
192:         ProviderKind::Google => google::models(),
193:         ProviderKind::Zai => zai::models(),
194:         ProviderKind::Synthetic => synthetic::models(),
195:         ProviderKind::TensorX => tensorx::models(),
196:         ProviderKind::DeepSeek => deepseek::models(),
197:         ProviderKind::OpenRouter => openrouter::models(),
198:         ProviderKind::Opencode => &[],
199:     }
200: }
201: 
202: impl ModelFamily {
203:     pub fn supports_tool_examples(self) -> bool {
204:         match self {
205:             ModelFamily::Claude | ModelFamily::Gpt | ModelFamily::Synthetic => true,
206:             ModelFamily::Generic | ModelFamily::Gemini | ModelFamily::Glm => false,
207:         }
208:     }
209: 
210:     /// Fallback for models missing from the static tables; per-model truth
211:     /// lives in `ModelEntry::vision`.
212:     pub fn supports_vision(self) -> bool {
213:         matches!(self, Self::Claude | Self::Gpt | Self::Gemini)
214:     }
215: }

217: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
218: pub struct Model {
219:     pub id: String,
220:     pub provider: ProviderKind,
221:     pub dynamic_slug: Option<String>,
222:     pub tier: ModelTier,
223:     pub family: ModelFamily,
224:     pub supports_tool_examples_override: Option<bool>,
225:     pub supports_thinking_override: Option<bool>,
226:     /// Resolved once at construction so every consumer reads the same answer.
227:     pub vision: bool,
228:     pub pricing: ModelPricing,
229:     pub max_output_tokens: u32,
230:     pub context_window: u32,
231: }
232: 
233: impl Model {
234:     /// When no static entry matches (a freshly released model the table has not
235:     /// caught up to yet), fall back to the provider defaults so it still resolves.
236:     fn from_base(provider: ProviderKind, model_id: &str, dynamic_slug: Option<&str>) -> Self {
237:         let static_entry = lookup_entry(models_for_provider(provider), model_id).ok();
238:         let spec = match dynamic_slug {
239:             Some(slug) => format!("{slug}/{model_id}"),
240:             None => format!("{provider}/{model_id}"),
241:         };
242:         let tier = crate::model_registry::model_registry()
243:             .read()
244:             .unwrap()
245:             .tier_for(&spec, provider, static_entry.map(|e| e.tier));
246:         let (family, pricing, max_output_tokens, context_window, vision) = match static_entry {
247:             Some(e) => (
248:                 e.family,
249:                 e.pricing.clone(),
250:                 e.max_output_tokens,
251:                 anthropic::shared::long_context_window(model_id).unwrap_or(e.context_window),
252:                 e.vision,
253:             ),
254:             None => {
255:                 let guard = crate::model_registry::model_registry().read().unwrap();
256:                 let discovered = guard.discovered(provider, model_id);
257:                 (
258:                     provider.family(),
259:                     discovered
260:                         .and_then(|d| d.pricing.clone())
261:                         .unwrap_or_default(),
262:                     discovered
263:                         .and_then(|d| d.max_output_tokens)
264:                         .unwrap_or_else(|| provider.fallback_max_output()),
265:                     discovered
266:                         .and_then(|d| d.context_window)
267:                         .unwrap_or_else(|| provider.fallback_context_window()),
268:                     provider.family().supports_vision(),
269:                 )
270:             }
271:         };
272:         Self {
273:             id: model_id.to_string(),
274:             provider,
275:             dynamic_slug: dynamic_slug.map(str::to_string),
276:             tier,
277:             family,
278:             supports_tool_examples_override: None,
279:             supports_thinking_override: None,
280:             vision,
281:             pricing,
282:             max_output_tokens,
283:             context_window,
284:         }
285:     }
286: 
287:     pub fn supports_thinking(&self) -> bool {
288:         self.supports_thinking_override
289:             .or_else(|| {
290:                 let guard = crate::model_registry::model_registry().read().unwrap();
291:                 guard
292:                     .discovered(self.provider, &self.id)
293:                     .and_then(|d| d.supports_thinking)
294:             })
295:             .unwrap_or_else(|| self.provider.supports_thinking())
296:     }
297: 
298:     pub fn supports_tool_examples(&self) -> bool {
299:         self.supports_tool_examples_override
300:             .unwrap_or_else(|| self.family.supports_tool_examples())
301:     }
302: 
303:     /// A model supports fast mode exactly when it carries fast-tier pricing, so
304:     /// capability and billing can never disagree. Bedrock reuses
305:     /// `ProviderKind::Anthropic` and the same table, so we also gate on the
306:     /// provider here: fast mode only exists on the direct API.
307:     pub fn supports_fast(&self) -> bool {
308:         self.pricing.fast.is_some() && self.provider == ProviderKind::Anthropic
309:     }
310: 
311:     pub fn spec(&self) -> String {
312:         if let Some(slug) = &self.dynamic_slug {
313:             format!("{slug}/{}", self.id)
314:         } else {
315:             format!("{}/{}", self.provider, self.id)
316:         }
317:     }
318: 
319:     pub fn from_tier(provider: ProviderKind, tier: ModelTier) -> Result<Self, ModelError> {
320:         if let Some(spec) = crate::model_registry::model_registry()
321:             .read()
322:             .unwrap()
323:             .spec_for_tier(provider, tier)
324:         {
325:             return Self::from_spec(&spec);
326:         }
327:         let entries = models_for_provider(provider);
328:         let entry = entries
329:             .iter()
330:             .find(|e| e.default && e.tier == tier)
331:             .ok_or(ModelError::NoDefault(provider, tier))?;
332:         let model_id = entry.prefixes[0];
333:         Self::from_spec(&format!("{provider}/{model_id}"))
334:     }
335: 
336:     pub fn from_tier_dynamic(
337:         provider: ProviderKind,
338:         tier: ModelTier,
339:         dynamic_slug: Option<&str>,
340:     ) -> Result<Self, ModelError> {
341:         if let Some(slug) = dynamic_slug {
342:             if let Some(model) = dynamic::find_model_for_tier(slug, tier) {
343:                 return Ok(model);
344:             }
345:             if let Some(model) = super::providers::custom::find_model_for_tier(slug, tier) {
346:                 return Ok(model);
347:             }
348:             let mut model = Self::from_tier(provider, tier)?;
349:             model.dynamic_slug = Some(slug.to_string());
350:             return Ok(model);
351:         }
352:         Self::from_tier(provider, tier)
353:     }
354: 
355:     pub fn from_spec(spec: &str) -> Result<Self, ModelError> {
356:         let (provider_str, model_id) = spec.split_once('/').ok_or(ModelError::InvalidFormat)?;
357: 
358:         if let Ok(provider) = ProviderKind::from_str(provider_str) {
359:             return Ok(Self::from_base(provider, model_id, None));
360:         }
361: 
362:         if let Some(base) = dynamic::base_for_slug(provider_str) {
363:             if let Some(model) = dynamic::lookup_model(provider_str, model_id) {
364:                 return Ok(model);
365:             }
366:             return Ok(Self::from_base(base, model_id, Some(provider_str)));
367:         }
368: 
369:         if let Some(model) = super::providers::custom::lookup_model(provider_str, model_id) {
370:             return Ok(model);
371:         }
372: 
373:         Err(ModelError::UnsupportedProvider(provider_str.to_string()))
374:     }
375: }

377: #[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
378: pub struct TokenUsage {
379:     /// Non-cached input tokens. Total input = `input + cache_read + cache_creation`.
380:     #[serde(rename = "input_tokens")]
381:     pub input: u32,
382:     #[serde(rename = "output_tokens")]
383:     pub output: u32,
384:     #[serde(rename = "cache_creation_input_tokens")]
385:     pub cache_creation: u32,
386:     #[serde(rename = "cache_read_input_tokens")]
387:     pub cache_read: u32,
388: }
389: 
390: impl From<StoredTokenUsage> for TokenUsage {
391:     fn from(s: StoredTokenUsage) -> Self {
392:         Self {
393:             input: s.input,
394:             output: s.output,
395:             cache_creation: s.cache_creation,
396:             cache_read: s.cache_read,
397:         }
398:     }
399: }
400: 
401: impl From<TokenUsage> for StoredTokenUsage {
402:     fn from(u: TokenUsage) -> Self {
403:         Self {
404:             input: u.input,
405:             output: u.output,
406:             cache_creation: u.cache_creation,
407:             cache_read: u.cache_read,
408:         }
409:     }
410: }
411: 
412: impl TokenUsage {
413:     pub fn total_input(&self) -> u32 {
414:         self.input + self.cache_read + self.cache_creation
415:     }
416: 
417:     pub fn context_tokens(&self) -> u32 {
418:         self.input + self.output + self.cache_creation + self.cache_read
419:     }
420: 
421:     pub fn cost(&self, pricing: &ModelPricing, fast: bool) -> f64 {
422:         let (input, output, cache_write, cache_read) = match &pricing.fast {
423:             Some(f) if fast => (
424:                 f.input,
425:                 f.output,
426:                 f.input * ModelPricing::CACHE_WRITE_MULTIPLIER,
427:                 f.input * ModelPricing::CACHE_READ_MULTIPLIER,
428:             ),
429:             _ => (
430:                 pricing.input,
431:                 pricing.output,
432:                 pricing.cache_write,
433:                 pricing.cache_read,
434:             ),
435:         };
436:         self.input as f64 * input / PER_MILLION
437:             + self.output as f64 * output / PER_MILLION
438:             + self.cache_creation as f64 * cache_write / PER_MILLION
439:             + self.cache_read as f64 * cache_read / PER_MILLION
440:     }
441: }
442: 
443: impl AddAssign for TokenUsage {
444:     fn add_assign(&mut self, rhs: Self) {
445:         self.input += rhs.input;
446:         self.output += rhs.output;
447:         self.cache_creation += rhs.cache_creation;
448:         self.cache_read += rhs.cache_read;
449:     }
450: }

459:     const TIERS: [ModelTier; 4] = [

466:     #[test_case("no-slash-here", ModelError::InvalidFormat ; "invalid_format")]

468:     fn from_spec_errors(spec: &str, expected: ModelError) {
469:         let err = Model::from_spec(spec).unwrap_err();
470:         assert_eq!(
471:             std::mem::discriminant(&err),
472:             std::mem::discriminant(&expected)

476:     #[test]
477:     fn total_input_includes_cached_tokens() {
478:         let usage = TokenUsage {
479:             input: 5_000,
480:             output: 1_000,
481:             cache_creation: 10_000,
482:             cache_read: 150_000,
483:         };
484:         assert_eq!(usage.total_input(), 165_000);
485:     }

487:     #[test]
488:     fn cost_computes_all_token_types() {
489:         let pricing = ModelPricing {
490:             input: 3.00,
491:             output: 15.00,
492:             cache_write: 3.75,
493:             cache_read: 0.30,
494:             fast: None,
495:         };
496:         let usage = TokenUsage {
497:             input: 1_000_000,
498:             output: 100_000,
499:             cache_creation: 200_000,
500:             cache_read: 500_000,
501:         };
502:         let cost = usage.cost(&pricing, false);
503:         let expected = 3.0 + 1.5 + 0.75 + 0.15;
504:         assert!((cost - expected).abs() < 1e-10);
505:     }

507:     #[test]
508:     fn fast_mode_applies_premium_rates() {
509:         let pricing = ModelPricing {
510:             input: 5.00,
511:             output: 25.00,
512:             cache_write: 6.25,
513:             cache_read: 0.50,
514:             fast: Some(FastPricing {
515:                 input: 30.00,
516:                 output: 150.00,
517:             }),
518:         };
519:         let usage = TokenUsage {
520:             input: 1_000_000,
521:             output: 1_000_000,
522:             cache_creation: 1_000_000,
523:             cache_read: 1_000_000,
524:         };
525:         let fast = usage.cost(&pricing, true);
526:         let expected = 30.0 + 150.0 + 37.5 + 3.0;
527:         assert!((fast - expected).abs() < 1e-10);
528:         assert!(fast > usage.cost(&pricing, false));
529:     }

601:                 continue;

605:                 if provider == ProviderKind::DeepSeek && tier == ModelTier::Weak {
606:                     continue;
607:                 }
608:                 // Compaction is user-assigned only, not in static registry
609:                 if tier == ModelTier::Compaction {
610:                     continue;
611:                 }
612:                 let model = Model::from_tier(provider, tier).unwrap();
613:                 assert_eq!(model.provider, provider);
614:                 assert_eq!(model.tier, tier);
615:                 assert!(model.max_output_tokens > 0);
616:                 assert!(model.context_window >= model.max_output_tokens);

636:             if provider.accepts_arbitrary_models() {
637:                 continue;
638:             }
639:             let entries = models_for_provider(provider);
640:             for &tier in &TIERS {
641:                 if provider == ProviderKind::DeepSeek && tier == ModelTier::Weak {
642:                     continue;
643:                 }
644:                 // Compaction is user-assigned only, not in static registry
645:                 if tier == ModelTier::Compaction {
646:                     continue;
647:                 }
648:                 let count = entries
649:                     .iter()
650:                     .filter(|e| e.tier == tier && e.default)
651:                     .count();
652:                 assert_eq!(

284: impl Provider for Zai {
285:     fn stream_message<'a>(
286:         &'a self,
287:         model: &'a Model,
288:         messages: &'a [Message],
289:         system: &'a str,
290:         tools: &'a Value,
291:         event_tx: &'a Sender<ProviderEvent>,
292:         opts: RequestOptions,
293:         _session_id: Option<&str>,
294:     ) -> BoxFuture<'a, Result<StreamResponse, AgentError>> {
295:         Box::pin(async move {
296:             let auth = self.auth.lock().unwrap().clone();
297:             let mut buf = String::new();
298:             let system = super::with_prefix(&self.system_prefix, system, &mut buf);
299:             let mut body = self.compat.build_body(model, messages, system, tools);
300:             if model.supports_thinking() {
301:                 opts.thinking
302:                     .apply_reasoning_effort(&mut body, EffortScale::Glm);
303:             }
304:             match self
305:                 .compat
306:                 .do_stream(model, &[], &body, event_tx, &auth)
307:                 .await
308:             {
309:                 Err(AgentError::Api { status, message })
310:                     if (status == 429 || status >= 500)
311:                         && (message.contains("1113") || message.contains("nsufficien")) =>
312:                 {
313:                     warn!(status, "insufficient funds, bailing out");
314:                     Err(AgentError::Api {
315:                         status: 402,
316:                         message,
317:                     })
318:                 }
319:                 result => result,
320:             }
321:         })
322:     }

325:         Box::pin(async move {

327:             self.compat.do_list_models(&auth).await
328:         })
329:     }

### Assistant

Here is a structured summary of all provider-related changes between v0.3.23..v0.3.26.

---

## 1. Opencode provider (`maki-providers/src/providers/opencode.rs`) — entirely new (1228 lines)

**What it does:** A multi-provider router that discovers available models and their API endpoints from a remote catalog at `https://models.dev/api.json`. A single `opencode` provider slug can serve models hosted by _any_ third-party vendor (NVIDIA, Fireworks, Opencode itself, etc.) without hard-coding each one.

**Catalog-based model discovery:**

1. **`CatalogIndex`** (line 34) — JSON structure where keys are provider slugs (e.g. `"opencode"`, `"nvidia"`) and values are `CatalogProvider` descriptors containing:
   - `env` — list of env vars to try for an API key
   - `npm` — SDK package name (`@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` or `@ai-sdk/anthropic`), which determines wire format
   - `api` — optional base URL override
   - `models` — a `HashMap<String, CatalogModel>` of model IDs to their limits/costs

2. **`init_catalog_blocking()`** (line 563) — called once via `OnceLock` at construction:
   - Checks a local cache file (`models-dev-catalog.json` in the cache dir) with a 24-hour TTL
   - On cache miss, fetches from `CATALOG_URL` over HTTP
   - Deserializes into `CatalogData` via `catalog_to_data()` (line 468)

3. **`catalog_to_data()`** (line 468) — filters `CatalogIndex` into a flat `HashMap<(provider, model_id), CatalogMeta>`:
   - Only allows `ALLOWED_NPM` packages: `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` and `@ai-sdk/anthropic` (line 466)
   - Skips providers with no `api` URL
   - **Key filtering logic** (lines 486–506): a model is included only if `has_api_key` is true, **or** the model is free (zero-cost) under the `opencode` provider itself. A config flag `enable_free_models` gates whether free models appear at all (default false).
   - Builds `ResolvedAuth` per provider (API key via env var, `x-api-key` for Anthropic SDK, `Bearer` otherwise)

4. **Routing at inference** (`stream_message`, line 317): the model ID is split at `/` — the first segment is the sub-provider, the rest is the actual model ID. The `api_format` field (`ChatCompletions` vs `Messages`) determines which handler is called:
   - `handle_catalog_chat_completions` (line 235) — delegates to `OpenAiCompatProvider`
   - `handle_catalog_messages` (line 254) — uses Anthropic's `messages` API format with SSE parsing

**`ProviderKind::Opencode`** returns `&[]` for static model entries (`model.rs:198`) — all models come from the dynamic catalog.

**Key structs/functions:**
| Symbol | Line | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `CatalogProvider` | 37 | Provider descriptor from catalog JSON |
| `CatalogModel` | 83 | Model entry with limits, cost, shape |
| `CatalogMeta` | 120 | Resolved/processed metadata for a model |
| `CatalogData` | 133 | In-memory lookup table + auth map |
| `Opencode` | 195 | The provider impl |
| `init_catalog_blocking()` | 563 | One-time catalog init |
| `catalog_to_data()` | 468 | Filter/index builder |

---

## 2. Copilot auth flow (`maki-providers/src/providers/copilot/auth.rs`)

**Before v0.3.24:** `load_token()` would:
1. Check env vars `GH_COPILOT_TOKEN`/`COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`
2. Check saved credentials
3. Fall through to **auto-discover** tokens from `~/.config/github-copilot/hosts.json` or `~/.config/gh/hosts.yml` (gh CLI config)

`login()` just called `load_token()` — if a token existed anywhere (env, saved, **or** ambient gh config), it said "Copilot token found." No token was ever saved. `logout()` returned an error saying auth is managed externally.

**After v0.3.24 (commit `e163ed7`):**

- **`load_token()`** (line 20) now only checks env vars and saved credentials — **no longer falls through to file discovery**. Returns a clear error: "not authenticated, run `maki auth login copilot` or set `GH_COPILOT_TOKEN`"
- **`discover_token()`** (new function, line 41) — extracted into its own function. Scans the same files but is only called from `login()`.
- **`login(dir: &StateDir)`** — now explicitly:
  - Calls `load_token()` first (fast path if already authed)
  - Calls `discover_token()` to find tokens from gh/Copilot config
  - **Saves** the discovered token via `save_provider_credentials()` — so subsequent sessions find it in saved credentials
- **`logout(dir: &StateDir)`** — now actually deletes saved credentials instead of rejecting the operation
- Tests migrated from ad-hoc `#[test]` functions to `#[test_case]` parametrized tests (lines 132–152)

**Architectural implication:** Explicit login is now required. The ambient-gh-fallback is removed from request-path — auth is explicit, discoverable, and persistent.

---

## 3. Z.AI quota/monitor endpoint (`maki-providers/src/providers/zai/mod.rs`)

**New code added:**

**`QUOTA_LIMIT_URL`** (line 27): `https://api.z.ai/api/monitor/usage/quota/limit`

**Response types** (lines 29–50):
```rust
struct QuotaResponse { data: QuotaData }
struct QuotaData { limits: Vec<QuotaLimit>, level: Option<String> }
struct QuotaLimit { kind: String, unit: u32, percentage: u32, next_reset_time: Option<u64> }
```

**`quota_label()`** (line 52) — maps `(kind, unit)` pairs to human-readable labels:
- `("TOKENS_LIMIT", 3)` → "5-hour tokens"
- `("TOKENS_LIMIT", 6)` → "Weekly tokens"
- `("TIME_LIMIT", _)` → "Subscription time"
- Falls back to `"{kind} #{unit}"` for unknown units

**`impl From<QuotaResponse> for ProviderUsage`** (line 61) — converts API response into the generic `ProviderUsage` type.

**`fetch_usage()`** (line 331) — new trait method implementation: GETs the quota URL, parses JSON, returns `Some(ProviderUsage)`.

**Thinking support:**
- `stream_message()` (line 285) now accepts `opts: RequestOptions` (was `_opts`), and applies `opts.thinking.apply_reasoning_effort(&mut body, EffortScale::Glm)` when `model.supports_thinking()` (line 300–302)
- `adjust_model()` (line 354) — the `glm-5.2` model gets `supports_thinking_override = Some(true)` (line 356)
- New `BuiltInProvider` entry with two plans: `"standard"` (default model `glm-5.1`) and `"coding"` (default model `glm-5-code`), lines 80–109

---

## 4. Types (`maki-providers/src/types.rs`) — new types added

**`EffortScale` enum** (lines 301–312):
```rust
pub enum EffortScale {
    Standard,   // adaptive → "medium"
    PreferHigh, // adaptive → "high"
    HighOnly,   // always "high"
    Glm,        // off → "none", budget ≥8192 → "xhigh"
}
```
Previously `apply_reasoning_effort` took no scale argument — it always used "medium"/"low"/"high". Now each provider dialect passes a scale to get correct reasoning-effort strings. The `Glm` variant sends "none" for Off (GLM reasons by default, so "none" is explicit) and "xhigh" for budgets ≥8192.

**`apply_reasoning_effort()`** signature changed from `(self, body)` to `(self, body, scale: EffortScale)` at line 368.

**`apply_google_thinking()`** (line 389) — new method, sets `generationConfig.thinkingConfig`:
- Adaptive → `{"includeThoughts": true}`
- Budget → `{"thinkingBudget": n}`

**`apply_local_thinking()`** (line 401) — new method, sets `thinking_budget_tokens`:
- Off → `0`, Adaptive → `-1`, Budget → `n`

**`RequestOptions::clamped()`** (line 473) — new method:
- Strips `thinking` to `Off` if `model.supports_thinking()` is false
- Strips `fast` to `false` if `model.supports_fast()` is false
- Single gate for UI, restored sessions, and subagents

**`ProviderUsage` struct** (line 495):
```rust
pub struct ProviderUsage {
    pub plan: Option<String>,
    pub limits: Vec<UsageLimit>,
}
```

**`UsageLimit` struct** (line 504):
```rust
pub struct UsageLimit {
    pub label: String,
    pub percentage: u32,
    pub reset_at: Option<u64>,
    pub detail: Option<String>,  // only in final version (added later by ZAI detail field)
}
```

**`Message::first_text_content()`** changed from private `fn` to `pub fn` (line 219).

---

## 5. Model capabilities (`maki-providers/src/model.rs`)

**`supports_thinking_override: Option<bool>`** added to `Model` struct (line 225). This enables per-model thinking capability flags independent of the provider-level default.

**`Model::supports_thinking()`** (line 287):
```rust
pub fn supports_thinking(&self) -> bool {
    self.supports_thinking_override
        .unwrap_or_else(|| self.provider.supports_thinking())
}
```
Resolution order: override → discovered metadata → provider default.

**`ModelInfo`** gains `supports_thinking: Option<bool>` (line 58 of the struct definition) — so runtime-discovered models (from `/models` endpoints) can advertise thinking support.

**`ProviderKind::Opencode`** added to `models_for_provider()` returning `&[]` — the Opencode provider has no static model entries; all models come from the catalog (line 198).

**`TokenUsage`** gains `From`/`Into` conversions with `StoredTokenUsage` (lines 390–410) for session persistence.

**New tests** (lines 580–595):
- `opencode_from_spec_parses_four_levels` — `"opencode/nvidia/openai/gpt-oss-120b"` correctly splits into provider=`Opencode`, id=`"nvidia/openai/gpt-oss-120b"`
- `opencode_from_spec_parses_three_levels` — `"opencode/opencode/big-pickle"` works

**Architectural implication:** Thinking capability is now per-model rather than per-provider. The `clamped()` method on `RequestOptions` ensures that even if UI state or restored sessions have thinking enabled, it's disabled before the request goes out to a non-thinking model. Combined with `adjust_model()` hooks, individual models can be toggled on/off without changes to the provider trait.

---

### Cross-cutting architectural themes

1. **Thinking becomes per-model**: `supports_thinking_override` on `Model`, `EffortScale` per-provider dialect, `adjust_model()` on the provider trait.
2. **Usage quotas become a first-class concept**: `ProviderUsage`/`UsageLimit` types, `Provider::fetch_usage()` trait method, CLI `/usage` command in the UI.
3. **Opencode enables a catalog-of-providers pattern**: one provider slug routes to dozens of vendors dynamically, with API format auto-detection.
4. **Copilot auth becomes explicit**: no more ambient credentials — users must `maki auth login copilot` to import and persist the token.

84: local description = [[Execute Python code in a sandboxed interpreter with tools as callable functions.
85: 
86: Use for chained/dependent tool calls and filtering/processing results, e.g. filtering web tool output. **DRAMATICALLY** faster than sequential tool calls!
87: 
88: - All tools are async and return strings: `result = await read(path='file.txt')`. Parse output yourself.
89: - Use `asyncio.gather()` for concurrency within one execution.
90: - Available libs: re, asyncio, sys, os, json. No other imports, no classes, no filesystem/network access.
91: - Fresh sandbox each run: no state persists between executions.
92: - 30 second timeout (configurable via `timeout` parameter).
93: - Skip it when a single tool call needs no transformation.
94: - NOT a thinking scratchpad. Reason in your response text.
95: ]]

98:   type = "object",
99:   required = { "code" },
100:   additionalProperties = false,
101:   properties = {
102:     code = {
103:       type = "string",

131: -- Shared predicate for describe and handler so advertised == callable.
132: -- The interpreter is a calling convention, not a capability grant: a read-only
133: -- subagent must not reach edit/write through Python.
134: local function interpreter_tools(tools, audience, workflow)
135:   local out = {}
136:   for _, t in ipairs(tools) do
137:     local aud = {}
138:     for _, a in ipairs(t.audiences) do
139:       aud[a] = true
140:     end
141:     if t.enabled and aud[audience] and (aud.interpreter or (workflow and aud.workflow)) then
142:       t.workflow_only = not aud.interpreter
143:       out[#out + 1] = t
144:     end
145:   end
146:   return out
147: end
148: 
149: local function matches_filter(name, dctx)
150:   if dctx.only then
151:     for _, n in ipairs(dctx.only) do
152:       if n == name then
153:         return true
154:       end
155:     end
156:     return false
157:   end
158:   if dctx.except then
159:     for _, n in ipairs(dctx.except) do
160:       if n == name then
161:         return false
162:       end
163:     end
164:   end
165:   return true
166: end
167: 
168: local function signature(t)
169:   local schema_props = (t.schema and t.schema.properties) or {}
170:   local required = {}
171:   for _, r in ipairs((t.schema and t.schema.required) or {}) do
172:     required[r] = true
173:   end
174:   local names = {}
175:   for pname in pairs(schema_props) do
176:     names[#names + 1] = pname
177:   end
178:   table.sort(names, function(a, b)
179:     local ra, rb = required[a] or false, required[b] or false
180:     if ra ~= rb then
181:       return ra
182:     end
183:     return a < b
184:   end)
185:   local params = {}
186:   for _, pname in ipairs(names) do
187:     local ptype = PY_TYPES[schema_props[pname].type] or "any"
188:     params[#params + 1] = required[pname] and (pname .. ": " .. ptype) or (pname .. ": " .. ptype .. " = None")
189:   end
190:   return "- " .. t.name .. "(" .. table.concat(params, ", ") .. ") -> str"
191: end
192: 
193: -- Keep cheap: runs on every request build. get_tools skips descriptions
194: -- to avoid recursion from describe callbacks.
195: local function describe(dctx)
196:   local parts = { description, TOOLS_HEADER }
197:   local has_workflow_only = false
198:   for _, t in ipairs(interpreter_tools(maki.api.get_tools(), dctx.audience, dctx.workflow)) do
199:     if matches_filter(t.name, dctx) then

201:       parts[#parts + 1] = signature(t) .. "\n"
202:     end
203:   end
204:   if has_workflow_only then
205:     parts[#parts + 1] = WORKFLOW_TOOLS_NOTE
206:   end
207:   return table.concat(parts)
208: end

242:     local name = t.name
243:     tools[name] = function(tool_input)

245:     end
246:   end
247: 
248:   local result, err = maki.interpreter.run(PREAMBLE .. input.code, {
249:     timeout = timeout,
250:     max_memory_mb = config.interpreter_max_memory_mb or DEFAULT_MAX_MEMORY_MB,
251:     on_output = show,

253:   })
254: 
255:   if err then

258:     end

261:     return { llm_output = err, is_error = true, body = buf }

//! Python execution bridge for the agent.
//!
//! We run Python in the monty sandbox, and bridge tool calls back to the agent.
//! Async awaits get batched via AsyncResolver so concurrent tool calls actually run in parallel.
//! Stdout streams to the UI every STREAM_FLUSH_INTERVAL so you see output as it happens.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::fmt::Write;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use maki_interpreter::runner::{self, ToolFn};
use maki_interpreter::{AsyncResolver, PendingCall};
use maki_tool_macro::Tool;
use serde::Deserialize;
use serde_json::Value;

use std::sync::Arc;

use crate::agent::tool_dispatch::Emit;
use crate::cancel::CancelToken;
use crate::permissions::PermissionManager;
use crate::task_set::TaskSet;
use crate::{AgentConfig, AgentEvent, AgentMode, EventSender, ToolInput, ToolOutput};
use async_lock::Mutex;

use smol::future::block_on;

use super::truncate_output;
use super::{Deadline, FileReadTracker};
use crate::tools::{ToolAudience, ToolRegistry};

const STREAM_FLUSH_INTERVAL: Duration = Duration::from_millis(100);
const PREAMBLE: &str = "import re\nimport asyncio\nimport sys\nimport os\nimport json\n";

struct InterpreterEnv {
    event_tx: EventSender,
    mode: AgentMode,
    cancel: CancelToken,
    deadline: Deadline,
    config: AgentConfig,
    permissions: Arc<PermissionManager>,
    file_tracker: Arc<FileReadTracker>,
    user_response_rx: Option<Arc<Mutex<flume::Receiver<String>>>>,
}

#[derive(Tool, Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
pub struct CodeExecution {
    #[param(
        description = "Python code to execute. Tools are async functions that return strings (not objects). You MUST await every call: `result = await read(path='/file')`. Use `await asyncio.gather(...)` for concurrency."
    )]
    code: String,
    #[param(description = "Timeout in seconds (default 30, max 300)")]
    timeout: Option<u64>,
}

impl CodeExecution {
    pub const NAME: &str = "code_execution";
    pub const DESCRIPTION: &str = include_str!("code_execution.md");
    pub const EXAMPLES: Option<&str> = Some(
        r##"[{"code": "files = (await glob(pattern='**/*.rs')).strip().split('\\n')\nresults = await asyncio.gather(*[read(path=f) for f in files if f.strip()])\nfor f, c in zip(files, results):\n    if 'fn main' in c: print(f)"},
            {"code": "result = await grep(pattern='TODO', include='*.rs')\nprint(f\"{len(result.strip().splitlines())} TODOs found\")"},
            {"code": "content = await webfetch(url='https://example.com/docs')\nfor line in content.splitlines():\n    if 'auth' in line.lower(): print(line)"}]"##,
    );

    pub async fn execute(&self, ctx: &super::ToolContext) -> Result<ToolOutput, String> {
        let timeout = Duration::from_secs(
            ctx.deadline.cap_timeout(
                self.timeout
                    .unwrap_or(ctx.config.code_execution_timeout_secs),
            )?,
        );
        let code = self.code.clone();
        let tool_use_id = ctx.tool_use_id.clone();
        let config = ctx.config.clone();
        let deadline = Deadline::after(timeout);
        let limits = runner::limits(timeout, config.interpreter_max_memory_mb * 1024 * 1024);
        let env = InterpreterEnv {
            event_tx: ctx.event_tx.clone(),
            mode: ctx.mode.clone(),
            cancel: ctx.cancel.clone(),
            deadline,
            config,
            permissions: ctx.permissions.clone(),
            file_tracker: ctx.file_tracker.clone(),
            user_response_rx: ctx.user_response_rx.clone(),
        };

        // We race cancel against the blocking thread. If cancel wins, the Python thread
        // keeps running till it finishes. Threads can not be killed safely.
        ctx.cancel
            .race(smol::unblock(move || {
                let tools = build_tool_fns(&env);
                let resolver = build_async_resolver(&env);
                let code = format!("{PREAMBLE}{code}");

                let result = if let Some(ref id) = tool_use_id {
                    let mut accumulated = String::new();
                    let mut last_flush = Instant::now();
                    runner::run_streaming(&code, &tools, Some(&resolver), limits, &mut |line| {
                        accumulated.push_str(line);
                        if last_flush.elapsed() >= STREAM_FLUSH_INTERVAL {
                            env.event_tx.try_send(AgentEvent::ToolOutput {
                                id: id.to_string(),
                                content: accumulated.clone(),
                            });
                            last_flush = Instant::now();
                        }
                    })
                } else {
                    runner::run(&code, &tools, Some(&resolver), limits)
                }
                .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;

                let mut output = String::new();
                if !result.stdout.is_empty() {
                    output.push_str(result.stdout.trim_end());
                    output.push('\n');
                }
                if let Some(ref val) = result.output {
                    if !output.is_empty() {
                        output.push('\n');
                    }
                    let _ = write!(output, "return: {val}");
                }
                if output.is_empty() {
                    output.push_str("(no output)");
                }

                Ok(ToolOutput::Plain(
                    truncate_output(
                        output,
                        env.config.max_output_lines,
                        env.config.max_output_bytes,
                    )
                    .into(),
                ))
            }))
            .await?
    }

    pub fn start_header(&self) -> String {
        let lines = self.code.lines().count();
        format!("{lines} lines")
    }
}

super::impl_tool!(
    CodeExecution,
    audience = super::ToolAudience::MAIN
        | super::ToolAudience::RESEARCH_SUB
        | super::ToolAudience::GENERAL_SUB,
    augment = |desc: &mut String, ctx: &super::DescriptionContext| {
        desc.push_str(&super::build_interpreter_tools_description(ctx.filter));
    },
);

impl super::ToolInvocation for CodeExecution {
    fn start_header(&self) -> super::HeaderFuture {
        super::HeaderFuture::Ready(super::HeaderResult::plain(CodeExecution::start_header(
            self,
        )))
    }
    fn start_input(&self) -> Option<ToolInput> {
        Some(ToolInput::Script {
            language: "python".into(),
            code: self.code.clone(),
        })
    }
    fn start_annotation(&self) -> Option<String> {
        Some(super::timeout_annotation(self.timeout.unwrap_or(30)))
    }
    fn execute<'a>(self: Box<Self>, ctx: &'a super::ToolContext) -> super::ExecFuture<'a> {
        Box::pin(async move { CodeExecution::execute(&self, ctx).await.into() })
    }
}

fn build_tool_fns(env: &InterpreterEnv) -> HashMap<String, ToolFn> {
    let mut tools: HashMap<String, ToolFn> = HashMap::new();

    for entry in ToolRegistry::native().iter().iter() {
        let tool_name = entry.name();
        if !entry.tool.audience().contains(ToolAudience::INTERPRETER) {
            continue;
        }
        if !super::is_tool_enabled(&env.config, tool_name) {
            continue;
        }
        let name = tool_name.to_string();
        let tx = env.event_tx.clone();
        let mode = env.mode.clone();
        let cancel = env.cancel.clone();
        let deadline = env.deadline;
        let permissions = Arc::clone(&env.permissions);
        let config = env.config.clone();
        let file_tracker = Arc::clone(&env.file_tracker);
        let user_response_rx = env.user_response_rx.clone();

        tools.insert(
            name.clone(),
            Box::new(
                move |fn_name: &str, args: Vec<Value>, kwargs: Vec<(String, Value)>| {
                    deadline.check()?;

                    let input = build_tool_input(&args, &kwargs)?;

                    let mut inner_ctx = super::interpreter_ctx(
                        &mode,
                        &tx,
                        cancel.clone(),
                        Arc::clone(&permissions),
                        Arc::clone(&file_tracker),
                        user_response_rx.clone(),
                    );
                    inner_ctx.deadline = deadline;
                    inner_ctx.config = config.clone();
                    let done = block_on(crate::agent::tool_dispatch::run(
                        ToolRegistry::native(),
                        inner_ctx.mcp.as_ref(),
                        String::new(),
                        fn_name,
                        &input,
                        &inner_ctx,
                        Emit::Silent,
                    ));
                    if done.is_error {
                        Err(done.output.as_text())
                    } else {
                        Ok(Value::String(done.output.as_text()))
                    }
                },
            ),
        );
    }

    tools
}

fn build_async_resolver(env: &InterpreterEnv) -> AsyncResolver {
    let tx = env.event_tx.clone();
    let mode = env.mode.clone();
    let cancel = env.cancel.clone();
    let deadline = env.deadline;
    let config = env.config.clone();
    let permissions = Arc::clone(&env.permissions);
    let file_tracker = Arc::clone(&env.file_tracker);
    let user_response_rx = env.user_response_rx.clone();

    Box::new(move |pending_calls: Vec<PendingCall>| {
        let config = config.clone();
        let file_tracker = Arc::clone(&file_tracker);
        let user_response_rx = user_response_rx.clone();
        smol::future::block_on(async {
            let call_ids: Vec<u32> = pending_calls.iter().map(|pc| pc.call_id).collect();
            let mut set = TaskSet::new();
            for pc in pending_calls {
                let tx = tx.clone();
                let mode = mode.clone();
                let cancel = cancel.clone();
                let permissions = Arc::clone(&permissions);
                let config = config.clone();
                let file_tracker = Arc::clone(&file_tracker);
                let user_response_rx = user_response_rx.clone();

                set.spawn(async move {
                    if let Err(e) = deadline.check() {
                        return (pc.call_id, Err(e));
                    }

                    let input = match build_tool_input(&pc.args, &pc.kwargs) {
                        Ok(v) => v,
                        Err(e) => return (pc.call_id, Err(e)),
                    };

                    let mut inner_ctx = super::interpreter_ctx(
                        &mode,
                        &tx,
                        cancel,
                        Arc::clone(&permissions),
                        file_tracker,
                        user_response_rx,
                    );
                    inner_ctx.deadline = deadline;
                    inner_ctx.config = config;
                    let done = crate::agent::tool_dispatch::run(
                        ToolRegistry::native(),
                        inner_ctx.mcp.as_ref(),
                        String::new(),
                        &pc.name,
                        &input,
                        &inner_ctx,
                        Emit::Silent,
                    )
                    .await;

                    let result = if done.is_error {
                        Err(done.output.as_text())
                    } else {
                        Ok(Value::String(done.output.as_text()))
                    };
                    (pc.call_id, result)
                });
            }

            let results: Vec<_> = set
                .join_all()
                .await
                .into_iter()
                .zip(&call_ids)
                .map(|(r, &call_id)| {
                    r.unwrap_or_else(|msg| {
                        tracing::error!(error = %msg, "code_execution inner tool panicked");
                        (call_id, Err(format!("tool panicked: {msg}")))
                    })
                })
                .collect();

            Ok(results)
        })
    })
}

fn build_tool_input(args: &[Value], kwargs: &[(String, Value)]) -> Result<Value, String> {
    if let Some(first) = args.first()
        && first.is_object()
    {
        return Ok(first.clone());
    }

    if !kwargs.is_empty() {
        let mut obj = serde_json::Map::new();
        for (k, v) in kwargs {
            obj.insert(k.clone(), v.clone());
        }
        return Ok(Value::Object(obj));
    }

    if args.is_empty() {
        return Ok(serde_json::json!({}));
    }

    Err("pass arguments as keyword arguments (e.g. read(path='/file'))".into())
}

    #[test_case(&[], &[],                                json!({})               ; "no_args")]
    fn build_tool_input_cases(args: &[Value], kwargs: &[(String, Value)], expected: Value) {

17: 
18: use crate::api::util::convert::{json_to_lua, lua_tool_result};
19: use crate::plugin_permissions::{Permission, PluginPermissions};
20: use crate::runtime::{TaskHandle, lock_cell};
21: 
22: const BRIDGE_CLOSED: &str = "tool bridge closed (cancelled)";
23: 
24: type CallResults = Vec<(u32, Result<Value, String>)>;
25: 
26: enum BridgeMsg {
27:     Line(String),
28:     Calls(Vec<PendingCall>, flume::Sender<CallResults>),
29: }
30: 
31: pub(crate) fn create_interpreter_table(lua: &Lua, perms: &PluginPermissions) -> LuaResult<Table> {
32:     let t = lua.create_table()?;
33:     t.set(
34:         "run",
35:         perms.guard_async(Permission::Run, lua, interpreter_run)?,
36:     )?;
37:     Ok(t)
38: }
39: 
40: fn required<T: mlua::FromLua>(opts: &Table, key: &str) -> LuaResult<T> {
41:     opts.get::<Option<T>>(key)?
42:         .ok_or_else(|| mlua::Error::runtime(format!("interpreter.run: '{key}' is required")))
43: }
44: 
45: fn forward_calls(
46:     tx: &flume::Sender<BridgeMsg>,
47:     calls: Vec<PendingCall>,
48: ) -> Result<CallResults, InterpreterError> {
49:     let (reply_tx, reply_rx) = flume::bounded(1);
50:     tx.send(BridgeMsg::Calls(calls, reply_tx))
51:         .map_err(|_| InterpreterError::Runtime(BRIDGE_CLOSED.into()))?;
52:     reply_rx
53:         .recv()
54:         .map_err(|_| InterpreterError::Runtime(BRIDGE_CLOSED.into()))
55: }
56: 
57: async fn call_lua_tool(lua: Lua, f: Option<Function>, pc: &PendingCall) -> Result<Value, String> {
58:     let Some(f) = f else {
59:         return Err(format!("unknown tool: {}", pc.name));
60:     };
61:     let input = build_tool_input(&pc.args, &pc.kwargs)?;
62:     let arg = json_to_lua(&lua, &input).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
63:     let values = f
64:         .call_async::<mlua::MultiValue>(arg)
65:         .await
66:         .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
67:     lua_tool_result(values)
68:         .map(Value::String)
69:         .map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", pc.name))
70: }
71: 
72: async fn interpreter_run(
73:     lua: Lua,
74:     (code, opts): (String, Table),
75: ) -> LuaResult<(Table, Option<String>)> {
76:     let timeout_secs: u64 = required(&opts, "timeout")?;
77:     let max_memory_mb: usize = required(&opts, "max_memory_mb")?;
78:     let on_output: Function = required(&opts, "on_output")?;
79:     let tools_tbl: Option<Table> = opts.get("tools")?;
80: 
81:     let mut fns: HashMap<String, Function> = HashMap::new();
82:     if let Some(t) = tools_tbl {
83:         for pair in t.pairs::<String, Function>() {
84:             let (name, f) = pair?;
85:             fns.insert(name, f);
86:         }
87:     }
88:     let names: Vec<String> = fns.keys().cloned().collect();
89: 
90:     let cancel = lua
91:         .app_data_ref::<TaskHandle>()
92:         .map(|h| lock_cell(&h).cancel.clone())
93:         .unwrap_or_else(CancelToken::none);
94: 
95:     let timeout = Duration::from_secs(timeout_secs);
96:     let limits = runner::limits(timeout, max_memory_mb * 1024 * 1024);
97: 
98:     let (tx, rx) = flume::unbounded::<BridgeMsg>();
99:     let run = smol::unblock(move || {
100:         let tools: HashMap<String, ToolFn> = names
101:             .into_iter()
102:             .map(|name| {
103:                 let tx = tx.clone();
104:                 let f: ToolFn = Box::new(
105:                     move |fn_name: &str, args: Vec<Value>, kwargs: Vec<(String, Value)>| {
106:                         let call = PendingCall {
107:                             call_id: 0,
108:                             name: fn_name.to_owned(),
109:                             args,
110:                             kwargs,
111:                         };
112:                         forward_calls(&tx, vec![call])
113:                             .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?
114:                             .pop()
115:                             .map(|(_, r)| r)
116:                             .unwrap_or_else(|| Err(BRIDGE_CLOSED.into()))
117:                     },
118:                 );
119:                 (name, f)
120:             })
121:             .collect();
122:         let resolver: AsyncResolver = {
123:             let tx = tx.clone();
124:             Box::new(move |pending| forward_calls(&tx, pending))
125:         };
126: 
127:         let mut flushed = 0usize;
128:         let result = runner::run_streaming(&code, &tools, Some(&resolver), limits, &mut |chunk| {
129:             flushed += chunk.len();
130:             for line in chunk.lines() {
131:                 let _ = tx.send(BridgeMsg::Line(line.to_owned()));
132:             }
133:         })
134:         .map_err(|e| e.to_string());
135:         if let Ok(ir) = &result {
136:             for line in ir.stdout[flushed..].lines() {
137:                 let _ = tx.send(BridgeMsg::Line(line.to_owned()));
138:             }
139:         }
140:         result
141:     });
142: 
143:     let recv_loop = async {
144:         while let Ok(msg) = rx.recv_async().await {
145:             match msg {
146:                 BridgeMsg::Line(line) => on_output.call::<()>(line)?,
147:                 BridgeMsg::Calls(batch, reply) => {
148:                     let futs = batch.into_iter().map(|pc| {
149:                         let f = fns.get(&pc.name).cloned();
150:                         let lua = lua.clone();
151:                         async move { (pc.call_id, call_lua_tool(lua, f, &pc).await) }
152:                     });
153:                     let _ = reply.send(join_all(futs).await);
154:                 }
155:             }
156:         }
157:         Ok::<(), mlua::Error>(())
158:     };
159: 
160:     let (result, cb) = cancel
161:         .race(futures_lite::future::zip(run, recv_loop))
162:         .await
163:         .map_err(mlua::Error::runtime)?;
164:     cb?;
165: 
166:     let tbl = lua.create_table()?;
167:     match result {
168:         Ok(ir) => {
169:             if !ir.stdout.is_empty() {
170:                 tbl.set("stdout", ir.stdout.trim_end())?;
171:             }
172:             if let Some(val) = ir.output {
173:                 tbl.set("output", val.to_string())?;
174:             }
175:             Ok((tbl, None))
176:         }
177:         Err(e) => Ok((tbl, Some(e))),
178:     }
179: }

1: local M = {}

3: local function split_lines(s)
4:   if s:sub(-1) == "\n" then
5:     s = s:sub(1, -2)
6:   end
7:   local lines = {}
8:   for line in (s .. "\n"):gmatch("([^\n]*)\n") do
9:     lines[#lines + 1] = line
10:   end
11:   return lines
12: end

14: function M.replace_lines(content, start_line, end_line, new_string)
15:   local trailing_nl = content:sub(-1) == "\n"
16:   local lines = split_lines(content)
17:   local inserting = end_line == nil
18: 
19:   if inserting then
20:     if start_line < 1 or start_line > #lines + 1 then
21:       return nil, string.format("start line %d out of range (1-%d)", start_line, #lines + 1)
22:     end
23:   else
24:     if start_line < 1 or start_line > #lines then
25:       return nil, string.format("start line %d out of range (1-%d)", start_line, #lines)
26:     end
27:     if end_line < start_line or end_line > #lines then
28:       return nil, string.format("end line %d out of range (%d-%d)", end_line, start_line, #lines)
29:     end
30:   end
31: 
32:   local skip_from = inserting and start_line or start_line
33:   local skip_to = inserting and start_line - 1 or end_line
34: 
35:   local result = {}
36:   for i = 1, skip_from - 1 do
37:     result[#result + 1] = lines[i]
38:   end
39:   if new_string ~= "" then
40:     for _, line in ipairs(split_lines(new_string)) do
41:       result[#result + 1] = line
42:     end
43:   end
44:   for i = skip_to + 1, #lines do
45:     result[#result + 1] = lines[i]
46:   end
47: 
48:   local joined = table.concat(result, "\n")
49:   return trailing_nl and joined .. "\n" or joined
50: end
51: 
52: return M

160:         if !self.has_describe_fn {
161:             return Cow::Borrowed(&self.description);
162:         }
163:         let dctx = dctx_json(ctx);
164:         if let Some(result) = local_describe(&self.plugin, &self.name, &dctx) {
165:             return match result {
166:                 Some(s) => Cow::Owned(s),
167:                 None => Cow::Borrowed(&self.description),
168:             };
169:         }
170:         let (reply_tx, reply_rx) = flume::bounded(1);
171:         let sent = self
172:             .tx
173:             .send(Request::Describe {
174:                 plugin: Arc::clone(&self.plugin),
175:                 tool: Arc::clone(&self.name),
176:                 dctx,
177:                 reply: reply_tx,
178:             })
179:             .is_ok();
180:         if sent {
181:             match reply_rx.recv_timeout(DESCRIBE_TIMEOUT) {
182:                 Ok(Some(s)) => return Cow::Owned(s),
183:                 Ok(None) => {}
184:                 Err(e) => tracing::warn!(
185:                     tool = %self.name,
186:                     error = %e,
187:                     "describe round trip failed; falling back to static description"
188:                 ),
189:             }
190:         }
191:         Cow::Borrowed(&self.description)
192:     }
