218:                 }))
219:             }
220:             Some(PermissionScopeKind::Callback) => PermissionState::NeedsCompute,
221:             None => PermissionState::Ready(None),
222:         };
223:         Ok(Box::new(LuaToolInvocation {
224:             tool: Arc::clone(&self.name),
225:             plugin: Arc::clone(&self.plugin),
226:             has_header_fn: self.has_header_fn,
227:             has_start_fn: self.has_start_fn,
228:             input: validated,
229:             tx: self.tx.clone(),
230:             permission_state,
231:             mutable_path_field: self.mutable_path_field.clone(),
232:             timeout: self.timeout,
233:             start_annotation: self.start_annotation.clone(),
234:         }))
235:     }
236: }
237: 
238: enum PermissionState {
239:     Ready(Option<PermissionScopes>),
240:     NeedsCompute,
241: }
242: 
243: struct LuaToolInvocation {
244:     tool: Arc<str>,
245:     plugin: Arc<str>,
246:     has_header_fn: bool,
247:     has_start_fn: bool,
248:     input: Value,
249:     tx: Sender<Request>,
250:     permission_state: PermissionState,
251:     mutable_path_field: Option<Arc<str>>,
252:     timeout: Option<Duration>,
253:     start_annotation: Option<StartAnnotation>,
254: }
255: 
256: impl ToolInvocation for LuaToolInvocation {
257:     fn start_header(&self) -> HeaderFuture {
258:         if !self.has_header_fn {
259:             return HeaderFuture::Ready(HeaderResult::plain(self.tool.to_string()));
260:         }
261:         let (reply_tx, reply_rx) = flume::bounded::<HeaderResult>(1);
262:         let tool = Arc::clone(&self.tool);
263:         let plugin = Arc::clone(&self.plugin);
264:         let input = self.input.clone();
265:         let tx = self.tx.clone();
266:         let fallback = tool.to_string();
267:         HeaderFuture::Pending {
268:             fallback: fallback.clone(),
269:             fut: Box::pin(async move {
270:                 let sent = tx
271:                     .send_async(Request::ComputeHeader {
272:                         plugin: Arc::clone(&plugin),
273:                         tool: Arc::clone(&tool),
274:                         input,
275:                         reply: reply_tx,
276:                     })
277:                     .await;
278:                 if sent.is_err() {
279:                     return HeaderResult::plain(fallback);
280:                 }
281:                 reply_rx
282:                     .recv_async()
283:                     .await
284:                     .unwrap_or_else(|_| HeaderResult::plain(fallback))
285:             }),
286:         }
287:     }
288: 
289:     fn start_annotation(&self) -> Option<String> {
290:         match self.start_annotation.as_ref()? {
291:             StartAnnotation::Timeout(field) => {
292:                 let secs = self.input.get(field.as_ref())?.as_u64()?;
293:                 Some(timeout_annotation(secs))
294:             }
295:             StartAnnotation::Count(field) => {
296:                 let field = field.as_ref();
297:                 let n = self.input.get(field)?.as_array()?.len();
298:                 let (singular, plural) = if let Some(stem) = field.strip_suffix('s') {
299:                     (stem, field)
300:                 } else {
301:                     (field, &*format!("{field}s"))
302:                 };
303:                 let label = if n == 1 { singular } else { plural };
304:                 Some(format!("{n} {label}"))
305:             }
306:         }
307:     }
308: 
309:     fn start<'a>(&'a self, ctx: &'a ToolContext) -> BoxFuture<'a, ()> {
310:         let id = ctx.tool_use_id.as_ref().filter(|_| self.has_start_fn);
311:         let Some(id) = id else {
312:             return Box::pin(std::future::ready(()));
313:         };
314:         let (reply_tx, reply_rx) = flume::bounded::<()>(1);
315:         let req = Request::StartTool {
316:             plugin: Arc::clone(&self.plugin),
317:             tool: Arc::clone(&self.tool),
318:             input: self.input.clone(),
319:             live: LiveCtx {
320:                 event_tx: ctx.event_tx.clone(),
321:                 tool_use_id: id.clone(),
322:             },
323:             ctx: Box::new(LuaCtx::start(ctx)),
324:             reply: reply_tx,
325:         };
326:         let tx = self.tx.clone();
327:         Box::pin(async move {
328:             if tx.send_async(req).await.is_ok() {
329:                 let _ = reply_rx.recv_async().await;
330:             }
331:         })
332:     }
333: 
334:     fn permission_scopes(&self) -> BoxFuture<'_, Option<PermissionScopes>> {
335:         match &self.permission_state {
336:             PermissionState::Ready(v) => Box::pin(std::future::ready(v.clone())),
337:             PermissionState::NeedsCompute => {
338:                 let (reply_tx, reply_rx) = flume::bounded(1);
339:                 let tx = self.tx.clone();
340:                 let plugin = Arc::clone(&self.plugin);
341:                 let tool = Arc::clone(&self.tool);
342:                 let input = self.input.clone();
343:                 let fallback = input.to_string();
344:                 Box::pin(async move {
345:                     if tx
346:                         .send_async(Request::ComputePermissionScopes {
347:                             plugin,
348:                             tool,
349:                             input,
350:                             reply: reply_tx,
351:                         })
352:                         .await
353:                         .is_err()
354:                     {
355:                         return Some(PermissionScopes::force_prompt(fallback));
356:                     }
357:                     match reply_rx.recv_async().await {
358:                         Ok(Some(scopes)) => Some(scopes),
359:                         _ => Some(PermissionScopes::force_prompt(fallback)),
360:                     }
361:                 })
362:             }
363:         }
364:     }
365: 
366:     fn mutable_path(&self) -> Option<&Path> {
367:         let field = self.mutable_path_field.as_deref()?;
368:         let val = self.input.get(field)?.as_str()?;
369:         Some(Path::new(val))
370:     }
371: 
372:     fn execute<'a>(self: Box<Self>, ctx: &'a ToolContext) -> ExecFuture<'a> {
373:         let deadline = ctx.deadline;
374:         let plugin = self.plugin;
375:         let tool = self.tool;
376:         let input = self.input;
377:         let tx = self.tx;
378:         let tool_timeout = self.timeout;
379: 
380:         Box::pin(async move {
381:             let effective_secs: Option<u64> = match tool_timeout {
382:                 Some(d) => match deadline.cap_timeout(d.as_secs()) {
383:                     Ok(s) => Some(s),
384:                     Err(e) => return Err(e).into(),
385:                 },
386:                 None => match deadline {
387:                     Deadline::At(_) => match deadline.cap_timeout(u64::MAX) {
388:                         Ok(s) => Some(s),
389:                         Err(e) => return Err(e).into(),
390:                     },
391:                     Deadline::None => None,
392:                 },
393:             };
394: 
395:             let (reply_tx, reply_rx) = flume::bounded::<ToolCallReply>(1);
396:             let live = ctx.tool_use_id.clone().map(|id| LiveCtx {
397:                 event_tx: ctx.event_tx.clone(),
398:                 tool_use_id: id,
399:             });
400:             let lua_ctx = LuaCtx::handler(ctx);
401: 
402:             if tx
403:                 .send_async(Request::CallTool {
404:                     plugin: Arc::clone(&plugin),
405:                     tool: Arc::clone(&tool),
406:                     input,
407:                     ctx: Box::new(lua_ctx),
408:                     deadline: match deadline {
409:                         Deadline::At(t) => Some(t),
410:                         Deadline::None => None,
411:                     },
412:                     reply: reply_tx,
413:                     live,
414:                 })
415:                 .await
416:                 .is_err()
417:             {
418:                 return Err("lua thread disconnected".to_string()).into();
419:             }
420: 
421:             let recv = async { Some(reply_rx.recv_async().await) };
422:             let result = match effective_secs {
423:                 Some(secs) => {
424:                     futures_lite::future::race(recv, async move {
425:                         smol::Timer::after(Duration::from_secs(secs)).await;
426:                         None
427:                     })
428:                     .await
429:                 }
430:                 None => recv.await,
431:             };
432: 
433:             match result {
434:                 None => Err(format!(
435:                     "plugin {} tool {} exceeded timeout ({}s)",
436:                     plugin,
437:                     tool,
438:                     effective_secs.unwrap_or(0)
439:                 ))
440:                 .into(),
441:                 Some(Err(_)) => Err("lua thread disconnected".to_string()).into(),
442:                 Some(Ok(reply)) => {
443:                     if let Some(ref id) = ctx.tool_use_id {
444:                         if let Some(live_buf) = reply.live_buf {
445:                             let _ = ctx.event_tx.send(AgentEvent::LiveToolBuf {
446:                                 id: id.clone(),
447:                                 body: live_buf,
448:                             });
449:                         }
450:                         crate::runtime::RestoreReply {
451:                             body: reply.snapshot,
452:                             header: reply.header,
453:                         }
454:                         .emit(id, None, &ctx.event_tx);
455:                     }
456:                     let format = reply.format;
457:                     let instructions = reply.instructions;
458:                     let image = reply.image;
459:                     let state = reply.state;
460:                     ToolExecResult {
461:                         output: reply.result.map(|s| {
462:                             if let Some(source) = image {
463:                                 ToolOutput::Image { source, text: s }
464:                             } else if let Some(diff) = reply.diff {
465:                                 ToolOutput::Diff {
466:                                     summary: s,
467:                                     path: diff.path,
468:                                     before: diff.before,
469:                                     after: diff.after,
470:                                 }
471:                             } else {
472:                                 let inner = TextOutput {
473:                                     text: s,
474:                                     instructions: instructions.filter(|b| !b.is_empty()),
475:                                     state,
476:                                 };
477:                                 match format {
478:                                     LuaOutputFormat::Markdown => ToolOutput::Markdown(inner),
479:                                     LuaOutputFormat::Plain => ToolOutput::Plain(inner),
480:                                 }
481:                             }
482:                         }),
483:                         annotation: reply.annotation,
484:                         written_path: reply.written_path,
485:                     }
486:                 }
487:             }
488:         })
489:     }
490: }
491: 
492: fn parse_slot(spec: &Table) -> LuaResult<Slot> {
493:     spec.get::<String>("slot")
494:         .map_err(|_| mlua::Error::runtime("'slot' is required"))?
495:         .parse()
496:         .map_err(|_| {
497:             mlua::Error::runtime(format!("unknown 'slot'. Valid: {}", Slot::valid_names()))
498:         })
499: }
500: 
501: fn parse_prompt_field(spec: &Table) -> LuaResult<Option<Vec<PromptId>>> {
502:     let parse_one = |s: &str| -> mlua::Result<PromptId> {
503:         s.parse().map_err(|_| {
504:             mlua::Error::runtime(format!(
505:                 "unknown 'prompt'. Valid: {}",
506:                 PromptId::valid_names()
507:             ))
508:         })
509:     };
510:     match spec.get::<LuaValue>("prompt") {
511:         Ok(LuaValue::String(s)) => Ok(Some(vec![parse_one(&s.to_str()?)?])),
512:         Ok(LuaValue::Table(t)) => {
513:             let mut ids = Vec::new();
514:             for pair in t.sequence_values::<mlua::String>() {
515:                 ids.push(parse_one(&pair?.to_str()?)?);
516:             }
517:             if ids.is_empty() {
518:                 return Err(mlua::Error::runtime(
519:                     "'prompt' table is empty or has no sequence entries; expected a list like {\"system\", \"general\"}",
520:                 ));
521:             }
522:             Ok(Some(ids))
523:         }
524:         Ok(LuaValue::Nil) | Err(_) => Ok(None),
525:         Ok(_) => Err(mlua::Error::runtime(
526:             "'prompt' must be a string or list of strings",
527:         )),
528:     }
529: }
530: 
531: fn validate_slot_prompt_compatibility(
532:     slot: Slot,
533:     prompts: &Option<Vec<PromptId>>,
534: ) -> LuaResult<()> {
535:     if let Some(prompts) = prompts {
536:         for &pid in prompts {
537:             if !pid.has_slot(slot) {
538:                 return Err(mlua::Error::runtime(format!(
539:                     "slot '{}' is not available for prompt '{}'",
540:                     slot, pid
541:                 )));
542:             }
543:         }
544:     }
545:     Ok(())
546: }
547: 
548: fn parse_hint_content(lua: &Lua, spec: &Table) -> LuaResult<HintContent> {
549:     let has_content = spec.contains_key("content")?;
550:     if !has_content {
551:         return Err(mlua::Error::runtime("'content' is required"));
552:     }
553: 
554:     match spec.get("content")? {
555:         LuaValue::String(s) => {
556:             let text = s.to_string_lossy();
557:             if text.is_empty() {
558:                 return Err(mlua::Error::runtime("'content' must not be empty"));
559:             }
560:             if text.len() > MAX_HINT_CONTENT_SIZE {
561:                 return Err(mlua::Error::runtime(format!(
562:                     "content exceeds the {} byte limit",
563:                     MAX_HINT_CONTENT_SIZE
564:                 )));
565:             }
566:             Ok(HintContent::Static(text))
567:         }
568:         LuaValue::Function(f) => Ok(HintContent::Callback(lua.create_registry_value(f)?)),
569:         _ => Err(mlua::Error::runtime(
570:             "'content' must be a string or function",
571:         )),
572:     }
573: }
574: 
575: pub(crate) fn create_api_table(
576:     lua: &Lua,
577:     pending: PendingTools,
578:     plugin: Arc<str>,
579: ) -> LuaResult<Table> {
580:     let t = lua.create_table()?;
581: 
582:     t.set(
583:         "register_tool",
584:         lua.create_function(move |lua, spec: Table| {
585:             register_tool_from_lua(lua, &spec, pending.clone())
586:         })?,
587:     )?;
588: 
589:     {
590:         let plugin = Arc::clone(&plugin);
591:         t.set(
592:             "register_prompt_hint",
593:             lua.create_function(move |lua, spec: Table| {
594:                 let slot: Slot = parse_slot(&spec)?;
595:                 if slot.kind() == SlotKind::Singleton {
596:                     return Err(mlua::Error::runtime(format!(
597:                         "register_prompt_hint is for aggregate slots ({}); \
598:                          use set_prompt for singleton slots ({})",
599:                         Slot::names_for_kind(SlotKind::Aggregate),
600:                         Slot::names_for_kind(SlotKind::Singleton),
601:                     )));
602:                 }
603:                 let prompts = parse_prompt_field(&spec)?;
604:                 validate_slot_prompt_compatibility(slot, &prompts)?;
605: 
606:                 let content = parse_hint_content(lua, &spec)?;
607:                 let reg = PromptHintRegistration {
608:                     prompts,
609:                     slot,
610:                     content,
611:                 };
612:                 let mut map = lua
613:                     .app_data_mut::<PromptHintCallbacks>()
614:                     .ok_or_else(|| mlua::Error::runtime("not initialized"))?;
615:                 map.entry(Arc::clone(&plugin)).or_default().push(reg);
616:                 Ok(())
617:             })?,
618:         )?;
619:     }
620: 
621:     {
622:         let plugin = Arc::clone(&plugin);
623:         t.set(
624:             "set_prompt",
625:             lua.create_function(move |lua, spec: Table| {
626:                 let slot: Slot = parse_slot(&spec)?;
627:                 if slot.kind() == SlotKind::Aggregate {
628:                     return Err(mlua::Error::runtime(format!(
629:                         "set_prompt is for singleton slots ({}); \
630:                          use register_prompt_hint for aggregate slots ({})",
631:                         Slot::names_for_kind(SlotKind::Singleton),
632:                         Slot::names_for_kind(SlotKind::Aggregate),
633:                     )));
634:                 }
635: 
636:                 let prompts = parse_prompt_field(&spec)?;
637:                 validate_slot_prompt_compatibility(slot, &prompts)?;
638: 
639:                 let content = parse_hint_content(lua, &spec)?;
640:                 let reg = PromptHintRegistration {
641:                     prompts,
642:                     slot,
643:                     content,
644:                 };
645:                 let mut map = lua
646:                     .app_data_mut::<PromptHintCallbacks>()
647:                     .ok_or_else(|| mlua::Error::runtime("not initialized"))?;
648:                 map.entry(Arc::clone(&plugin)).or_default().push(reg);
649:                 Ok(())
650:             })?,
651:         )?
652:     }
653: 
654:     t.set(
655:         "register_command",
656:         lua.create_function(move |lua, spec: Table| {
657:             register_command_from_lua(lua, &spec, Arc::clone(&plugin))
658:         })?,
659:     )?;
660: 
661:     t.set("get_tools", lua.create_function(get_tools_from_lua)?)?;
662:     t.set("get_tool", lua.create_function(get_tool_from_lua)?)?;
663: 
664:     Ok(t)
665: }
666: 
667: /// Registry snapshot without descriptions (avoids recursion from describe callbacks).
668: fn get_tools_from_lua(lua: &Lua, opts: Option<Table>) -> LuaResult<Table> {
669:     let registry = lua
670:         .app_data_ref::<Arc<ToolRegistry>>()
671:         .map(|r| Arc::clone(&r))
672:         .ok_or_else(|| mlua::Error::runtime("get_tools: tool registry not available"))?;
673:     let mut disabled: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
674:     if let Some(o) = opts
675:         && let Some(config) = o.get::<Option<Table>>("config")?
676:     {
677:         disabled = config
678:             .get::<Option<Vec<String>>>("disabled_tools")?
679:             .unwrap_or_default();
680:     }
681: 
682:     let out = lua.create_table()?;
683:     for (i, entry) in registry.iter().iter().enumerate() {
684:         let t = tool_entry_to_lua(lua, entry)?;
685:         t.set("enabled", is_tool_enabled(&disabled, entry.name()))?;
686:         out.set(i + 1, t)?;
687:     }
688:     Ok(out)
689: }
690: 
691: fn tool_entry_to_lua(lua: &Lua, entry: &RegisteredTool) -> LuaResult<Table> {
692:     let audience = entry.tool.audience();
693:     let audiences = lua.create_table()?;
694:     for (flag, name) in maki_agent::tools::registry::AUDIENCE_NAMES {
695:         if audience.contains(*flag) {
696:             audiences.push(*name)?;
697:         }
698:     }
699:     let t = lua.create_table()?;
700:     t.set("name", entry.name())?;
701:     t.set("schema", json_to_lua(lua, &entry.tool.schema())?)?;
702:     t.set("audiences", audiences)?;
703:     if let Some(kind) = entry.tool.tool_kind() {
704:         t.set("kind", kind)?;
705:     }
706:     Ok(t)
707: }
708: 
709: /// Single-tool lookup that also hands out `header`/`restore` handles for
710: /// Lua tools (nil for MCP or missing tools), wrapped so one broken tool
711: /// cannot break a composing caller. Kept apart from `get_tools` so the
712: /// listing stays a cheap data-only snapshot.
713: fn get_tool_from_lua(lua: &Lua, name: String) -> LuaResult<LuaValue> {
714:     let registry = lua
715:         .app_data_ref::<Arc<ToolRegistry>>()
716:         .map(|r| Arc::clone(&r))
717:         .ok_or_else(|| mlua::Error::runtime("get_tool: tool registry not available"))?;
718:     let Some(entry) = registry.get(&name) else {
719:         return Ok(LuaValue::Nil);
720:     };
721:     let t = tool_entry_to_lua(lua, &entry)?;
722:     if let Some((header, restore)) = local_tool_handles(&name) {
723:         if let Some(f) = header {
724:             t.set("header", wrap_header(lua, name.clone(), f)?)?;
725:         }
726:         if let Some(f) = restore {
727:             t.set("restore", wrap_restore(lua, name, f)?)?;
728:         }
729:     }
730:     Ok(LuaValue::Table(t))
731: }
732: 
733: /// The one contract every `get_tool` handle obeys: it never throws; an
734: /// error from the wrapped fn is logged and becomes nil.
735: fn wrap_nothrow(
736:     lua: &Lua,
737:     tool: String,
738:     handle: &'static str,
739:     f: Function,
740:     norm: impl Fn(&Lua, LuaValue) -> LuaResult<LuaValue> + Send + 'static,
741: ) -> LuaResult<Function> {
742:     lua.create_function(
743:         move |lua, args: MultiValue| match f.call::<LuaValue>(args) {
744:             Ok(v) => norm(lua, v),
745:             Err(e) => {
746:                 tracing::warn!(tool, handle, error = %e, "get_tool handle failed");
747:                 Ok(LuaValue::Nil)
748:             }
749:         },
750:     )
751: }
752: 
753: /// Normalizes a header fn to one spans line or nil: a plain string gets
754: /// the standalone header style, a buf return contributes its first line.
755: fn wrap_header(lua: &Lua, tool: String, f: Function) -> LuaResult<Function> {
756:     wrap_nothrow(lua, tool, "header", f, |lua, v| match v {
757:         LuaValue::String(s) => {
758:             let span = lua.create_table()?;
759:             span.raw_set(1, s)?;
760:             span.raw_set(2, PLAIN_HEADER_STYLE)?;
761:             let line = lua.create_table()?;
762:             line.raw_set(1, span)?;
763:             Ok(LuaValue::Table(line))
764:         }
765:         LuaValue::UserData(ud) => {
766:             let Ok(h) = ud.borrow::<BufHandle>() else {
767:                 return Ok(LuaValue::Nil);
768:             };
769:             match h.buf.read().first() {
770:                 Some(line) => Ok(LuaValue::Table(line_to_lua(lua, line)?)),
771:                 None => Ok(LuaValue::Nil),
772:             }
773:         }
774:         _ => Ok(LuaValue::Nil),
775:     })
776: }
777: 
778: /// Normalizes a restore fn to its body buf or nil (whether it returned
779: /// the buf directly or a `{ body = buf }` reply), so callers composing
780: /// another tool's rendering need no pcall of their own. The ctx arg may be
781: /// a real `LuaCtx` or a plain `{ tool_output_lines =, state = }` table (how
782: /// batch drives child restores); either way the fn sees a restore `LuaCtx`.
783: fn wrap_restore(lua: &Lua, tool: String, f: Function) -> LuaResult<Function> {
784:     let prepped = lua.create_function(move |lua, mut args: MultiValue| {
785:         let ctx = normalize_restore_ctx(lua, args.get(3))?;
786:         while args.len() < 4 {
787:             args.push_back(LuaValue::Nil);
788:         }
789:         args[3] = ctx;
790:         f.call::<MultiValue>(args)
791:     })?;
792:     wrap_nothrow(lua, tool, "restore", prepped, |_lua, v| {
793:         Ok(match &v {
794:             LuaValue::UserData(ud) if ud.is::<BufHandle>() => v,
795:             LuaValue::Table(t) => t
796:                 .get::<mlua::AnyUserData>("body")
797:                 .ok()
798:                 .filter(|ud| ud.is::<BufHandle>())
799:                 .map(LuaValue::UserData)
800:                 .unwrap_or(LuaValue::Nil),
801:             _ => LuaValue::Nil,
802:         })
803:     })
804: }
805: 
806: fn normalize_restore_ctx(lua: &Lua, v: Option<&LuaValue>) -> LuaResult<LuaValue> {
807:     if let Some(LuaValue::UserData(ud)) = v
808:         && ud.is::<LuaCtx>()
809:     {
810:         return Ok(LuaValue::UserData(ud.clone()));
811:     }
812:     let (tol, state) = match v {
813:         Some(LuaValue::Table(t)) => (
814:             t.get::<LuaValue>("tool_output_lines")
815:                 .ok()
816:                 .and_then(|v| lua.from_value::<ToolOutputLines>(v).ok())
817:                 .unwrap_or_default(),
818:             t.get::<LuaValue>("state")
819:                 .ok()
820:                 .and_then(|v| lua_to_json(&v).ok())
821:                 .filter(|v| !v.is_null()),
822:         ),
823:         _ => (ToolOutputLines::default(), None),
824:     };
825:     let ud = lua.create_userdata(LuaCtx::restore(tol, state))?;
826:     Ok(LuaValue::UserData(ud))
827: }
828: 
829: fn is_valid_tool_name(name: &str) -> bool {
830:     if name.is_empty() || name.len() > TOOL_NAME_MAX {
831:         return false;
832:     }
833:     let mut chars = name.chars();
834:     let first = chars.next().unwrap();
835:     if !first.is_ascii_alphabetic() && first != '_' {
836:         return false;
837:     }
838:     chars.all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '_')
839: }
840: 
841: fn parse_audience(audiences: Option<mlua::Table>) -> LuaResult<ToolAudience> {
842:     let Some(arr) = audiences else {
843:         return Ok(ToolAudience::default());
844:     };
845:     let mut flags = ToolAudience::empty();
846:     let mut count = 0;
847:     for item in arr.sequence_values::<String>() {
848:         let s = item?;
849:         count += 1;
850:         flags |= match s.as_str() {
851:             "all" => ToolAudience::all(),
852:             other => ToolAudience::parse_name(other)
853:                 .ok_or_else(|| mlua::Error::runtime(format!("unknown audience: {other}")))?,
854:         };
855:     }
856:     if count == 0 {
857:         return Err(mlua::Error::runtime(
858:             "register_tool: 'audiences' must be omitted or non-empty",
859:         ));
860:     }
861:     Ok(flags)
862: }
863: 
864: fn parse_timeout(spec: &Table) -> LuaResult<Option<Duration>> {
865:     let value: LuaValue = spec.get("timeout").unwrap_or(LuaValue::Nil);
866:     match value {
867:         LuaValue::Nil | LuaValue::Boolean(false) => Ok(None),
868:         LuaValue::Integer(0) => Ok(None),
869:         LuaValue::Integer(n) if n > 0 => Ok(Some(Duration::from_secs(n as u64))),
870:         LuaValue::Number(n) if n > 0.0 && n.is_finite() => Ok(Some(Duration::from_secs(n as u64))),
871:         LuaValue::Number(0.0) => Ok(None),
872:         _ => Err(mlua::Error::runtime(TIMEOUT_PARSE_ERR)),
873:     }
874: }
875: 
876: fn spec_opt<T: mlua::FromLua>(spec: &Table, key: &str, expected: &str) -> LuaResult<Option<T>> {
877:     spec.get::<Option<T>>(key)
878:         .map_err(|_| mlua::Error::runtime(format!("register_tool: '{key}' must be {expected}")))
879: }
880: 
881: fn check_schema_field(schema: &Value, key: &str, field: &str, expected: &str) -> LuaResult<()> {
882:     let matches = schema
883:         .get("properties")
884:         .and_then(|p| p.get(field))
885:         .and_then(|s| s.get("type"))
886:         .and_then(|t| t.as_str())
887:         .is_some_and(|t| t == expected);
888:     if matches {
889:         Ok(())
890:     } else {
891:         Err(mlua::Error::runtime(format!(
892:             "register_tool: {key} field '{field}' not in schema properties or not type '{expected}'"
893:         )))
894:     }
895: }
896: 
897: fn require_schema_field(spec: &Table, key: &str, schema: &Value) -> LuaResult<Option<Arc<str>>> {
898:     let Some(field) = spec_opt::<String>(spec, key, "a string")? else {
899:         return Ok(None);
900:     };
901:     check_schema_field(schema, key, &field, "string")?;
902:     Ok(Some(Arc::from(field.as_str())))
903: }
904: 
905: fn parse_start_annotation(spec: &Table, schema: &Value) -> LuaResult<Option<StartAnnotation>> {
906:     match spec.get::<Option<LuaValue>>("start_annotation")? {
907:         None => Ok(None),
908:         Some(LuaValue::String(s)) => {
909:             let field = s.to_str()?.to_owned();
910:             check_schema_field(schema, "start_annotation", &field, "array")?;
911:             Ok(Some(StartAnnotation::Count(Arc::from(field.as_str()))))
912:         }
913:         Some(LuaValue::Table(t)) => {
914:             let field: String = t.get("field").map_err(|_| {
915:                 mlua::Error::runtime("register_tool: start_annotation.field required")
916:             })?;
917:             if t.get::<Option<String>>("kind")?.as_deref() != Some("timeout") {
918:                 return Err(mlua::Error::runtime(
919:                     "register_tool: start_annotation.kind must be 'timeout'",
920:                 ));
921:             }
922:             check_schema_field(schema, "start_annotation", &field, "integer")?;
923:             Ok(Some(StartAnnotation::Timeout(Arc::from(field.as_str()))))
924:         }
925:         Some(_) => Err(mlua::Error::runtime(
926:             "register_tool: 'start_annotation' must be a string field name or a table",
927:         )),
928:     }
929: }
930: 
931: fn register_tool_from_lua(lua: &Lua, spec: &Table, pending: PendingTools) -> LuaResult<()> {
932:     let name: String = spec
933:         .get("name")
934:         .map_err(|_| mlua::Error::runtime("register_tool: missing 'name'"))?;
935:     if !is_valid_tool_name(&name) {
936:         return Err(mlua::Error::runtime(format!(
937:             "register_tool: invalid name '{name}'"
938:         )));
939:     }
940:     let description: String = spec.get("description").unwrap_or_default();
941:     if description.trim().is_empty() {
942:         return Err(mlua::Error::runtime(
943:             "register_tool: description must be non-empty",
944:         ));
945:     }
946:     let handler: Function = spec
947:         .get("handler")
948:         .map_err(|_| mlua::Error::runtime("register_tool: missing 'handler'"))?;
949:     let schema_table: LuaValue = spec
950:         .get("schema")
951:         .map_err(|_| mlua::Error::runtime("register_tool: missing 'schema'"))?;
952:     let audiences: Option<mlua::Table> = spec.get("audiences").ok();
953: 
954:     let schema_val: Value = lua.from_value(schema_table)?;
955:     let param_schema = try_from_json(&schema_val).map_err(mlua::Error::runtime)?;
956: 
957:     if !spec.get::<LuaValue>("permission_scope")?.is_nil() {
958:         return Err(mlua::Error::runtime(
959:             "register_tool: 'permission_scope' was removed; use permission_scopes = \"<field>\" or permission_scopes = function(input) ... end",
960:         ));
961:     }
962:     let mutable_path_field = require_schema_field(spec, "mutable_path", &schema_val)?;
963: 
964:     let permission_scopes = match spec.get::<LuaValue>("permission_scopes")? {
965:         LuaValue::Nil => None,
966:         LuaValue::String(s) => {
967:             let field = s.to_str()?.to_owned();
968:             check_schema_field(&schema_val, "permission_scopes", &field, "string")?;
969:             Some(PermissionScopeSpec::Field(Arc::from(field.as_str())))
970:         }
971:         LuaValue::Function(f) => Some(PermissionScopeSpec::Callback(lua.create_registry_value(f)?)),
972:         _ => {
973:             return Err(mlua::Error::runtime(
974:                 "register_tool: 'permission_scopes' must be a string field name or a function",
975:             ));
976:         }
977:     };
978: 
979:     let header_fn: Option<Function> = spec.get("header").ok();
980:     let restore_fn: Option<Function> = spec.get("restore").ok();
981:     let start_fn: Option<Function> = spec.get("start").ok();
982:     let kind: Option<Arc<str>> = spec
983:         .get::<String>("kind")
984:         .ok()
985:         .map(|s| Arc::from(s.as_str()));
986:     let audience = parse_audience(audiences)?;
987:     let timeout = parse_timeout(spec)?;
988:     let start_annotation = parse_start_annotation(spec, &schema_val)?;
989:     let handler_key: RegistryKey = lua.create_registry_value(handler)?;
990:     let header_key = header_fn
991:         .map(|f| lua.create_registry_value(f))
992:         .transpose()?;
993:     let restore_key = restore_fn
994:         .map(|f| lua.create_registry_value(f))
995:         .transpose()?;
996:     let start_key = start_fn.map(|f| lua.create_registry_value(f)).transpose()?;
997: 
998:     let describe_fn: Option<Function> = spec.get("describe").ok();
999:     let describe_key = describe_fn
1000:         .map(|f| lua.create_registry_value(f))
1001:         .transpose()?;
1002: 
1003:     let examples: Option<Value> =
1004:         spec_opt::<Table>(spec, "examples", "a table (array of example inputs)")?
1005:             .map(|t| lua.from_value(LuaValue::Table(t)))
1006:             .transpose()
1007:             .map_err(|e| mlua::Error::runtime(format!("register_tool: invalid examples: {e}")))?;
1008: 
1009:     let name: Arc<str> = Arc::from(name.as_str());
1010: 
1011:     pending
1012:         .lock()
1013:         .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
1014:         .push(PendingTool {
1015:             name,
1016:             description,
1017:             schema: param_schema,
1018:             audience,
1019:             kind,
1020:             handler_key,
1021:             header_key,
1022:             restore_key,
1023:             start_key,
1024:             permission_scopes,
1025:             mutable_path_field,
1026:             timeout,
1027:             start_annotation,
1028:             examples,
1029:             describe_key,
1030:         });
1031: 
1032:     Ok(())
1033: }
1034: 
1035: fn register_command_from_lua(lua: &Lua, spec: &Table, plugin: Arc<str>) -> LuaResult<()> {
1036:     let name: String = spec
1037:         .get("name")
1038:         .map_err(|_| mlua::Error::runtime("register_command: missing 'name'"))?;
1039:     if name.is_empty() {
1040:         return Err(mlua::Error::runtime(
1041:             "register_command: name must be non-empty",
1042:         ));
1043:     }
1044:     let description: String = spec.get("description").unwrap_or_default();
1045:     let handler: Function = spec
1046:         .get("handler")
1047:         .map_err(|_| mlua::Error::runtime("register_command: missing 'handler'"))?;
1048: 
1049:     let handler_key = lua.create_registry_value(handler)?;
1050:     let name: Arc<str> = Arc::from(name.as_str());
1051:     let description: Arc<str> = Arc::from(description.as_str());
1052: 
1053:     {
1054:         let mut map = lua
1055:             .app_data_mut::<CommandHandlerMap>()
1056:             .ok_or_else(|| mlua::Error::runtime("register_command: not initialized"))?;
1057:         map.entry(Arc::clone(&plugin)).or_default().insert(
1058:             Arc::clone(&name),
1059:             CommandEntry {
1060:                 handler: handler_key,
1061:                 description,
1062:             },
1063:         );
1064:     }
1065: 
1066:     let map = lua
1067:         .app_data_ref::<CommandHandlerMap>()
1068:         .ok_or_else(|| mlua::Error::runtime("register_command: not initialized"))?;
1069:     let writer = lua
1070:         .app_data_ref::<LuaCommandWriter>()
1071:         .ok_or_else(|| mlua::Error::runtime("register_command: not initialized"))?;
1072:     publish_command_snapshot(&map, &writer);
1073: 
1074:     Ok(())
1075: }

1077: pub(crate) type ToolCallResult = Result<String, String>;
1078: 
1079: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
1080: pub(crate) enum LuaOutputFormat {
1081:     #[default]
1082:     Plain,
1083:     Markdown,
1084: }
1085: 
1086: const LUA_FORMAT_MARKDOWN: &str = "markdown";
1087: const LUA_FORMAT_PLAIN: &str = "plain";
1088: 
1089: pub(crate) struct DiffPayload {
1090:     pub path: String,
1091:     pub before: String,
1092:     pub after: String,
1093: }
1094: 
1095: pub(crate) struct ToolCallReply {
1096:     pub result: ToolCallResult,
1097:     pub snapshot: Option<BufferSnapshot>,
1098:     pub header: Option<BufferSnapshot>,
1099:     pub live_buf: Option<Arc<SharedBuf>>,
1100:     pub format: LuaOutputFormat,
1101:     pub annotation: Option<String>,
1102:     pub instructions: Option<Vec<InstructionBlock>>,
1103:     pub written_path: Option<String>,
1104:     pub diff: Option<DiffPayload>,
1105:     /// Set via `image = { media_type = "image/png", data = <base64> }` in the
1106:     /// handler return; becomes `ToolOutput::Image` with `llm_output` as caption.
1107:     pub image: Option<ImageSource>,
1108:     pub state: Option<Value>,
1109: }
1110: 
1111: impl ToolCallReply {
1112:     pub fn from_lua_value(val: &LuaValue) -> Self {
1113:         let mut result = coerce_tool_result(val);
1114:         let LuaValue::Table(t) = val else {
1115:             return Self::plain(result);
1116:         };
1117:         let (snapshot, live_buf) = Self::extract_body_handle(t);
1118:         let header = t
1119:             .get::<LuaValue>("header")
1120:             .ok()
1121:             .and_then(|v| Self::extract_snapshot(&v));
1122:         let format = extract_format(t);
1123:         let annotation = t.get::<String>("annotation").ok();
1124:         let instructions = extract_instructions(t);
1125:         let written_path = t.get::<String>("written_path").ok();
1126:         let diff = t.get::<String>("diff_path").ok().map(|path| DiffPayload {
1127:             path,
1128:             before: t.get::<String>("diff_before").ok().unwrap_or_default(),
1129:             after: t.get::<String>("diff_after").ok().unwrap_or_default(),
1130:         });
1131:         // A malformed image fails the call; dropping it silently would leave
1132:         // a caption claiming pixels the model never receives.
1133:         let image = match extract_image(t) {
1134:             Ok(image) => image,
1135:             Err(e) => {
1136:                 result = Err(e);
1137:                 None
1138:             }
1139:         };
1140:         let state = match t.get::<LuaValue>("state") {
1141:             Ok(LuaValue::Nil) | Err(_) => None,
1142:             Ok(v) => crate::api::util::convert::lua_to_json(&v)
1143:                 .inspect_err(|e| tracing::warn!(error = %e, "tool state is not JSON-serializable, dropping it"))
1144:                 .ok(),
1145:         };
1146:         Self {
1147:             result,
1148:             snapshot,
1149:             header,
1150:             live_buf,
1151:             format,
1152:             annotation,
1153:             instructions,
1154:             written_path,
1155:             diff,
1156:             image,
1157:             state,
1158:         }
1159:     }
1160: 
1161:     fn extract_body_handle(t: &mlua::Table) -> (Option<BufferSnapshot>, Option<Arc<SharedBuf>>) {
1162:         t.get::<LuaValue>("body")
1163:             .ok()
1164:             .and_then(|v| {
1165:                 let ud = v.as_userdata()?;
1166:                 let h = ud.borrow::<BufHandle>().ok()?;
1167:                 Some((Some(h.buf.take()), Some(Arc::clone(&h.buf))))
1168:             })
1169:             .unwrap_or((None, None))
1170:     }
1171: 
1172:     fn extract_snapshot(val: &LuaValue) -> Option<BufferSnapshot> {
1173:         let ud = val.as_userdata()?;
1174:         let h = ud.borrow::<BufHandle>().ok()?;
1175:         Some(h.buf.take())
1176:     }
1177: 
1178:     pub fn plain(result: ToolCallResult) -> Self {
1179:         Self {
1180:             result,
1181:             snapshot: None,
1182:             header: None,
1183:             live_buf: None,
1184:             format: LuaOutputFormat::default(),
1185:             annotation: None,
1186:             instructions: None,
1187:             written_path: None,
1188:             diff: None,
1189:             image: None,
1190:             state: None,
1191:         }
1192:     }
1193: 
1194:     pub fn err(msg: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
1195:         Self::plain(Err(msg.into()))
1196:     }
1197: }
1198: 
1199: fn extract_format(t: &mlua::Table) -> LuaOutputFormat {
1200:     let Ok(LuaValue::String(s)) = t.get::<LuaValue>("format") else {
1201:         return LuaOutputFormat::default();
1202:     };
1203:     let Ok(s) = s.to_str() else {
1204:         return LuaOutputFormat::default();
1205:     };
1206:     match &*s {
1207:         LUA_FORMAT_MARKDOWN => LuaOutputFormat::Markdown,
1208:         LUA_FORMAT_PLAIN => LuaOutputFormat::Plain,
1209:         _ => LuaOutputFormat::default(),
1210:     }
1211: }
1212: 
1213: fn extract_image(t: &mlua::Table) -> Result<Option<ImageSource>, String> {
1214:     let entry = match t.get::<LuaValue>("image") {
1215:         Ok(LuaValue::Table(entry)) => entry,
1216:         Ok(LuaValue::Nil) | Err(_) => return Ok(None),
1217:         Ok(other) => {
1218:             return Err(format!(
1219:                 "tool 'image' field must be a table {{ media_type, data }}, got {}",
1220:                 other.type_name()
1221:             ));
1222:         }
1223:     };
1224:     let media_type = entry
1225:         .get::<String>("media_type")
1226:         .map_err(|_| "tool image is missing 'media_type'".to_owned())?;
1227:     let media_type = ImageMediaType::from_mime(&media_type).ok_or_else(|| {
1228:         let supported: Vec<&str> = ImageMediaType::ALL.iter().map(|m| m.mime()).collect();
1229:         format!(
1230:             "unsupported tool image media_type '{media_type}' ({})",
1231:             supported.join(", ")
1232:         )
1233:     })?;
1234:     let data = entry
1235:         .get::<String>("data")
1236:         .map_err(|_| "tool image is missing base64 'data'".to_owned())?;
1237:     // Bad base64 would land in history and fail every later request;
1238:     // validate once at the boundary.
1239:     if data.is_empty() {
1240:         return Err("tool image 'data' is empty".to_owned());
1241:     }
1242:     BASE64
1243:         .decode(data.as_bytes())
1244:         .map_err(|e| format!("tool image 'data' is not valid base64: {e}"))?;
1245:     Ok(Some(ImageSource::new(media_type, Arc::from(data))))
1246: }
1247: 
1248: fn extract_instructions(t: &mlua::Table) -> Option<Vec<InstructionBlock>> {
1249:     let Ok(LuaValue::Table(arr)) = t.get::<LuaValue>("instructions") else {
1250:         return None;
1251:     };
1252:     let mut blocks = Vec::new();
1253:     for pair in arr.sequence_values::<LuaValue>() {
1254:         let Ok(LuaValue::Table(entry)) = pair else {
1255:             continue;
1256:         };
1257:         let Ok(path) = entry.get::<String>("path") else {
1258:             continue;
1259:         };
1260:         let Ok(content) = entry.get::<String>("content") else {
1261:             continue;
1262:         };
1263:         blocks.push(InstructionBlock { path, content });
1264:     }
1265:     if blocks.is_empty() {
1266:         None
1267:     } else {
1268:         Some(blocks)
1269:     }
1270: }
1271: 
1272: pub(crate) fn coerce_tool_result(result: &LuaValue) -> ToolCallResult {
1273:     match result {
1274:         LuaValue::String(s) => s.to_str().map(|s| s.to_owned()).map_err(|e| e.to_string()),
1275:         LuaValue::Table(t) => {
1276:             let output = t.get::<LuaValue>("llm_output").ok().and_then(|v| {
1277:                 if let LuaValue::String(s) = v {
1278:                     s.to_str().ok().map(|s| s.to_owned())
1279:                 } else {
1280:                     None
1281:                 }
1282:             });
1283:             match output {
1284:                 Some(s) if matches!(t.get::<LuaValue>("is_error"), Ok(LuaValue::Boolean(true))) => {
1285:                     Err(s)
1286:                 }
1287:                 Some(s) => Ok(s),
1288:                 None => Err(TOOL_HANDLER_RETURN_ERR.to_string()),
1289:             }
1290:         }
1291:         _ => Err(TOOL_HANDLER_RETURN_ERR.to_string()),
1292:     }
1293: }

1345:     fn invocation(input: Value) -> LuaToolInvocation {
1346:         let (tx, _rx) = flume::unbounded();
1347:         LuaToolInvocation {
1348:             tool: Arc::from("test_tool"),

1572:     fn timeout_spec(lua: &Lua, value: LuaValue) -> Table {
1573:         let t = lua.create_table().unwrap();
1574:         if !matches!(value, LuaValue::Nil) {
1575:             t.set("timeout", value).unwrap();
1576:         }
1577:         t
1578:     }
1579: 
1580:     fn timeout_ok(lua: &Lua, value: LuaValue) -> Option<Duration> {
1581:         parse_timeout(&timeout_spec(lua, value)).unwrap()
1582:     }
1583: 
1584:     fn timeout_err(lua: &Lua, value: LuaValue) {
1585:         let err = parse_timeout(&timeout_spec(lua, value)).unwrap_err();
1586:         assert!(err.to_string().contains(TIMEOUT_PARSE_ERR));
1587:     }

1629:     fn reply_table(lua: &Lua, output: &str, format: Option<&str>, is_error: bool) -> LuaValue {

1633:             t.set("is_error", true).unwrap();
1634:         }
1635:         if let Some(f) = format {

1639:     }

48: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
49: pub enum ToolFilter {
50:     #[default]
51:     All,
52:     Only(Vec<String>),
53:     AllExcept(Vec<String>),
54: }
55: 
56: impl ToolFilter {
57:     pub fn matches(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
58:         match self {
59:             Self::All => true,
60:             Self::Only(allowed) => allowed.iter().any(|n| n == name),
61:             Self::AllExcept(blocked) => !blocked.iter().any(|n| n == name),
62:         }
63:     }
64: 
65:     pub fn excluding(self, names: &[&str]) -> Self {
66:         if names.is_empty() {
67:             return self;
68:         }
69:         match self {
70:             Self::All => Self::AllExcept(names.iter().map(|s| (*s).to_owned()).collect()),
71:             Self::Only(allowed) => Self::Only(
72:                 allowed
73:                     .into_iter()
74:                     .filter(|n| !names.iter().any(|x| *x == n))
75:                     .collect(),
76:             ),
77:             Self::AllExcept(mut blocked) => {
78:                 for &n in names {
79:                     if !blocked.iter().any(|b| b == n) {
80:                         blocked.push(n.to_owned());
81:                     }
82:                 }
83:                 Self::AllExcept(blocked)
84:             }
85:         }
86:     }
87: 
88:     pub fn from_config(config: &AgentConfig, model: &Model, extra_exclude: &[&str]) -> Self {
89:         let base = if config.allowed_tools.is_empty() {
90:             Self::All
91:         } else {
92:             Self::Only(
93:                 config
94:                     .allowed_tools
95:                     .iter()
96:                     .filter(|s| is_builtin_tool(s))
97:                     .cloned()
98:                     .collect(),
99:             )
100:         };
101:         let mut exclude: Vec<&str> = extra_exclude.to_vec();
102:         exclude.extend(capability_exclusions(model));
103:         exclude.extend(config.disabled_tools.iter().map(|s| s.as_str()));
104:         base.excluding(&exclude)
105:     }
106: }
107: 
108: /// One gate for every definitions builder (main loop, headless, Lua): a model
109: /// without vision never learns `view_image` exists.
110: pub fn capability_exclusions(model: &Model) -> &'static [&'static str] {
111:     if model.vision {
112:         &[]
113:     } else {
114:         &[VIEW_IMAGE_TOOL_NAME]
115:     }
116: }

120: pub fn is_tool_enabled(disabled_tools: &[String], name: &str) -> bool {
121:     !disabled_tools.iter().any(|s| s == name)
122: }

140: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default)]
141: pub enum Deadline {
142:     #[default]
143:     None,
144:     At(Instant),
145: }
146: 
147: impl Deadline {
148:     pub fn after(duration: Duration) -> Self {
149:         Self::At(Instant::now() + duration)
150:     }
151: 
152:     pub fn check(self) -> Result<(), String> {
153:         match self {
154:             Self::None => Ok(()),
155:             Self::At(instant) if instant.saturating_duration_since(Instant::now()).is_zero() => {
156:                 Err(DEADLINE_EXCEEDED.into())
157:             }
158:             Self::At(_) => Ok(()),
159:         }
160:     }
161: 
162:     pub fn cap_timeout(self, timeout_secs: u64) -> Result<u64, String> {
163:         match self {
164:             Self::None => Ok(timeout_secs),
165:             Self::At(instant) => {
166:                 let remaining = instant.saturating_duration_since(Instant::now());
167:                 if remaining.is_zero() {
168:                     Err(DEADLINE_EXCEEDED.into())
169:                 } else {
170:                     Ok(timeout_secs.min(remaining.as_secs().max(1)))
171:                 }
172:             }
173:         }
174:     }
175: }
176: 
177: pub fn timeout_annotation(secs: u64) -> String {
178:     let d = Duration::from_secs(secs);
179:     let formatted: String = format_duration(d)
180:         .to_string()
181:         .chars()
182:         .filter(|c| !c.is_whitespace())
183:         .collect();
184:     format!("{formatted} timeout")
185: }

227: pub(crate) fn resolve_path(path: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
228:     let expanded = if let Some(rest) = path.strip_prefix("~/") {
229:         let home = HOME.as_deref().ok_or("cannot expand ~: HOME not set")?;
230:         home.join(rest).to_string_lossy().into_owned()
231:     } else if path == "~" {
232:         let home = HOME.as_deref().ok_or("cannot expand ~: HOME not set")?;
233:         home.to_string_lossy().into_owned()
234:     } else {
235:         path.to_string()
236:     };
237: 
238:     if Path::new(&expanded).is_relative() {
239:         let cwd = env::current_dir().map_err(|e| format!("cwd error: {e}"))?;
240:         Ok(cwd.join(&expanded).to_string_lossy().into_owned())
241:     } else {
242:         Ok(expanded)
243:     }
244: }
245: 
246: pub fn resolve_search_path(path: Option<&str>) -> Result<String, String> {
247:     match path {
248:         Some(p) => resolve_path(p),
249:         None => env::current_dir()
250:             .map(|p| p.to_string_lossy().into_owned())
251:             .map_err(|e| format!("cwd error: {e}")),
252:     }
253: }
254: 
255: static CWD: LazyLock<Option<PathBuf>> = LazyLock::new(|| env::current_dir().ok());
256: static HOME: LazyLock<Option<PathBuf>> = LazyLock::new(maki_storage::paths::home);
257: 
258: pub(crate) fn relative_path(path: &str) -> String {
259:     let p = Path::new(path);
260:     if let Some(cwd) = CWD.as_deref()
261:         && let Ok(rel) = p.strip_prefix(cwd)
262:     {
263:         return format_rel("", ".", rel);
264:     }
265:     if let Some(home) = HOME.as_deref()
266:         && let Ok(rel) = p.strip_prefix(home)
267:     {
268:         return format_rel("~/", "~", rel);
269:     }
270:     path.to_string()
271: }
272: 
273: fn format_rel(prefix: &str, fallback: &str, rel: &Path) -> String {
274:     let s = rel.to_string_lossy();
275:     if s.is_empty() {
276:         fallback.into()
277:     } else {
278:         format!("{prefix}{s}")
279:     }
280: }
281: 
282: /// Convenience wrapper that always respects gitignore.
283: pub fn walk_builder(root: &str, patterns: &[&str]) -> Result<WalkBuilder, String> {
284:     walk_builder_opts(root, patterns, true)
285: }
286: 
287: /// `.git` is always excluded, even when `gitignore` is false.
288: pub fn walk_builder_opts(
289:     root: &str,
290:     patterns: &[&str],
291:     gitignore: bool,
292: ) -> Result<WalkBuilder, String> {
293:     let mut ob = ignore::overrides::OverrideBuilder::new(root);
294:     ob.add("!.git").expect("!.git is a valid glob");
295: 
296:     for p in patterns {
297:         ob.add(p)
298:             .map_err(|e| format!("invalid glob pattern: {e}"))?;
299:     }
300: 
301:     let overrides = ob
302:         .build()
303:         .map_err(|e| format!("invalid glob pattern: {e}"))?;
304: 
305:     let mut wb = WalkBuilder::new(root);
306:     wb.hidden(false).overrides(overrides);
307:     if !gitignore {
308:         wb.ignore(false)
309:             .git_ignore(false)
310:             .git_global(false)
311:             .git_exclude(false);
312:     }
313:     Ok(wb)
314: }

316: pub fn mtime(path: &Path) -> SystemTime {
317:     fs::metadata(path)
318:         .and_then(|m| m.modified())
319:         .unwrap_or(SystemTime::UNIX_EPOCH)
320: }

322: pub(crate) fn truncate_bytes(line: &str, max_bytes: usize) -> String {
323:     if line.len() > max_bytes {
324:         let boundary = line.floor_char_boundary(max_bytes);
325:         format!("{}...", &line[..boundary])
326:     } else {
327:         line.to_owned()
328:     }
329: }
330: 
331: pub fn truncate_output(text: String, max_lines: usize, max_bytes: usize) -> String {
332:     const TRUNCATED_MARKER: &str = "[truncated]";
333:     let mut lines = text.lines();
334:     let mut result = String::new();
335:     let mut truncated = false;
336: 
337:     for _ in 0..max_lines {
338:         let Some(line) = lines.next() else { break };
339:         if !result.is_empty() {
340:             result.push('\n');
341:         }
342:         result.push_str(line);
343:         if result.len() > max_bytes {
344:             let boundary = result.floor_char_boundary(max_bytes);
345:             result.truncate(boundary);
346:             truncated = true;
347:             break;
348:         }
349:     }
350: 
351:     if !truncated && lines.next().is_some() {
352:         truncated = true;
353:     }
354: 
355:     if truncated {
356:         result.push('\n');
357:         result.push_str(TRUNCATED_MARKER);
358:     }
359:     result
360: }

603:     fn cap_timeout_ok(deadline: Deadline, requested: u64, expected: u64) {

618:         assert_eq!(expired.cap_timeout(120).unwrap_err(), DEADLINE_EXCEEDED);

85: fn model_to_lua_table(lua: &Lua, model: &Model) -> LuaResult<Table> {

87:     tbl.set("id", model.id.clone())?;

94: fn dispatch_ctx<'a>(ctx: &'a LuaCtx, method: &str) -> Result<&'a AgentContext, String> {
95:     ctx.agent()
96:         .ok_or_else(|| ctx.cap_err(&format!("maki.agent.{method}")))
97: }

99: type Pair<T> = (Option<T>, Option<String>);
100: 
101: fn err_pair<T>(err: impl ToString) -> Pair<T> {
102:     (None, Some(err.to_string()))
103: }
104: 
105: /// `maki.agent.*` convention: wrong argument types throw; every value or
106: /// runtime failure (including a ctx without dispatch capability) returns
107: /// `(nil, err)`.
108: macro_rules! try_pair {
109:     ($e:expr) => {
110:         match $e {
111:             Ok(v) => v,
112:             Err(e) => return Ok(err_pair(e)),
113:         }
114:     };
115: }
116: 
117: async fn resolve_model(
118:     lua: Lua,
119:     (ctx, opts): (mlua::UserDataRef<LuaCtx>, Option<Table>),
120: ) -> LuaResult<Pair<Table>> {
121:     let agent = try_pair!(dispatch_ctx(&ctx, "resolve_model"));
122:     let tier_str = opts
123:         .as_ref()
124:         .and_then(|t| t.get::<Option<String>>("tier").ok().flatten());
125:     let spec_str = opts
126:         .as_ref()
127:         .and_then(|t| t.get::<Option<String>>("spec").ok().flatten());
128: 
129:     let model = match spec_str {
130:         Some(ref spec) => try_pair!(Model::from_spec(spec)),
131:         None => try_pair!(resolve_model_from_ctx(agent, tier_str.as_deref())),
132:     };
133:     Ok((Some(model_to_lua_table(&lua, &model)?), None))
134: }

137:     _lua: Lua,
138:     (ctx, opts): (mlua::UserDataRef<LuaCtx>, Table),
139: ) -> LuaResult<Pair<String>> {
140:     let agent = try_pair!(dispatch_ctx(&ctx, "system_prompt"));
141:     let prompt_id_str: String = opts.get("prompt_id")?;
142:     let prompt_id = match prompt_id_str.as_str() {
143:         "research" => maki_agent::prompt::PromptId::Research,
144:         "general" => maki_agent::prompt::PromptId::General,
145:         "system" => maki_agent::prompt::PromptId::System,
146:         other => return Ok(err_pair(format!("unknown prompt_id: {other}"))),
147:     };
148:

151:     let instructions = match instructions_val {

249: /// Lock-free reads via `ArcSwap`, writes swap in a new snapshot atomically.
250: pub struct ToolRegistry {

252: }
253: 
254: impl Default for ToolRegistry {
255:     fn default() -> Self {
256:         Self::new()
257:     }
258: }
259: 
260: #[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
261: pub enum RegistryError {
262:     #[error("tool '{name}' is already registered (existing source: {existing})")]
263:     NameConflict { name: String, existing: String },
264: }
265: 
266: impl ToolRegistry {
267:     pub fn new() -> Self {
268:         Self {
269:             tools: ArcSwap::from_pointee(Vec::new()),
270:         }
271:     }
272: 
273:     /// The process-wide registry. Every tool in it comes from a Lua plugin
274:     /// or an MCP server; Rust itself registers nothing.
275:     pub fn global() -> &'static Self {
276:         Self::global_arc()
277:     }
278: 
279:     pub fn global_arc() -> &'static Arc<Self> {
280:         static GLOBAL: LazyLock<Arc<ToolRegistry>> =
281:             LazyLock::new(|| Arc::new(ToolRegistry::new()));
282:         &GLOBAL
283:     }
284: 
285:     pub fn get(&self, name: &str) -> Option<RegisteredTool> {
286:         self.tools.load().iter().find(|t| t.name() == name).cloned()
287:     }
288: 
289:     pub fn has(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
290:         self.tools.load().iter().any(|t| t.name() == name)
291:     }
292: 
293:     pub fn register(&self, tool: Arc<dyn Tool>, source: ToolSource) -> Result<(), RegistryError> {
294:         let name = tool.name().to_owned();
295:         let mut conflict = None;
296:         self.tools.rcu(|current| {
297:             conflict = None;
298:             if let Some(existing) = current.iter().find(|t| t.name() == name) {
299:                 conflict = Some(existing.source.as_log_field().into_owned());
300:                 return Vec::clone(current);
301:             }
302:             let mut next = Vec::with_capacity(current.len() + 1);
303:             next.extend(current.iter().cloned());
304:             next.push(RegisteredTool {
305:                 tool: Arc::clone(&tool),
306:                 source: source.clone(),
307:             });
308:             next
309:         });
310:         if let Some(existing) = conflict {
311:             return Err(RegistryError::NameConflict { name, existing });
312:         }
313:         Ok(())
314:     }
315: 
316:     /// All-or-nothing: a name clash rolls back the whole batch so an MCP server
317:     /// never ends up half-registered.
318:     pub fn register_many(
319:         &self,
320:         entries: impl IntoIterator<Item = (Arc<dyn Tool>, ToolSource)>,
321:     ) -> Result<(), RegistryError> {
322:         let entries: Vec<_> = entries.into_iter().collect();
323:         let mut conflict = None;
324:         self.tools.rcu(|current| {
325:             conflict = None;
326:             let mut next = Vec::clone(current);
327:             for (tool, source) in &entries {
328:                 let name = tool.name();
329:                 if let Some(existing) = next.iter().find(|t| t.name() == name) {
330:                     conflict = Some(RegistryError::NameConflict {
331:                         name: name.to_owned(),
332:                         existing: existing.source.as_log_field().into_owned(),
333:                     });
334:                     return Vec::clone(current);
335:                 }
336:                 next.push(RegisteredTool {
337:                     tool: Arc::clone(tool),
338:                     source: source.clone(),
339:                 });
340:             }
341:             next
342:         });
343:         if let Some(e) = conflict {
344:             return Err(e);
345:         }
346:         Ok(())
347:     }
348: 
349:     pub fn clear_mcp_server(&self, server: &str) {
350:         self.tools.rcu(|current| {
351:             current
352:                 .iter()
353:                 .filter(
354:                     |t| !matches!(&t.source, ToolSource::Mcp { server: s } if s.as_ref() == server),
355:                 )

427:     /// Rebuilt each request so tools registered mid-session (MCP handshake) show
428:     /// up on the very next turn.
429:     pub fn definitions(
430:         &self,
431:         vars: &Vars,
432:         ctx: &DescriptionContext,
433:         supports_examples: bool,
434:     ) -> Value {
435:         let snapshot = self.tools.load();
436:         let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(snapshot.len());
437:         for entry in snapshot.iter() {
438:             if !entry.tool.audience().contains(ctx.audience) {
439:                 continue;
440:             }
441:             if !ctx.filter.matches(entry.name()) {
442:                 continue;
443:             }
444:             let description = vars.apply(&entry.tool.description(ctx)).into_owned();
445:             let mut def = json!({
446:                 "name": entry.name(),
447:                 "description": description,
448:                 "input_schema": entry.tool.schema(),
449:             });
450:             if let Some(examples) = entry.tool.examples() {
451:                 if supports_examples {
452:                     def["input_examples"] = examples;
453:                 } else if let Some(text) = format_examples_as_text(&examples) {
454:                     let merged =
455:                         format!("{}\n\n{}", def["description"].as_str().unwrap_or(""), text);
456:                     def["description"] = Value::String(merged);
457:                 }
458:             }
459:             out.push(def);
460:         }
461:         Value::Array(out)
462:     }

464:     pub fn iter(&self) -> RegistrySnapshot {
465:         RegistrySnapshot(self.tools.load_full())
466:     }
467: }

469: pub struct RegistrySnapshot(Arc<Vec<RegisteredTool>>);

471: impl RegistrySnapshot {
472:     pub fn iter(&self) -> std::slice::Iter<'_, RegisteredTool> {
473:         self.0.iter()
474:     }
475: 
476:     pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
477:         self.0.len()
478:     }
479: 
480:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
481:         self.0.is_empty()
482:     }
483: }
484: 
485: fn format_examples_as_text(examples: &Value) -> Option<String> {
486:     let arr = examples.as_array()?;
487:     if arr.is_empty() {
488:         return None;
489:     }
490:     let mut text = String::from("Examples:");
491:     for ex in arr {
492:         if let Some(code) = ex.get("code").and_then(|c| c.as_str()) {
493:             text.push_str("\n```\n");
494:             text.push_str(code);
495:             text.push_str("\n```");
496:         }
497:     }
498:     Some(text)
499: }

### Assistant

Here's the full architecture analysis of the Lua plugin migration between v0.3.23 and v0.3.26.

---

## 1. `code_execution`: Rust native → Lua plugin

### Old Rust native (`maki-agent/src/tools/code_execution.rs`, 376 lines, v0.3.23)

The tool was a `#[derive(Tool)]` struct `CodeExecution` with a `#[param]`-annotated schema. It used the `maki-tool-macro` proc macro for schema generation. The `execute()` method:

- Built a `HashMap<String, ToolFn>` by iterating `ToolRegistry::native()` — a separate list of Rust-native tools — and filtering for `ToolAudience::INTERPRETER` (line ~180 in the old file).
- Spawned `smol::unblock` to run the monty sandbox on a blocking thread.
- Piped stdout through `AgentEvent::ToolOutput` events every `STREAM_FLUSH_INTERVAL` (100ms).
- Used `crate::agent::tool_dispatch::run()` to dispatch inner tool calls from Python, with a `TaskSet` for concurrent `asyncio.gather` support.
- Cancellation raced `CancelToken` against the blocking thread.
- All tool discovery, input parsing, permission checking, and output truncation was in Rust.

### New Lua plugin (`plugins/code_execution/init.lua`, 263 lines)

The Lua plugin calls `maki.api.register_tool(...)` with a plain Lua table:

```lua
maki.api.register_tool({
  name = "code_execution",
  description = description,
  describe = describe,
  schema = schema,           -- plain Lua table, not a proc macro
  examples = examples,
  start = start,
  handler = handler,
  header = header,
  restore = restore,
  ...
})
```

**Key architectural difference**: The Python sandbox runner (`maki-interpreter`) is still Rust, but the orchestration layer moved to Lua:

| Concern | Old (Rust) | New (Lua) |
|---|---|---|
| Tool definition | `#[derive(Tool)]` + `Serde` | `maki.api.register_tool({...})` |
| Tool discovery | `ToolRegistry::native()` | `maki.api.get_tools()` |
| Audience filtering | `ToolAudience::INTERPRETER` bitflag | `aud.interpreter` field on each tool entry |
| Tool description for model | `build_interpreter_tools_description()` | `describe(dctx)` Lua callback, dynamic per-audience/filter |
| Python tool call dispatch | `tool_dispatch::run()` with `ToolRegistry::native()` | `maki.agent.call_tool(ctx, name, input, opts)` |
| Output truncation | `truncate_output()` in Rust | `maki.truncate` Lua module |
| Script rendering | N/A (no UI) | `maki.ui.buf()`, `maki.ui.highlight()` for syntax-highlighted line-numbered preview |
| Lifecycle callbacks | `start_header()`, `start_input()`, `execute()` | `start`, `handler`, `header`, `restore` named functions |

The Lua plugin uses `maki.interpreter.run(code, opts)` to invoke the sandbox — a new Lua API that bridges to the Rust monty runner.

---

## 2. `maki-lua/src/api/interpreter.rs` — NEW (179 lines)

This exposes `maki.interpreter.run(code, opts)` to Lua. It creates a `BridgeMsg` channel to communicate between the blocking monty thread and the async Lua thread:

```rust
pub(crate) fn create_interpreter_table(lua: &Lua, perms: &PluginPermissions) -> LuaResult<Table> {
    t.set("run", perms.guard_async(Permission::Run, lua, interpreter_run)?)?;
}
```

**What it does**:
- Accepts `code`, `timeout`, `max_memory_mb`, `on_output` callback, and `tools` table (name → Lua function map).
- Spawns `smol::unblock` for the monty runner on a blocking thread.
- Uses a `flume::unbounded` channel with two message types: `BridgeMsg::Line(String)` for stdout and `BridgeMsg::Calls(Vec<PendingCall>, Sender<CallResults>)` for batched tool calls.
- The **recv_loop** runs on the Lua thread: lines go to `on_output`, batches are dispatched via `call_lua_tool()` which calls the Lua function, collects results, and sends them back.
- Cancellation via `CancelToken` from the task's `TaskCell`.
- Returns `(result_table, error_string)` — the Lua convention of `(nil, err)` on failure.

**Critical design**: The one-channel FIFO preserves ordering of stdout and tool-call results, and dropping the channel (cancellation) makes the blocked thread unwind cleanly.

---

## 3. `maki-agent/src/tools/interpreter_bridge.rs` — NEW (72 lines)

This is the *shared Rust helper* that both the old code_execution and the new Lua API use. It lives in `maki-agent` because it needs access to `tool_dispatch::run`:

```rust
pub async fn dispatch(ctx: &ToolContext, name: &str, input: &Value) -> Result<String, String> {
    let done = tool_dispatch::run(&ctx.registry, ctx.mcp.as_ref(), ...).await;
    flatten(&done)
}
```

**Key functions**:
- `dispatch()` — calls `tool_dispatch::run` and flattens the result.
- `flatten()` — the *single* place where `ToolDoneEvent` becomes text (shared by interpreter and `maki.agent.call_tool`). Handles image output (drops pixels, appends the note).
- `build_tool_input()` — converts positional args + kwargs to a JSON object (moved from the old code_execution, same logic, more tests).

The `maki.agent.call_tool` Lua API (in `maki-lua/src/api/agent.rs`) calls this same `flatten()` function, ensuring the two paths never diverge.

---

## 4. `plugins/edit/init.lua` and `edit_helpers.lua` — the new `edit_lines` tool

**`edit_lines`** (registered at line 258 of `init.lua`) lets the model edit by line number:

```lua
maki.api.register_tool({
  name = "edit_lines",
  schema = {
    properties = {
      path = { type = "string", required = true },
      start = { type = "integer", description = "First line (1-indexed)", required = true },
      ["end"] = { type = "integer", description = "Last line, inclusive. Omit to insert." },
      new_string = { type = "string", required = true },
    },
  },
  handler = function(input, ctx)
    return replace_lines(content, input.start, end_line, input.new_string)
  end,
})
```

**`edit_helpers.lua`** implements `replace_lines()`:
- `end = nil` → insert before `start` line (no deletion).
- `end` set → replace lines `start..end` inclusive with `new_string`, or delete the range if `new_string` is empty.
- Preserves trailing newline.

All three edit tools (`edit`, `multiedit`, `edit_lines`) share `apply_edit()` which does: abspath → permission check → read → transform → write → `ctx:record_read()`. The `diff_result()` function returns `llm_output`, `diff_path`, `diff_before`, `diff_after`, `written_path` — all fields that the Lua runtime (`tool.rs`) maps into `ToolOutput::Diff`.

---

## 5. Core Lua API changes for plugin-hosted tools

### `runtime.rs` — the plugin host loop

The **`LuaRuntime::load_source()`** method (line 1026) is the core of the change:

1. Clears stale pending tools and plugin keys.
2. Creates a fresh `maki` global table via `create_maki_global()` — this includes `maki.api`, `maki.interpreter`, `maki.agent`, etc.
3. Executes the plugin source inside a sandboxed Lua environment.
4. After execution, **drains** the `PendingTools` list (accumulated by `maki.api.register_tool()` calls).
5. Converts each `PendingTool` into an `Arc<dyn Tool>` via `LuaTool` struct.
6. Calls `self.registry.replace_plugin(&name, registry_entries)` — atomically swaps the plugin's tools in the global `ToolRegistry` via `ArcSwap`.

The `LuaRuntime` also stores `ToolKeys` (registry keys for handler, header, restore, start, describe, permission_scopes callbacks) in a `PluginMap` for later dispatch.

### `api/tool.rs` — the `LuaTool` adapter

`LuaTool` implements the `Tool` trait (line 154). Its `parse()` method creates a `LuaToolInvocation` which:

- `start_header()` → sends `Request::ComputeHeader` to the Lua thread.
- `start()` → sends `Request::StartTool` for live preview.
- `permission_scopes()` → either extracts from a field, or sends `Request::ComputePermissionScopes` to a Lua callback.
- `execute()` → sends `Request::CallTool` with input, deadline, live context, and awaits the `ToolCallReply` on a flume channel with timeout.

The `ToolCallReply::from_lua_value()` (line 1112) parses the Lua handler's return value — supporting `string`, or `{ llm_output, is_error, body, header, format, diff_path, diff_before, diff_after, image, instructions, state, annotation, written_path }`.

### `api/agent.rs` — `maki.agent.call_tool`

The `call_tool()` function (line 223) is the bridge for Lua plugins calling other tools:
- Converts Lua input to JSON.
- Clones the `ToolContext` via `agent.to_tool_context()`.
- Supports `timeout`, `on_live_buf`, `on_annotation` options.
- Calls `dispatch_racing_live()` which runs `tool_dispatch::run()` alongside consuming live events from a channel.
- Uses `interpreter_bridge::flatten()` to convert the result to text.

This is what `code_execution`'s Lua plugin uses: `maki.agent.call_tool(ctx, name, tool_input, { timeout = timeout })`.

### `api/mod.rs` — `create_maki_global()`

This function assembles the `maki` table from all API modules. The key addition is:

```rust
maki.set("interpreter", interpreter::create_interpreter_table(lua, permissions)?)?;
agent::register(lua, &maki)?;
```

### `ToolRegistry` changes

The registry (`maki-agent/src/tools/registry.rs`) lost its `native()` method entirely. The comment at line 273 says it all:

```rust
/// The process-wide registry. Every tool in it comes from a Lua plugin
/// or an MCP server; Rust itself registers nothing.
```

The `ToolSource` enum has only `Lua` and `Mcp` variants — no `Native`. The `replace_plugin()` method (line 361) atomically swaps all tools for a plugin via `ArcSwap`, enabling hot-reload.

---

## Summary: Architecture shift

```
v0.3.23 (Rust-native tools)                    v0.3.26 (Lua-hosted tools)
┌──────────────────────────────┐               ┌──────────────────────────────────┐
│ ToolRegistry::native()       │               │ ToolRegistry (global, ArcSwap)    │
│   + Rust #[derive(Tool)]     │               │   ├─ ToolSource::Lua { plugin }   │
│   + Lua plugins (few)        │               │   └─ ToolSource::Mcp { server }   │
│   + MCP servers              │               │                                  │
│                             │               │  LuaRuntime::load_source()        │
│ code_execution:              │               │    → exec plugin source           │
│   Rust struct + proc macro   │               │    → drain PendingTools           │
│   build_tool_fns() in Rust   │               │    → replace_plugin()             │
│   tool_dispatch::run()       │               │                                  │
│   smol::unblock + monty      │               │  code_execution (Lua plugin):     │
│                             │               │    maki.api.register_tool(...)     │
│                             │               │    maki.interpreter.run(...)       │
│                             │               │    maki.agent.call_tool(...)       │
│                             │               │    maki.ui.buf() / highlight()    │
└──────────────────────────────┘               └──────────────────────────────────┘
```

**What moved**:
- Tool definition → `maki.api.register_tool()` Lua call
- Schema → plain Lua table (no proc macro)
- Tool description → `describe(dctx)` Lua callback
- Python sandbox invocation → `maki.interpreter.run()` Lua API
- Tool dispatch from Python → `maki.agent.call_tool()` Lua API
- UI rendering → `maki.ui.buf()` + `ToolView` Lua module
- Output truncation → `maki.truncate` Lua module
- Permission & config → `LuaCtx` userdata methods

**What stayed in Rust**:
- `maki-interpreter` (monty sandbox runner) — the actual Python execution
- `maki-lua/src/api/interpreter.rs` — the Lua↔monty bridge with the FIFO channel
- `maki-agent/src/tools/interpreter_bridge.rs` — shared `dispatch()`/`flatten()`/`build_tool_input()`
- `ToolRegistry` with `ArcSwap` — lock-free concurrent tool storage
- `LuaTool` / `LuaToolInvocation` — the `Tool` + `ToolInvocation` trait impls that dispatch to Lua
- `tool_dispatch::run()` — the core dispatch loop (still dispatches all tools, now including Lua-hosted ones)
